COMCOR 19.00.01 Stormwater Management
19.00.01.01 Authority and Purpose
      A.   In accordance with the authority conferred under Chapter 19, Section
19-3 1, of the Montgomery County Code, 1994, as amended (hereinafter referred
to as the "Code"), the County Executive hereby promulgates this regulation for
the purpose of implementing the County's stormwater management program as set
forth in Chapter 19 of the Code.
      B.   This regulation pertains to all applications for approval of
preliminary plans, stormwater management plans and sediment control permits,
the issuance of building permits for new construction, financial security
requirements, easements, agreements and maintenance requirements for on-site
stormwater management controls, best management practices design criteria, and
waivers.
19.00.01.02 Definitions
      The definitions of terms used in this regulation are provided in Chapter
19, Section 19-21, of the Code. For purposes of this regulation, the following
additional words and phrases will have the meanings respectively ascribed to
them by this regulation:
      Hotspot: An area where land use or activities generate highly
contaminated runoff with concentrations of pollutants in excess of those
typically found in stormwater.
      Soil Survey: The Soil Survey of Montgomery County, Maryland, Natural
Resources Conservation Service, U.S. Department of Agriculture, July 1995.
      Stormwater management concept plan: A statement or drawing, or both,
describing the manner in which stormwater runoff from the proposed development
will be controlled to minimize damage to neighboring properties and receiving
streams and to also prevent the discharge of pollutants into surface waters.
19.00.01.03 General Administration; Stages of Plan Approval
      A.   Stormwater management concept stage.
         1.   Plan required. Before the Montgomery County Planning Board
approves a preliminary plan of subdivision, the Department of Permitting
Services must review and approve a stormwater management concept plan submitted
by the applicant. If a preliminary plan of subdivision or site plan is not
required, then the Department must approve the stormwater management concept
plan before the applicant may apply for a sediment control permit.
         2.   Contents. The concept plan must include the following
information:
            a)   A description of how stormwater runoff from the development
will be controlled to preserve or improve water quality, prevent on-site and
off-site stream channel erosion, and maintain groundwater levels;
            b)   An analysis of existing water quality conditions, including
locating streams, impoundments, and wetlands on the site;
            c)   The results of geotechnical investigations, such as soil
borings and perc tests when structural recharge is proposed; and
            d)   An indication of the method of access to the facilities from
public rights of way for the purpose of maintenance.
         3.   Notice to other property owners. The applicant must provide
written notification of the pending preliminary plan application to the owners
of any properties that adjoin the site of the proposed development or that are
within 500 feet downstream of the proposed development within 10 days after
having submitted the application. The notice must be sent by registered mail
and must include a copy of the stormwater management concept plan, the
preliminary plan reference number, and a statement informing the property
owners that they must submit in writing any comments concerning the preliminary
plan to the Department within 21 days after receiving the notice. The applicant
must certify to the Department that the applicant has provided the required
notice to property owners by submitting a copy of the notice and a list of the
persons notified to the Department within 20 days after submitting the
preliminary plan application.
         4.   Hydrology. This Section presumes that pre-development conditions
are woodland or meadow in good hydrologic condition for the planning and
placement of stormwater management structures.
      B.   Sediment control permit stage.
         1.   Any person required under Chapter 19 of the Code to obtain a
sediment control permit must include a stormwater management design plan as
part of the application for that permit. The design plan must conform to the
approved stormwater management concept plan. The application must include:
            a)   construction drawings for all stormwater management facilities
in accordance with criteria established in Chapter 19 of the Code;
            b)   construction specifications;
            C)   structural computations and certifications signed by an
engineer registered in the state of Maryland;
            d)   supporting hydrologic, hydraulic, and design computations;
            e)   soil analysis;
            f)   drainage area and watershed data;
            g)   a landscape plan, prepared by a landscape architect registered
in the state of Maryland, for all surface structures, that addresses aesthetic,
habitat, and water quality needs, and is in conformance with Department
standards;
            h)   for ponds, if any, standard certifications and signature
blocks must be on design drawings before submittal for signature to the
Montgomery Soil Conservation District; and
            i)   all other necessary information needed for review and approval
by the Department.
         2.   If the proposed stormwater management facility is on land that is
either owned by or proposed for dedication to the Maryland-National Capital
Park and Planning Commission, the stormwater management design plan must be
approved by the Board before the Department may approve the plan and issue a
building permit for the proposed development. An applicant that proposes
dedicating land to the Commission must enter into an agreement to dedicate land
with the Board and provide a certified copy of that agreement to the Department
along with the Board's written approval of the design plan.
         3.   If constructing a stormwater management facility on the proposed
development site is likely to affect existing or proposed water and sewer
lines, the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission's approval of the stormwater
management concept plan is required before the Department may approve the plan
and issue a building permit for the proposed development.
      C.   Qualifications for Both Concept and Design Plans
         1.   Stormwater management concept and design plans must be prepared
by a professional engineer, professional land surveyor, or landscape architect
licensed in Maryland. If a stormwater best management practice requires either
a dam safety permit from the Maryland Department of the Environment or a small
pond approval from the District, the design plan must be prepared by a
professional engineer licensed in the State of Maryland.
         2.   Best management practices. The applicant must document adherence
to minimum stormwater control requirements at the stormwater management concept
plan approval stage and at the sediment control permit approval stage. Before
an application for a sediment control permit is approved, the applicant must
enter into an easement and maintenance agreement with the County, approved as
to form and substance by the Director, to ensure continued compliance with
structural and nonstructural best management practices; however, the Director
may waive this requirement as it relates to nonstructural best management
practices for single family lots or properties when the Director is satisfied
and reasonably certain that the nonstructural best management practices will
remain functional after construction of the development is complete.
      D.   Installation Inspections
         1.   The applicant must notify the Department at least 48 hours before
beginning any construction activity in conjunction with a stormwater management
plan and hold a pre-construction conference with a designated representative of
the Department.
         2.   The Department or a professional engineer licensed by the State
of Maryland must perform installation inspections of any stormwater management
facility under construction as needed to ensure that the facility complies with
approved plans. The inspector must perform the inspections in accordance with
Department-approved checklists for each type of stormwater management facility.
The person performing the inspection must prepare a written inspection report
for the Department to maintain that includes the following information:
            a)   The date and location of the inspection;
            b)   Whether construction was in compliance with the approved
stormwater management plan;
            C)   Any variations from the approved construction specifications;
and
            d)   Any existing violations of applicable County law.
         3.   The Department must notify the applicant in writing if the person
conducting the inspection observes any violations of applicable County law
during the inspection. The written notification must describe the nature of the
violation and prescribe the corrective action needed.
         4.   No construction work on a stormwater management facility may
proceed until the Department inspects and approves the work previously
completed and furnishes the results of the inspection reports to the applicant
after completing each required inspection.
         5.   If the applicant and the Department have entered into a financial
security agreement that specifies the various stages of work to be completed on
the facility, the applicant must contact the Department after completing each
stage to request an inspection. After the Director certifies that the applicant
has completed that stage of work in accordance with the approved plan, the
Director may reduce the required financial security by a prorated amount or may
direct the Director of Finance to refund to the applicant a prorated share of
the amount of financial security that the applicant deposited with the County.
         6.   Once construction is complete, the applicant must submit an as-
built plan and certification to the Department to ensure that the stormwater
management facility has been constructed in conformance with approved plans and
specifications. The plan and certification must be prepared by a professional
engineer, professional land surveyor, or landscape architect that is licensed
or registered in the State of Maryland or by any other person whose
qualifications to prepare as-built plans and certifications are acceptable to
the Department. A Maryland-licensed professional engineer must prepare the
plans and certifications for ponds.
19.00.01.04 Stormwater Management Measures
      A.   Structural Stormwater Management Measures
         1.   An applicant must design and construct the following structural
best management practices in accordance with the Design Manual as well as local
standards instituted by the Department to satisfy the applicable minimum
control requirements established under County law:
            a)   Stormwater management ponds;
            b)   Stormwater management wetlands;
            C)   Stormwater management infiltration;
            d)   Stormwater management filtering systems; and
            e)   Stormwater management open channel systems.
         2.   The applicant must consider performance criteria specified in the
Design Manual in relation to general feasibility, conveyance, pretreatment,
treatment and geometry, environment and landscaping, and maintenance when
selecting structural management practices.
         3.   The applicant must select structural stormwater management
practices to accommodate the unique hydrologic or geologic regions of the
County.
      B.   Nonstructural Stormwater Management Measures
         1.   An applicant must apply the following nonstructural best
management practices in accordance with the Design Manual as well as local
standards instituted by the Department to minimize increases in new development
runoff.
            a)   Natural area conservation;
            b)   Disconnection of rooftop runoff;
            C)   Disconnection of non-rooftop runoff;
            d)   Sheet flow to buffers;
            e)   Grass channels; and
            f)   Environmentally sensitive development.
         2.   The Director may reduce the minimum control requirements
specified under County law when nonstructural stormwater management practices
are incorporated into site designs according to the Design Manual.
      C.   Specific Design Considerations
         1.   Water quality. The design of best management practices must
consider - the thermal effects of the development on receiving streams. The
applicant must mitigate these effects if the Director determines that
mitigation is necessary to preserve the water quality of the receiving streams.
         2.   Recharge. If the delineation is unclear in the Soil Survey or if
a hydrologic soil group is not assigned to a specific soil, then the default
hydrologic soil group for recharge design is "B."1 There are no recharge
requirements for redevelopment project sites or for sites identified as
hotspots.
         3.   Channel protection. All surface ponds in Use III, Use IV, and
high quality Use I watersheds must be designed to provide 12-hour extended
detention of the one-year, 24-hour storm event. All other surface ponds and all
underground structures must be designed to provide 24-hour extended detention
of the one-year, 24-hour storm event.
1Soil types are grouped hydrologically in the Soil Survey.
         4.   Flood protection.
            a)   Overbank flood protection may only be required if the Director
determines that the receiving floodplain, flow path, or storm drain system is
insufficient to handle the flow from a 10-year storm. In such cases, the
stormwater management concept plan must show how the peak discharge of the
predeveloped 10-year, 24hour storm is maintained.
            b)   Management of the 100-year storm is required only when the
department determines that controls are necessary to protect existing
buildings.
         5.   Nonstructural best management practices. The Director may accept
nonstructural management practices to help satisfy the minimum stormwater
control requirements when the Director is reasonably certain that the
nonstructural management practices will remain functional after construction of
the development is complete.
19.00.01.05 Contributions and Dedications
      A.   An applicant making a contribution under Chapter 19 must provide the
contribution to the County before the Director issues a building permit for the
development.
      B.   An applicant dedicating land under Chapter 19 must sign any
agreement entered into with the Department or the Board before recording the
plats for the land being dedicated. If no recorded plat is required, then the
applicant must enter into the agreement with the Department or the Board before
the Director may issue a building permit to the applicant. The applicant must
provide to the Department a certified copy of any signed agreement entered into
with the Board.
19.00.01.06 Inspections and Maintenance
      A.   Notification required. A person must notify the Department of
Environmental Protection at least 48 hours before initiating any maintenance
work on a stormwater management facility.
      B.   Qualifications of maintenance personnel. A person that performs
repair or maintenance on a stormwater management facility must have
demonstrated experience in stormwater management facility construction and
inspection and hold a certificate of attendance awarded through a training
program approved by the Department of Environmental Protection. A person that
performs repair or maintenance on an underground facility must have the
training and credentials required under applicable state and federal law.
      C.   Final inspection. Upon completion of the repair or maintenance on a
stormwater management facility, the Department must conduct a final inspection
of the facility. If the Director determines that the facility is not in proper
working condition, the Director must prepare a written report specifying the
additional repair or maintenance needed to place the facility in proper working
condition and provide a copy of the report to the owner of the facility.
19.00.01.07 Disposal Requirements
      A.   Any person performing repair or maintenance on a stormwater
management facility must ensure that the receptacle used to transport materials
or debris resulting from the repair or maintenance has been cleaned of all
septage residue if the receptacle was previously used to transport septage.
      B.   Any person that transports waste materials resulting from repair or
maintenance of a stormwater management facility must submit a report to the
Department of Environmental Protection within 24 hours after disposing of the
materials. The report must be on a form provided by the Department of
Environmental Protection and must include the following information along with
a copy of the receipt from the disposal facility where the materials are
deposited:
         1.   Name, address, and phone number of the person transporting the
materials;
         2.   Sequence number and location of the facility from which the
materials were removed;
         3.   Types of structures from which the materials were removed and the
number of structures at the site;
         4.   Amount and types of waste materials removed;
         5.   Date the material was removed; and
         6.   Location of the facility to which the materials were delivered
for disposal.
19.00.01.08 Severability
      If a court holds that a portion of this regulation is invalid, the other
portions remain in effect.
19.00.01.09 Effective Date
      This regulation takes effect upon approval by the County Council.
   (Administrative History: Reg. No. 7-02 (Method 2); Dept.: Environmental
Protection and Permitting Services; Supersedes: Reg. No. 5-90)

first. Fees for the issuance or renewal of sediment control permits are:

         Activities   $260.00

         management facilities   $260.00
      4.   All other sediment control permits (Per square feet of disturbed
area)   $0.030
         Minimum fee   $670.00
      5.   Technical revisions to permits with no increase in
         disturbed area   35% of original fee
         Maximum fee   $1,450.00
         Minimum fee   $670.00
19.06.01.02 Stormwater Management Concept Plan Fees
      Stormwater management concept plans may include one or more of the
following:
      -   Onsite water quality control
      -   Onsite water quantity control
      -   A waiver of onsite water quality control
      -   A waiver of onsite water quantity control

      Fees for the evaluation of stormwater management concepts are:
Size of Development

July 1, 1997

         accordance with the standard contribution categories listed in
         Executive Regulation 5-90, Section 2.A.2.e.   $425.00

concept plans are 50% of the original fee for modifications that include
reevaluation of stormwater management facility sizing, design, or location, and
20% of the original fee for all other modifications.

      All fees must be paid at the time of application or before the Department
initiates reviews.
      Fees for the administration of the Floodplain District Program are:

July 1, 1997
      1.   Floodplain District Permit   $335.00

C.3.   $85.00
19.06.01.04 General
      The following provisions pertain to all fees covered by this regulation:
      1.   Refunds
         All fees are non-refundable.
      2.   Extensions
         The fee to extend sediment control and floodplain district permits
after written application and before the expiration of the original permit is
$85.00. Each extension is limited to six (6) months. Only two (2) extensions
may be granted for each permit. All subsequent extensions are considered to be
technical revisions.
      3.   Transfers
         Permit fees are not transferrable.
      4.   Change of Legal Description or Ownership
         The fee for a revision to a sediment control permit or a floodplain
district permit for changes of legal description or ownership is the minimum
permit fee.
      5.   Late Payment of Fees
         If fees are not paid as described in this regulation, the application
for permit will be returned to the applicant until such fees are paid.
      6.   Bond Replacement
         The fee for replacement of a Performance Bond, Cash Bond, Irrevocable
Letter of Credit, or Certificate of Guarantee is $50.00. If the purpose of the
replacement is to reduce the amount of the instrument due to partial completion
of stormwater management facilities, the fee is $100.00.
19.06.01.05 Severability
      If a court holds that part of this regulation is invalid, the invalidity
does not affect other parts.
19.06.01.06 Effective Date
      This regulation becomes effective on July 1, 1997.

***** SEC. 19-10 PERFORMANCE BOND — REGULATIONS *****
COMCOR 19.10.01 Certificates of Guarantee for Erosion and Sediment Control and
Stormwater Management
19.10.01.01
      In accordance with procedures authorized in Chapter 19, Article I, title
"Erosion and Sediment Control" Sections 19-10 and 19-17, Article II, title
"Stormwater Management", Sections 19-31 and 19-32 of the Montgomery County Code
1984, as amended, the following Executive Regulation pertains to the
establishment and use of Certificates of Guarantee to satisfy the requirements
of Chapter 19, Sections 19-10 and 19-32 of the Montgomery County Code 1984, as
amended.
19.10.01.02 Procedure for Approval to Issue Certificates of Guarantee
      A.   Any organization interested in applying to the Department of
Environmental Protection (DEP) for approval to issue Certificates of Guarantee,
pursuant to Chapter 19, Sections 19-10 and 19-32 of the Montgomery County Code,
1984, as amended, must submit to DEP a written request for such approval. The
written request must be signed by the president or chief executive officer of
the organization. The written request must set forth each of the Application
Standards, as listed below, and must explain in detail how the applicant meets
or exceeds each Application Standard.
      B.   Application Standards:
         1.   Structure of Approved Organization:
            a.   The organization must be incorporated under the laws of the
State of Maryland and must be in good standing under said laws at the time of
application. The organization must file a copy of its charter with DEP. It is
the duty of the organization, once approved, to file copies of all charter
amendments with DEP, and ensure that its corporate charter is not forfeited or
revoked during the time it is issuing Certificates of Guarantee.
            b.   The principal office of the organization must be located in
the State of Maryland and the address must be listed on the application.
            c.   The organization must have a resident agent, as required by
Maryland Corporation Law. The organization must inform DEP on the application
of the resident agent's name and address. It is the duty of the organization,
once approved, to notify DEP of all changes in the resident agent's name and
address.
            d.   The organization must have adopted working by-laws, copies of
which must be filed with DEP. It is the duty of the organization, once
approved, to file copies of any changes to the by-laws with DEP.
            e.   The organization must have a board consisting of not less than
three (3) directors. The board of directors is responsible for setting the
policy of the organization. Additionally, the board of directors is responsible
for admitting new members (although it may delegate this responsibility to a
specific committee), suspending or terminating existing members, approving
project applications, and taking action with respect to members who are
experiencing difficulty in connection with an individual project.
            f.   The officers of the organization must be elected at least
annually and must consist of at least a president and a secretary/treasurer.
The president presents such matters to the board of directors (as require board
approval) and controls and directs the activities and business of the
organization through its executive officer and staff. The treasurer is
responsible for reporting the financial condition of the organization,
submitting an annual budget for the board's approval, and obtaining an annual
audit of the organization's financial records. The secretary is responsible for
keeping the minutes of the Board of Directors and preserving them as a
permanent record.
            g.   The organization must have an executive officer who is
responsible for handling the routine or day-to-day affairs of the organization.
            h.   The organization must employ legal counsel who is admitted to
practice before the Court of Appeals of Maryland. It is the duty of the
organization to notify DEP of the name, address and telephone number of its
legal counsel on the application and whenever the legal counsel changes.
            i.   The organization must maintain normal business hours, from
approximately 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., five days a week, weekends and holidays
excepted. The office must have a listed telephone number which is operational
during business hours.
            j.   The organization or its members must be able to demonstrate
experience and technical competence in the supervision of .the construction of
public and private improvements in connection with the development of property
for residential, commercial or industrial use, including, without limitation;
grading, street and road construction, sediment control and stormwater
management (hereinafter referred to as Guaranteed Work).
         2 .   Meetings:
            a.   The organization must hold its annual meeting at a date, time
and place which has been communicated in writing to DEP at least twenty (20)
days in advance. DEP may, at its discretion, send a representative to the
annual meeting.
            b.   The organization must hold regular meetings, on at least a
monthly basis, at a date, time and place which has been communicated in writing
to DEP at least ten (10) days in advance of each meeting. DEP may, at its
discretion, send a representative to any or all of such meetings.
            c.   The organization must maintain at its business office, a
corporate record book which contains, inter alia, minutes of all the
organization's meetings signed by the secretary. The corporate record book must
be open for inspection, during business hours, to a representative of DEP.
            d.   At the regular and annual meetings the business of the
organization must include the admission of new members to the organization,
suspension or termination of members of the organization, consideration and
approval of applications by members for a Certificate of Guarantee and
consideration of any pending Certificates of Guarantee in which the
organization has been informed that a member of the organization is
experiencing difficulty in construction of the Guaranteed Work.
         3.   Financial Responsibility:
            a.   The organization must have monetary assets of at least 5% of
the total amount of the outstanding Certificates of Guarantee. The cost of the
Guaranteed Work is as set forth in the permit issued by Montgomery County.
            b.   The organization must hold the aforesaid monies, in a
federally or state insured interest-bearing account as determined by the board
of directors.
            c.   The organization must, at the request of DEP, from time to
time, promptly inform DEP of the amount of monies being held by the
organization and the manner in which said monies are being held.
            d.   The organization must employ a certified public accountant to
prepare an annual profit and loss statement. Monthly financial reports may be
signed by the organization's vice-president or treasurer. A copy of these
financial documents must be forwarded, upon completion, promptly to DEP.
         4.   Membership:
            a.   In those cases where the organization is wholly owned by a
parent corporation, the organization may require, as a condition of membership
in the organization, that the member also be a member in good standing of the
parent corporation. Said parent corporation may restrict membership in the
parent corporation to those members who share a common business purpose, e.g.,
builders or developers, provided said restriction has a rational basis, and
further provided there is no discrimination among prospective members based on
race, creed, color, sex, age or national origin.
      C.   Review and Approval of Applications by DEP:
         Upon receipt of the written application from an organization for
approval to issue Certificates of Guarantee, and upon receipt of any and all
additional information which DEP may reasonably require, DEP must, within
thirty (30) days, notify the applicant, in writing, of the director's decision.
Any decision not to approve an organization must contain a written explanation
of the reason or reasons for disapproval. Any organization aggrieved by the
Director's decision may submit further written material to the director in
writing within ten (10) days from receipt of the decision of disapproval. Upon
reconsideration by the Director a written decision must be issued to the
organization, in writing, within fifteen (15) days after receipt of the written
materials. The decision of the Director is final except for further judicial
review otherwise provided by law.
19.10.01.03
      This regulation will take effect 30 days after the date of adoption by
the County Council.
   (Administrative History: Reg. No. 13-90 (Method 2); Dept.: Environmental
Protection; Supersedes: Reg. No. 40-86)
COMCOR 19.10.02 Erosion and Sediment Control Rules and Regulations
19.10.02.01
      Under procedures authorized in Chapter 19, Article I entitled "Erosion
and Sediment Control," Sections 19-10 and 19-17, and in Chapter 2A, Section 2A-
15, of the Montgomery County Code 1972, as amended, the following Executive
Regulation pertains to Sediment Control Plans and all land disturbing
activities as defined by Chapter 19. Definitions of the terms used in these
Regulations are provided in Chapter 19, Sections 19-1 and 19-21.
19.10.02.02
      All land disturbing activities and sediment control plans must comply
with these Rules and Regulations.
      Any violation of these provisions is a violation of Chapter 19. A person
must not violate the provisions of Chapter 19 or these Rules and Regulations.
19.10.02.03
      General Administration - Erosion and Sediment Control Plans
      A.   The plans submitted by the Applicant must be designed to minimize
sedimentation on any off-site property, and in storm drains and watercourses.
The plans must show on-site grading and drainage control designed in a manner
to prevent off-site property damage. The review of sediment control plans may
include on-site field evaluation.
      B.   The Department must not approve any plan unless the plan meets the
provisions of Chapter 19 and these Rules and Regulations. If the plan is not
approved as submitted, the Department must give timely written notification of
the deficiencies to the applicant.
      C.   Erosion and Sediment Control plans for specific sites must be
prepared by a professional engineer or land surveyor unless prior written
approval of preparation by another person has been granted by the Department.
      D.   In addition to approval by the department, the Maryland National
Capital Park and Planning Commission (M.N.C.P.P.C) must approve erosion and
sediment control plans for facilities that are to be located on property owned
by or to be dedicated to the M.N.C.P.P.C..
      E.   The following information, proposals, and supporting certifications
must be submitted with the Erosion and Sediment Control (SC) Plans. The SC plan
must be submitted with 2 prints for review. Other information may be submitted
as separate items as per the checklist below. A reproducible must be submitted
once the plan is ready to be approved. Items may be added to or deleted from
this list if deemed necessary by the Department.
         1.   Sediment Control Application (retain pink copy for applicant's
record)
         2.   1F-1 form
         3.   Vicinity sketch, legend, scale, north arrow (Show on SC plan).
         4.   Title block by subdivision name, lot, block or other legal
descriptive title (Show on SC plan).
         5.   Boundary line outline, ownership and total acreage of property
for which work is to be performed. (Show on SC plan, where applicable).
         6.   Delineation of total area to be disturbed (Show on SC plan).
         7.   Existing and proposed elevations and contours on the site. A 2'
contour interval must be used, unless otherwise specified by the plan approval
agency. (Show on SC plan).
         8.   Existing and proposed improvements to the property; including,
but not limited to: streets, parking lots, utility installations, buildings,
retaining walls, and other structures (Show on SC plan).
         9.   Delineation of the 100-year floodplain. No fill or permanent
structures are permitted within the confines of the 100-year floodplain without
a floodplain district permit (Show on SC plan).
         10.   Grade establishment plans and profiles for public streets, where
applicable, as submitted to the Montgomery County Department of Transportation
(1 copy).
         11.   Storm drainage study including drainage area map, computations,
and scale. Delineate contributory subdrainage areas within and outside of the
site. Indicate the flow of a 10 year storm (Q10) for any area served by an
existing or proposed on-site drain or channel (2 copies).
         12.   Show how all storm drainage is handled. Where public storm
drainage is involved, Montgomery County Department of Transportation must
review for issuance of storm drainage permits. Show receiving channel profile
and typical cross-section. Indicate velocity of Q10 storm flows at pipe
outfalls, outfall structures and receiving channels at the property line. Show
existing and proposed contours for a minimum of 100 feet below storm drain
outfalls (show on SC plan).
         13.   On projects requiring on-site stormwater management, the
Stormwater Management Rules and Regulations adopted pursuant to Article II of
this Chapter apply.
         14.   Sediment control measures must be designed to minimize erosion
and off-site sedimentation from start of land disturbance to establishment of
permanent stabilization. Sediment control measures must be located so that
construction during the approved phase will not interfere with the function of
that measure. (Show on SC plan).
         15.   Sediment control measures must not be constructed within 20 feet
of any building foundation. A building permit must not be issued for
construction within 20 feet of a sediment control measure unless removal of the
measure is approved by the Department. (show on SC plan).
         16.   The plan must include a construction sequence that requires
clearing for, installation and approval of required sediment control measures
prior to commencing any other land disturbing activity. Installation of storm
drainage, utility construction, installation/conversion of stormwater
management structures, temporary and permanent stabilization must be included
in the sequence with other construction activities. The sequence must specify
removal of sediment control measures only with prior inspection and permission.
(show on SC plan).
         17.   Temporary diversion of all storm drain outfalls into sediment
trapping devices is encouraged. Diversion is required when the off-site
drainage area to a storm drain system does not exceed 50% of the on-site
drainage area to that system. This requirement may be waived if the Department
determines that site conditions make the practice impossible (show on SC plan).
         18.   Sediment control measures must be detailed on the drawings in
accordance with the Standards and Specifications (show on SC plan).
         19.   On projects incorporating sediment basins, the following
information must be submitted:
            a.   Specific location of the dam (show on SC plan);
            b.   Plan view of the dam and the storage basin (show on SC plan);
            c.   Cross section and profile of dam, emergency spillway, and
principal spillway. (show on SC plan);
            d.   Specific details, notes, and construction specifications (show
on SC plan); and
            e.   Run-off calculations for 10-year storm (show on design data
sheet similar to that shown in the Standards and Specifications).
         20.   Temporary sediment basins and traps that pond water greater than
nine (9) feet in width and eighteen (18) inches in depth must be surrounded by
safety fence at least forty-two (42) inches in height with openings not greater
than three (3) inches in width. This fence must be firmly anchored to posts no
more than eight (8) feet apart and constructed in a manner to prevent sagging.
(Show on SC plan).
         21.   Shoring, retaining walls, and other devices to safeguard public
streets, alleys, or other properties or persons must be designed by a
professional engineer, and meet accepted engineering standards. Federal
regulations governing excavations, trenching, and shoring must be followed in
the design of these supporting systems.
         22.   Erosion and Sediment Control Plans must include the following
certifications:
            a.   Owner/Developer's Certification: which certifies that all
activities covered by the sediment control permit will be done in conformance
with tne approved plan and that there will be a person responsible for sediment
control on the construction project who has a current certificate of training
at a Maryland Department of the Environment approved training program for the
control of sedimentation and erosion. The certification must be dated and
signed by the owner/developer. (Show on SC plan).
            b.   Design Certification: which certifies that the plan has been
prepared in accordance with the Standards and Specifications, and the
Montgomery County Erosion and Sediment Control Rules and Regulations. The
certification must be dated and signed by the professional engineer or land
surveyor and registration number given. (Show on SC plan)
            c.   Certification of cut and fill and disturbed area: which
certifies the estimated amounts of fill, cut and disturbed area as shown on the
approved plan. The certification must be dated and signed by the professional
engineer or land surveyor and registration number given. (Show on SC plan).
         23.   Where protection of specimen trees and/or other vegetation is
required, it must be shown on the plan. The method of protection must be
specified with a detail or excerpt from the Standards and Specifications given
(show on SC plan).
         24.   A temporary stabilization note must be placed on the plan that
conforms with the requirements of paragraphs G and H of
19.10.02.04 of these Rules and Regulations (Show on SC Plan).
         25.   After the plan has been reviewed by the Department, the owner
must be notified in writing as to fee and bond required. The appropriate forms
for bonding and easement will be mailed, along with the fee and bond notice.
         26.   When the above requirements have been satisfied and the plan is
approved, three (3) sets of prints (4 sets if stormwater management plans are
required) must be submitted to the Department prior to issuance of permit.
      F.   The Department may waive the requirement for scale plans or drawings
if proposed land disturbing activity will comply with the limitations of the
Small Land Disturbing Activities Agreement. Those limitations are as follows:
         1.   The property must not be disturbed more than 20,000 square feet
for commercial, or 30,000 square feet for residential development at any one
time;
         2.   Proposed impervious surfaces on the property must not total
greater than 15,000 square feet;
         3.   Volume of earth movement on the property must be less than 1,000
cubic yards; and
         4.   No more than 3 contiguous lots or parcels must be approved for
development at one time under one ownership through use of this agreement.
19.10.02.04 Erosion and Sediment Control
      A.   The permittee must notify the Department 48 hours before commencing
any land disturbing activity and, unless waived by the Department, is required
to hold a pre-construction meeting between the permittee or representative and
an authorized representative of the Department.
      B.   The permittee must:
            (1)   construct all erosion and sediment control measures as per
the approved plan;
            (2)   have them inspected by the Department prior to beginning any
other land disturbances;
            (3)   ensure that all runoff from disturbed areas is directed to
the sediment control devices; and
            (4)   obtain permission from the department prior to removal of any
erosion or sediment control measure.
      C.   The permittee must direct water run-off from any land disturbing
activity through an approved sediment control measure.
      D.   The permittee must protect all points of construction ingress and
egress to prevent the deposition of materials onto traversed public
thoroughfare(s). This may be accomplished by installing and maintaining a
stabilized construction entrance, or by washing all vehicle wheels in a safe
disposal area. All materials deposited onto public thoroughfare(s) must be
removed immediately.
      E.   The permittee must periodically inspect and maintain all erosion and
sediment control measures in continuously effective condition until they are
removed with permission from the Department.
      F.   The permittee must fence the perimeter of all temporary sediment
basins or traps, which pond water in a pool greater than nine (9) feet in width
or eighteen (18) inches in depth, with a safety fence greater than forty-two
(42) inches in height and openings no greater than three (3) inches in width.
The fence must be firmly anchored to posts no more than eight (8) feet apart
and be constructed to prevent sagging.
      G.   All slopes steeper than 3:1, basin or trap embankments, and
perimeter dikes must be stabilized with sod, seed and anchored straw mulch, or
other approved stabilization measures, within seven (7) calendar days of
establishment. Areas disturbed outside of the perimeter sediment control system
must be minimized and immediately stabilized. Maintenance must be performed as
necessary to ensure continued stabilization.
      H.   The permittee must apply sod, seed and anchored straw mulch, or
other approved stabilization measures to all disturbed areas within fourteen
(14) calendar days after stripping and grading activities have ceased on that
area. Maintenance must be performed as necessary to ensure continued
stabilization. Active construction areas, such as borrow or stockpile areas,
roadway improvements, and areas within fifty (50) feet of a building under
construction, may be exempted from this requirement, provided that erosion and
sediment control measures are installed and maintained to protect those areas.
During the months of November through February, when seeding and sodding are
found to be impractical, an approved anchored mulch must be applied. In these
cases, seeding must be completed prior to the following April 15.
      I.   Prior to removal of sediment control measures, the permittee must
stabilize all contributory disturbed areas using sod or an approved permanent
seed mixture with required soil amendments and an approved anchored mulch. Wood
fiber mulch may only be used in seeding season where the slope does not exceed
10% and grading has been done to promote sheet flow drainage. Areas brought to
finished grade during the seeding season must be permanently stabilized within
fourteen (14) calendar days of establishment. When property is brought to
finished grade during the months of November through February, and seeding and
sodding is found to be impractical, an approved anchored mulch must be applied
to critical areas. The final permanent stabilization must be completed prior to
the following April 15.
      J.   The Department must inspect all permitted land disturbing activity,
except where waived under Chapter 19, Subsection 19-12(g), and may require the
permittee to obtain testing, special inspections, and professional
certification, and/or to submit "as-built" plans to ensure that construction
has been done in conformance with provisions of the approved plan and
applicable standards and specifications. Where testing, special inspections,
and professional certification, or "as-built" plans are required, reports
documenting acceptability of the work must be submitted to the Department
within a specified time.
      K.   The Department must withhold issuance of a completion certificate
for release of the performance bond or other instrument for those projects
requiring testing, special inspection, professional certification, and "as-
built" plans until all of the above have been accepted by the Department.
      L.   When the approved erosion and sediment control plans include
sediment basins, inspection is required at the following stages of
construction:
         1.   Stripping of area under embankment;
         2.   Core trench excavation;
         3.   Installation of riser and pipe spillway;
         4.   Backfill of riser and pipe spillway;
         5.   Emergency spillway construction;
         6.   Outlet protection; and
         7.   Final stabilization.
         Additional inspections may be required if needed to assure compliance
with the approved plan and specifications. Construction must not proceed to the
next stage until each inspection has been made and approved by this Department
or inspected and certified as provided for in Chapter 19, Subsection 12(g). In
either case, this Department must be notified twenty-four (24) hours prior to
each required inspection.
      M.   The site, work, materials, plans, and test reports must be available
at all times for inspection by duly authorized officials of Montgomery County.
      N.   Surface flows over cut and fill slopes must be controlled by either
re-directing flows from traversing the slopes or by installing mechanical
devices to lower the water downslope without causing erosion. Dikes must be
installed and maintained at the top of cut or fill slopes until the slope and
drainage area are fully stabilized.
      O.   Permanent swales or other points of concentrated water flow must be
stabilized with sod, or seed with an approved erosion control matting.
      P.   Temporary sediment trapping devices must be removed within thirty
(30) calendar days following establishment of permanent stabilization in all
contributory drainage areas. Stormwater management structures used temporarily
for sediment control must be converted to the permanent configuration within
this time period as well.
19.10.02.05 Grading Control
      A.   No permanent cut or fill slope with a gradient steeper than 3:1 is
permitted in lawn maintenance areas. A slope gradient of up to 2:1 is permitted
in low maintenance areas provided that those areas are indicated on the erosion
and sediment control plan with a low-maintenance ground cover specified. Slope
gradient steeper than 2:1 is not permitted with vegetative stabilization.
      B.   The permittee must provide transition into the grade of the
adjoining property at or before the boundary line. An exception may be given
where a retaining wall is properly designed and built entirely on the property
of the owner who creates the grading, or where that owner has a letter of
authorization from the adjoining property owner to extend the slope into the
adjoining property.
19.10.02.06 Drainage Control
      A.   The permittee must not create a fill which causes water to pond on
off-site or adjacent property, unless the fill is associated with an approved
temporary sediment control structure, permanent stormwater management
structure, or planned landscape structure. The permittee must first obtain
ownership or easement for that use from the owner of the off-site or adjacent
property.
      B.   The permittee must install a splashblock at the bottom of each
downspout unless the downspout is connected by a drain line to an acceptable
outlet.
      C.   For finished grading, the permittee must provide adequate gradients
so as to: (1) prevent water from standing on the surface of lawns more than
twenty-four (24) hours after the end of a rainfall, except in swale flow areas
which may drain as long as forty-eight (48) hours after the end of a rainfall,
and (2) provide positive drainage away from all building foundations or
openings
19.10.02.07 Design Criteria
      The following design criteria are acceptable for use, and must be
referenced or shown on plans submitted to the Department:
      A.   The "1983 Maryland Standards and Specifications for Soil Erosion and
Sediment Control," or any subsequent revisions;
      B.   Storm Drain Design Standards and Specifications, by the Washington
Suburban Sanitary Commission;
      C.   Interim Storm Drain Design Criteria, by the Montgomery County
Department of Transportation;
      D.   SCS, Maryland Standards and Specifications for Ponds, Practice Code
378, revised;
      E.   SCS Technical Release No. 55, Urban Hydrology for Small Watersheds;
      F.   SCS Engineering Field Manual; and
      G.   Interim Hydraulic Criteria for Design of Highways, by the Maryland
State Highway Administration.
19.10.02.08 Effective Date
      This Executive Regulation will take effect 30 days after the date of
adoption by the County Council.
(Administrative History: Reg. No. 36-90 (Method 2); Dept.: Environmental
Protection; Supersedes: Reg. No. 38-86)

***** SEC. 19-29 STORMWATER MANAGEMENT LOAN PROGRAM — REGULATIONS *****
COMCOR 19.29.01 Stormwater Management Loan Program
19.29.01.01 Background Information
      1.1   On November 20, 2001, the County Council amended County law
regarding storm water management facilities by enacting revisions to Sections
19-20 through 19-35 of the Montgomery County Code. These amendments create a
loan program to help property owners upgrade their storm water management
facilities to meet approved design standards. The countywide storm water
program will provide publicly funded maintenance to replace private maintenance
for the facilities that have been improved through County loans and
subsequently accepted by the County for continued maintenance. The loan
program, which is to be administered by the Department of Environmental
Protection ("DEP" or the "Department"), is designed to promote a countywide
storm water maintenance program. These amendments enable the County to comply
with the requirements of the NPDES (National Pollutant Discharge Elimination
System) permit, issued to the County under the authority of the federal Clean
Water Act.
19.29.01.02 Administration and Procedures
2.1   Use of Funds
         The principal use of funds from the Storm Water Management Loan
Program (the "Program") is to facilitate the repair and upgrade of storm water
management structures belonging to private property owners by helping the
owners restore the structures to their originally approved design standards or
better if required under existing law or agreed to by the County and the
property owner. The funds may also be used to help repair any property damage
associated with the restoration or upgrade of a storm water management
structure. Once this is accomplished, borrower must enter into an agreement
with the County providing for the restored structure to subsequently be
publicly maintained under the County-wide storm water management program.
2.2   Limitations on Use of Funds
         The use of funds from the Storm Water Management Loan Program, as
described in Section 2.1, is subject to the following limitations:
         a.   The proposed scope of work must be pre-approved by DEP.
         b.   Before authorizing direct disbursement of any payments due to a
contractor that the borrower has hired to upgrade a storm water management
facility under an agreement created solely between the borrower and the
contractor, DEP must confirm that the contractor has either performed or made
satisfactory progress toward performing the pre-approved repairs and
maintenance work correctly and in accordance with the agreed upon scope of
work.
         c.   The County must make loan payments directly to the contractor on
a draw down schedule consisting of installments. The first installment of 25
percent of the total sum due under the contract is payable only after the
County receives a request for payment from the borrower in a form approved by
the County and the Department has verified that the contractor has ordered
materials and begun performance. The remaining installments are payable at
various completion stages under the agreed upon scope of work. In each
instance, the borrower must request payment from the County and the Department
must verify that the contractor has performed each repair or maintenance task
correctly before the County may authorize a payment to the contractor.
         d.   Any contractor that a borrower hires to upgrade a storm water
management facility must execute a performance bond naming Montgomery County as
the obligee before the County may pay the contractor under the Program.
         e.   A borrower must not use County funds to pay for a contractor's
unanticipated costs. All cost overruns are the responsibility of the borrower,
not the County.
2.3   Application Procedures
         The Director approves and denies loans for property owners who apply
for funds under the Storm Water Management Loan Program. The Director may
delegate this authority. Applications must be submitted in writing in a form
approved by the Department and forwarded, along with the financial information
described in Section 2.6, to the following address:
            Director
            Department of Environmental Protection
            255 Rockville Pike, Suite 120
            Rockville, Maryland 20850
2.4   Lending Standards
         When reviewing applications for the use of funds from the Storm Water
Management Loan Program, the Director must consider the following factors:
         a.   Existing commitments for use of the funds;
         b.   The existence and expectation of funds projected to be available
in the program;
         c.   The degree to which the proposed use of funds will further DEP's
storm water quality and quantity control goals;
         d.   Financial requirements and capacity to repay the loan as
described in Section 2.6; and
         e.   Other factors that the Director deems consistent with Department
goals of preparing storm water management facilities for public maintenance.
2.5   Priorities
         a.   The Director may give priority to loan applicants who propose to
upgrade the following facilities and structures:
            (1)   Ponds with structural problems that prevent them from
functioning as designed (e.g., dry ponds that are full of water, wet ponds that
are leaking);
            (2)   Dams classified as high or significant hazards with
structural problems involving the dam or pond controls that could cause an
increased potential for failure;
            (3)   Underground structures (metal pipes especially) with
structural problems that could cause a parking lot to collapse and cause
injuries or significant property damage;
            (4)   Structures with other safety problems;
            (5)   Larger ponds (i.e., drainage area larger than 50 acres) with
structural problems; and
            (6)   Smaller facilities with structural defects in the pipes,
controls, concrete structures or embankment.
         b.   In addition to the priorities described in this Section, the
Director may take into account the size of the drainage area served by a storm
water facility and may also approve loans for applicants to upgrade other types
of facilities and structures, including the following:
            (1)   Facilities with a great pollution potential if not repaired
and maintained. (This category includes old oil grit separators, because of the
limited storage provided and the nature of collected road and parking lot
pollutants.)
            (2)   Nonfunctioning structures that offer real opportunity for
environmental improvements through repair or replacement (i.e., wetland habitat
potential).
            (3)   Wet ponds that create temperature discharge problems for
temperature sensitive downstream waters.
            (4)   Structures, as determined by the Department, where
abandonment, or removal is environmentally and economically prudent.
2.6   Financial Requirements
         a.   Funds to be disbursed under this program are available to
property owners who demonstrate, to the satisfaction of the Director, that they
are able to repay the loan. The Director must not approve a loan application
unless the Director finds that an applicant's credit record, if applicable,
includes the following information:
            (1)   The income generated or potentially generated by the
applicant;
            (2)   The current expenses or anticipated expenses of the
applicant;
            (3)   The amount of any outstanding loans and the monthly payments
required to repay the loans;
            (4)   Other financial resources that the applicant indicates are
available to repay the loan;
            (5)   The ability of the applicant to generate additional fees or
contributions to repay the loan;
            (6)   The credit history of the applicant, if applicable; and
            (7)   The collateral that the applicant is willing to offer as
security.
         b.   The applicant must furnish the following financial information
when submitting the loan application to DEP for review:
            (1)   Financial statements, which at a minimum include a Statement
of Position (i.e., balance sheet) and a Statement of Operations (i.e., income
statement) for the most recent fiscal year, preferably accompanied by an
independent public accountant's report;
            (2)   An itemized budget reflecting revenues and expenditures for
the current fiscal year, and next fiscal year, if available;
            (3)   Descriptions and cost estimates of the repairs and
maintenance work needed to restore the facility;
            (4)   A description and estimated value of collateral that the
applicant is willing to offer as security.
            (5)   Copies of federal and state tax returns for the 3 previous
years, if applicable;
            (6)   Proof of other financial resources available to repay the
loan; and
            (7)   Any other financial information that the Director may from
time to time deem necessary to adequately assess the creditworthiness of loan
applicants.
         c.   Common ownership communities. Subsection b(l) is not applicable
if the borrower is a common ownership community such as a condominium or
homeowners association. For a common ownership community association to be
eligible for a loan under the Program, the association's governing documents
must not prohibit the association from assiging special assessments or monthly
assessment income as collateral for the loan.
2.7   Loan Terms and Conditions
         a.   The maximum repayment term for any loan under the Storm Water
Management Loan Program is 10 years.
         b.   Loans made available through the Program carry an interest rate
equal to the County's current rate of earnings on invested funds on the day
that the loan is approved, plus an additional one percent to cover
administrative costs. The interest rate must remain constant for the full term
of the loan.
         c.   Borrowers must make all payments according to the time and
frequency schedule stipulated in the loan agreement.
         d.   The Director must not forgive a loan. However, the Director may
defer payments when a borrower demonstrates, to the satisfaction of the
Director, a sufficient temporary hardship to significantly impede the
borrower's ability to make timely payments. The Director may approve a deferral
request for a period not to exceed 6 months. The Chief Administrative Officer
must approve any subsequent deferral of the same loan.
         e.   During any period of deferment, the borrower has the option to:
            (1)   continue paying the accrued interest while only the principal
of the loan is deferred; or
            (2)   defer both the principal and the interest so that the
deferred interest continues to accrue during the deferment period.
2.8   Appeals
         An applicant whose loan request is denied for any reason other than
insufficient funds in the Program to approve the request may make a formal
request for reconsideration of the decision to deny the loan by filing an
appeal in writing with the Director within 30 days after the applicant receives
written notification that the loan was not approved. The Director must review
the request for reconsideration and render a final written decision on behalf
of the County within 30 days after receiving the appeal.
2.9   Loan Nonpayment or Default
   The Director must forward any loan that the Director deems to be in default
under the terms of the loan agreement to the Office of the County Attorney
within one month after the date of the default to initiate collection efforts.
(Administrative History: Reg. No. 11-00 (Method 1); Dept.: Environmental
Protection)

19.31.01.03 Contribution Limits
      The contribution required must not exceed the cost of providing onsite
SWM. In such cases where the applicant can provide evidence, acceptable to DEP,
that onsite SWM can be provided at a lower cost (including the cost of land and
long term maintenance) than the required contribution, the Director will adjust
the contribution to be no greater than the applicant’s estimated cost
(including land cost and long term maintenance) of providing onsite SWM.
19.31.01.04 Other Contribution Options
      By mutual agreement of the applicant and the Director, and when the
applicant has obtained a waiver of the required onsite SWM, DEP (or MNCPPC when
the site is on parkland) may accept the dedication of land, other specific
improvements, or an easement for the construction, operation, and maintenance
of an offsite SWM facility in lieu of a portion of or all of the monetary
contribution.
19.31.01.05 Grandfather Clause
      For land that was granted a waiver of onsite stormwater management prior
to the effective date of this executive regulation the amount of contribution
will be based on the previously adopted schedules, provided that the
contribution is paid by July 1, 1991. If the contribution is not paid
      by that date, the amount will be in accordance with the current schedule
as adopted by this regulation.
19.31.01.06 Effective Date
      This Executive Regulation takes effect 30 days after the date of adoption
by the County Council.
