APPENDIX J      MONTGOMERY COUNTY GOVERNMENT JOB SHARING AGREEMENT
(If 2 full-time employees wish to share one job, each must complete a separate
agreement.)
This agreement is between ______________________________________,
_______________________
               employees name            position
and the Montgomery County __________________________________________. The
effective date of
               department/office name
this job sharing agreement is _______________________________. The work
schedule is as follows:
                  date
Sunday _______________   Monday _______________   Tuesday _______________
Wednesday _______________   Thursday _______________   Friday _______________
Saturday _______________. The work schedule must include not less than 40
regularly scheduled hours per pay period.
Attach a copy of the job sharing plan that shows how the duties of the position
will be divided.
The employee understands and accepts the following conditions of job sharing
and part-time employment:
   •   Annual leave, sick leave, holiday leave, and personal leave days are
prorated.
   •   Paid time off (PTO) is prorated.
   •   Health benefits are not affected and remain the same.
   •   Retirement benefits may be based on a combination of full-time and part-
time service.
   •   Life insurance and tuition assistance benefits (ETAP) decrease by 50
percent.
   •   Long term disability benefits are not available to part-time employees.
   •   The maximum for deferred compensation is 25 percent of salary.
   •   Seniority credits for reduction-in-force (RIF) and for meeting minimum
qualification requirements are prorated. For example, one year of part-time
service at 40 hours per pay period equals 6 months of seniority for RIF or 6
months of experience toward minimum qualification requirements.
   •   If the employee works more than 40 hours in a pay period, the employee
must not be paid at the overtime rate or receive compensatory time at the
overtime rate unless the employee has worked more than 40 hours in a work week
or 80 hours in a pay period.
   •   All other benefits and the laws, regulations, and rules that determine
the job sharers conditions of employment apply as to a part-time employee.
The supervisor and department director must evaluate the job sharing agreement
under the following standards:
   •   operational requirements must be met;
   •   service to clients or the public must be maintained or improved;
   •   costs to the County must not increase;
   •   each office or operation must have enough staff on duty during the
normal period of public service, and
   •   the job sharing arrangement must not diminish the ability of the
department to assign responsibility and accountability to the employee for
providing County services and performing the employees official duties.
The supervisor must review the plan and meet with the employee or employees to
discuss the plan. The supervisor should suggest any adjustments to the plan
necessary to maintain the effectiveness of the work unit. If the supervisor and
employee agree, they must sign the completed job sharing agreement and submit
it to the department director for approval. If they cannot agree, the
supervisor must submit to the department director a written summary of the
areas of agreement and disagreement and a copy of the proposed plan.
The department director must review the job sharing plan and:
   •   approve it
   •   disapprove it, or
   •   suggest changes in the terms for consideration by the employee and the
supervisor to help them reach agreement on the plan.
If the plan is not approved, the department director must give the employee the
reason for not approving the request. The decision of the department director
is final.
The department director must:
   •   give a copy of the approved or disapproved plan to the employee
   •   ensure that a copy is placed in each employees department operating
file, and
   •   send a copy to the Director, Office of Human Resources.
If one of the job-sharing employees leaves, the department director may:
   •   renew the job sharing agreement and fill the vacant position under merit
system procedures, or
   •   dissolve the job sharing agreement and return the remaining employee to
full-time status.
If the department director dissolves the job sharing agreement and the
remaining employee refuses to return to a full-time position, the department
director may abolish the part-time position and conduct a RIF under Section 30*
of the Personnel Regulations. The decision of the department director is final.

APPENDIX N   ANNUAL LEAVE TRANSFER FORM
To be completed by employee, employees spouse, and spouses supervisor:
Under Section 16-13 of the Personnel Regulations and Article 14.14 of the MCGEO
Agreement, an employee who is married to another County employee may transfer
annual leave to the employees spouse to enable the spouse to use the leave to
care for a child or children. The following conditions apply to the annual
leave transfer:
   •   the employee or the employees spouse must have legal responsibility for
the care of the child or children;
   •   the spouse must use the leave to care for:
       °   a child or children under the age of 13; or
       °   an older child with a medically certified disability that makes the
child incapable of self care;
   •   the employees spouse must sign the form to indicate that he or she has
agreed to accept the transferred leave;
   •   the spouses supervisor must sign the form indicating that the employees
spouse is eligible to use the transferred leave under the terms of the
Personnel Regulations or MCGEO Agreement; and;
   •   an employee may transfer leave to the employees spouse only in
increments of 40 hours.

is required to obtain a benefit. While you are not required to provide this
information, failure to do so may result in a denial of your request for FMLA
leave. You have 15 calendar days to return this form to your supervisor.

APPENDIX T MONTGOMERY COUNTY GOVERNMENT CERTIFICATION FOR SERIOUS INJURY OR
ILLNESS OF COVERED SERVICEMEMBER FOR MILITARY FAMILY LEAVE
(Family and Medical Leave Act of 1993)
___________________________________________________________________________________________
The Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) provides that an employer may require
an employee seeking military family leave due to a serious injury or illness of
a covered servicemember to submit a timely, and complete certification
providing sufficient facts to support the request for leave.
 
SECTION I: For Completion by the EMPLOYEE and/or the COVERED SERVICEMEMBER for
whom the Employee Is Requesting Leave The employee or covered servicemember
should complete Section I before having Section II completed. Your response is
required to obtain or retain the benefit of FMLA-protected leave. Failure to do
so may result in a denial of an employee’s FMLA request. You have 15 calendar
days to return this form to your supervisor.
SECTION II: For Completion by a UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE (“DOD”)
HEALTH CARE PROVIDER or a HEALTH CARE PROVIDER who is either: (1) a United
States Department of Veterans Affairs (“VA”) health care provider; (2) a DOD
TRICARE network authorized private health care provider; or (3) a DOD non-
network TRICARE authorized private health care provider.  
INSTRUCTIONS to the HEALTH CARE PROVIDER: The employee listed on Page 2 has
requested leave under the FMLA to care for a family member who is a member of
the Regular Armed Forces, the National Guard, or the Reserves who is undergoing
medical treatment, recuperation, or therapy, is otherwise in outpatient status,
or is otherwise on the temporary disability retired list for a serious injury
or illness. For purposes of FMLA leave, a serious injury or illness is one that
was incurred in the line of duty on active duty that may render the
servicemember medically unfit to perform the duties of his or her office,
grade, rank, or rating.
A complete and sufficient certification to support a request for FMLA leave due
to a covered servicemember’s serious injury or illness includes written
documentation confirming that the covered servicemember’s injury or illness was
incurred in the line of duty on active duty and that the covered servicemember
is undergoing treatment for such injury or illness by a health care provider
listed above. Answer, fully and completely, all applicable parts. Several
questions seek a response as to the frequency or duration of a condition,
treatment, etc. Your answer should be your best estimate based upon your
medical knowledge, experience, and examination of the patient. Be as specific
as you can; terms such as “lifetime,” “unknown,” or “indeterminate” may not be
sufficient to determine FMLA coverage. Limit your responses to the condition
for which the employee is seeking leave.

before any of the below sections can be completed by a health care provider.)

***** MONTGOMERY COUNTY CODE CHAPTER 33, ARTICLE III. EMPLOYEES RETIREMENT
SYSTEM, SEC. 33-37 MEMBERSHIP REQUIREMENTS AND MEMBERSHIP GROUPS REGULATIONS

COMCOR 33.37.01 Elected Officials Plan
33.37.01.01 Authority
   (a)   The County Executive is empowered to adopt regulations under Method
(3), under Section 2A-15 of the Montgomery County Code, to allow eligible
elected officials to make the choices provided in Chapter 33, Section 33-37 of
the Montgomery County Code.
33.37.01.02 Purpose
   (a)   The Montgomery County Elected Officials' Plan Regulations are
established to provide uniform procedures for the administration of the Elected
Officials' Plan. These Regulations are promulgated to assist elected officials
who are eligible to participate in the Elected Officials' Plan and to promote
and implement efficient and equitable practices consistent with Chapter 33 of
the Montgomery County Code.
33.37.01.03 Applicability
   (a)    These regulations apply to the elected officials described in Section
4(b)(1)* herein.
      *Editors note—see
33.37.01.04(b)(1)
33.37.01.04 Definitions
   (a)   The definition for words contained in this Section will be construed
as being consistent with, supplementary, and additional to any definitions
contained in Article III, Chapter 33 of the Montgomery County Code.
   (b)   For the purpose of the Montgomery County Elected Officials' Plan
Regulations, the following words have the meanings indicated:
      (1)   Elected official. Means the sheriff, the state's attorney, and any
County official elected for a fixed term as specifically provided for in the
Charter.
      (2)   Elected officials' participant. Means a member who is participating
in the elected officials' plan.
      (3)   Elected officials' plan. Means the defined contribution plan that
the County establishes for elected officials.
      (4)   Member. Means an employee or official of the County government or a
participating agency or political subdivision who is contributing to the
retirement system.
      (5)   Retirement system. Means the employees' retirement system of the
County, as provided in Article III, Chapter 33 of the Montgomery County Code.
33.37.01.05 Eligibility
   (a)   An individual who was an elected official on December 1, 1986, and who
was a Group A employee prior to December 1, 1986, must continue to participate
in the retirement plan of the retirement system in which the individual
participated immediately prior to December 1, 1986, except that the individual
may choose to become an elected officials' participant at any time while an
elected official.
   (b)   An individual who was an elected official on December 1, 1986, and who
was not a member of a retirement plan of the retirement system on November 30,
1986, as a result of exercising the right described in Section 33-37(c) of the
Montgomery County Code, may elect to become an elected officials' participant
at any time while an elected official.
   (c)   An individual who was an elected official on December 1, 1986, and who
was not a Group A employee on November 30, 1986, must become an elected
officials participant on December 1, 1986, except that the individual may
choose to participate in another retirement plan of the retirement system in
which the elected official would otherwise be eligible to participate.
   (d)   An individual who becomes an elected official on or after December 2,
1986, but before December 1, 1989, must become an elected officials participant
on the date the individual becomes an elected official, except that the
individual may choose to participate in a retirement plan of the retirement
system in which the elected official would otherwise be eligible to
participate.
   (e)   An individual who becomes an elected official on or after December 1,
1989, must become an elected officials participant on the date the individual
becomes an elected officia1.
33.37.01.06 Election to Participate in Elected Officials Plan
   (a)   Informational Requirement
      (1)   An elected official who may elect to participate in the elected
officials' plan must fulfill an informational requirement before being eligible
to make the election.
      (2)   An elected official may fulfill the informational requirement by
participating in at least one of the following informational activities:
         (A)   Receipt and review of a written summary of the elected
officials' plan prepared by the Division of Employee Services, Office of
Personnel.
         (B)   Attendance at an interview with a representative of the Division
of Employee Services, Office of Personnel.
   (b)   Election
      (1)   An elected official who has met the requirement of subsection (a)
may elect to participate in the elected officials plan by filing the following
letter, or such other document which evidences the election and is signed by
the elected official, with the Division of Employee Services, Office of
Personnel:
         (FORM OF ELECTION TO PARTICIPATE IN ELECTED OFFICIALS' PLAN)
            Division of Employee Services
            Office of Personnel
            Executive Office Building
            101 Monroe Street
            Rockville, Maryland 20850
            Attn: ________________________
         (DATE)
            Dear ________________________:
            Pursuant to Section 33-37(5)(A) of the Montgomery County Code, I
hereby elect to become a participant of the Elected Officials' Plan of the
Employees' Retirement System as of __________________________.
         I hereby acknowledge that I have fulfilled the informational
requirement of Section 6(a)(1) of the Elected Officials' Plan Regulations by
participating in at least one of the following activities:
            1.    Receipt and review of a summary of the Elected Officials Plan
prepared by the Division of Employee Services, Office of Personnel.
            2.   Attendance at an interview with a representative of the
Division of Employee Services, Office of Personnel.
               _______________________________
               (Signature of Elected Official)
      (2)   An elected official may file the election to participate in the
elected officials plan at any time while an elected official.
33.37.01.07 Election to Participate in Another Retirement System Plan and
Decline Participation in Elected Officials Plan
   (a)   Informational Requirement
      (1)   An elected official who may decline participation in the elected
officials plan and elect to participate in the another retirement system plan
in which the elected official would otherwise be eligible to participate must
fulfill an informational requirement before being eligible to make the
election.
      (2)   An elected official may fulfill the informational requirement by
participating in at least one of the following informational activities:
         (A)   Receipt and review of a written summary of the elected officials
plan prepared by the Division of Employee Services, Office of Personnel.
         (B)   Attendance at an interview with a representative of the Division
of Employee Services, Office of Personnel.
   (b)   Election
      (1)   An elected official who has met the requirement of subsection (a)
may decline participation in the elected officials plan and elect to
participate in another retirement system plan for which the elected official is
otherwise eligible by filing the following letter, or such other document which
evidences the election and is signed by the elected official, with the Division
of Employee Services, Office of Personnel:
