cause the election to be void and the elected official must continue to
participate in the elected officials' plan as if no election had been filed.
         (A)   Elected officials who would otherwise become an elected
officials' participant pursuant to Section 33-37(4)(B) of the Montgomery County
Code must file such election before July 1, 1987.
         (B)   Elected officials who would otherwise become an elected
officials' participant pursuant to Section 33-37(4)(C) of the Montgomery County
Code must file such election before the date that is seven months from the date
the individual became an elected official.
      (3)   An election made pursuant to Section 7(b)* of these Regulations to
participate in another retirement system plan is irrevocable.
         *Editors note—see
33.37.01.07(b)
33.37.01.08 Severability
   (a)   If a court holds that part of this regulation is invalid, the
invalidity does not affect other parts.
(Administrative History: Reg. No. 24-87 (Method 3); Dept.: Human Resources;
Supersedes: Reg. No. 24-87E)
***** MONTGOMERY COUNTY CODE CHAPTER 33, ARTICLE III. EMPLOYEES RETIREMENT
SYSTEM, SEC. 33-60 THE BOARD OF INVESTMENT TRUSTEES POWERS AND DUTIES
REGULATIONS *****
COMCOR 33.60.01 Maintaining Indicia of Ownership of Plan Assets of the
Employees Retirement System
33.60.01.01 Purpose
Section 33-60(b)(6) of the Montgomery County Code ("Code") requires that the
Board of Investment Trustees (the "Board") maintain indicia of ownership of
assets of the Montgomery County Employees' Retirement System (the "Retirement
System") within the jurisdiction of the district courts of the United States,
except as authorized by executive regulation adopted using Method 3. The
executive regulation must be substantially equivalent to the federal
regulations under the Employees' Retirement Income Security Act of 1974
("ERISA"), as amended, on the same issue. This Regulation is promulgated to
provide exceptions to the rule set forth in Section 33-60(b)(6) of the Code for
the purpose of facilitating investments outside of the United States.
33.60.01.02 Definitions
For purposes of this regulation:
      (1)   The term "Bank" means a bank, as defined in Section 202(a)(2) of
the federal Investment Advisors Act of 1940, that has, as of the last day of
its most recent fiscal year, equity capital in excess of $1,000,000.
      (2)   The term "Broker/Dealer" means a broker or dealer registered under
the Securities Exchange Act of 1934.
      (3)   The term "depository" means any company, or agency or
instrumentality of government, that acts as a custodian of securities in
connection with a system for the central handling of securities whereby all
securities of a particular class or series or any issuer deposited within the
system are treated as fungible and may be transferred, loaned, or pledged by
bookkeeping entry without physical delivery of securities certificates.
      (4)   The term "Entity" includes any partnership, joint venture,
corporation, mutual company, joint-stock company, trust, estate, unincorporated
organization, association, or employee organization.
      (5)   The term "Insurance Company" means an insurance company which is
qualified under the laws of more than one State to manage, acquire, or dispose
of any asset of a plan, which the insurance company has, as of the last day of
its most recent fiscal year, net worth in excess of $1,000,000 and which is
subject to supervision and examination by the State authority having
supervision over insurance companies.
      (6)   The term "Investment Advisor" means an investment advisor
registered under the Investment Advisors Act of 1940 that has, as of the last
day of its most recent fiscal year, total client assets under its management
and control in excess of $50,000,000.
      (7)   The term "management and control" means the power to direct the
acquisition or disposition through purchase, sale, pledging, or other means.
      (8)   The term "State" means any state of the United States, the District
of Columbia, Puerto Rico, the Virgin Islands, American Samoa, Guam, Wake
Island, or the Canal Zone.
33.60.01.03 General Rule: Indicia of Ownership of Assets Must be Maintained
with Jurisdiction of the District Courts of the United States
The Board may not maintain the indicia of ownership of any assets of the
Retirement System outside the jurisdiction of the district courts of the United
States.
33.60.01.04 Exceptions to the General Rule
Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Board may maintain the indicia of ownership
of any assets of the Retirement System outside the jurisdiction of the district
courts of the United States if:
      (1)   Such assets are:
         (i)   securities issued by an Entity which is not organized under the
laws of the United States or any State and does not have its principal place of
business within the United States;
         (ii)   securities issued by a government other than the government of
the United States or of a State, or any political subdivision, agency or
instrumentality of such a government;
         (iii)   securities issued by an Entity, the principal trading market
for which securities is outside the jurisdiction of the district courts of the
United States; or
         (iv)    currency issued by a government other than the government of
the United States if such currency is maintained outside the jurisdiction of
the district courts of the United States solely as an incident to the purchase,
sale or maintenance ofl securities described in paragraph (1) of this section;
and
      (2)   (i)   Such assets are under the management and control of a
fiduciary which is a corporation or partnership organized under the laws of the
United States or a State, which fiduciary has its principal place of business
within the United States and which is:
            (A)    A Bank;
            (B)    An Insurance Company; or
            (C)    An Investment Advisor with either
               (1)   shareholders' or partners' equity in excess of $750,000 or
               (2)   all of its obligations and liabilities assumed or
guaranteed by a Bank, Insurance Company, an Investment Advisor with
shareholders' or partners' equity in excess of $750,000, or a Broker/Dealer
that has, as of the last day of its most recent fiscal year, net worth in
excess of $750,000; or
         (ii)    Such indicia of ownership of assets are either:
            (A)    In the physical possession of, or, as a result of normal
business operations, are in transit to the physical possession of, an Entity or
individual which is organize under the laws of the United States or a State,
which Entity or individual has its principal place of business in the United
States and which is:
               (1)   A Bank;
               (2)   A Broker/Dealer that has, as of the last day of its most
recent fiscal year, net worth in excess of $750,000; or
               (3)   A Broker/Dealer that has all of its obligations and
liabilities assumed or guaranteed by a Bank, Insurance Company, an Investment
Advisor with shareholders' or partners' equity in excess of $750,000, or a
Broker/Dealer that has, as of the last day of its most recent fiscal year, net
worth in excess of $750,000; or
            (B)   Maintained by a Broker/Dealer, described in paragraph (2)(ii)
(A)(2) or (3) of this section, in the custody of an Entity designated by the
Securities and Exchange Commission as a "satisfactory control location" with
respect to such broker or dealer pursuant to Rule 15c3-3 under the Securities
Exchange Act of 1934 provided that:
               (1)   Such Entity holds the indicia of ownership as agent for
the Broker/Dealer, and
               (2)   Such Broker/Dealer is liable to the plan to the same
extent it would be if it retained the physical possession of the indicia of
ownership pursuant to paragraph (2)(ii)(A) of this section; or
            (C)   Maintained by a Bank, in the custody of an Entity that is a
foreign securities depository; foreign clearing agency which acts as a
securities depository, or foreign bank which Entity is supervised or regulated
by a government agency or regulatory authority in the foreign jurisdiction
having authority over such depositories, clearing agencies or banks, provided
that:
               (1)   The foreign Entity holds the indicia of ownership as agent
for the Bank;
               (2)   The Bank is liable to the Retirement System to the same
extent it would be if it retained the physical possession of the indicia of
ownership within the United States;
               (3)   The indicia of ownership are not subject to any right,
charge, security interest, lien or claim of any kind in favor of the foreign
Entity except for their safe custody or administration;
               (4)   Beneficial ownership of the assets represented by the
indicia of ownership is freely transferable without the payment of money or
value other than for safe custody or administration; and
               (5)   Upon request by the Board, which is responsible for the
selection and retention of the Bank, the Bank identifies to the Board the name,
address and principal place of business of the foreign Entity which acts as
custodian for the Retirement System pursuant to this paragraph (2)(ii)(C), and
the name and address of the government agency or other regulatory authority
that supervises or regulates that foreign Entity.
33.60.01.05 Indicia of Ownership Maintained in Canada
Notwithstanding any requirement of Section III,* the Board may maintain in
Canada the indicia of ownership of plan assets which are attributable to a
contribution made on behalf of a Retirement System member who is a citizen or
resident of Canada, if such indicia of ownership must remain in Canada in order
for the Retirement System to qualify for and maintain tax exempt status under
the laws of Canada or to comply with other applicable laws of Canada or any
province of Canada.
   *Editors note—see
33.60.01.03
33.60.01.06 Effective date
This regulation is effective on September 30, 1992 .
(Administrative History: Reg. No. 63-92 (Method 3); Dept.: Finance)
***** MONTGOMERY COUNTY CODE CHAPTER 33, ARTICLE VI. DISABILITY BENEFITS, SEC.
33-86 APPLICABILITY REGULATIONS *****
COMCOR 33.86.01 Disability Benefits Program
33.86.01.01
   Editors note—This Regulation does not contain a Section 1.
33.86.01.02 Purpose
   (a)   The Montgomery County Disability Benefits Program Regulations are
established to provide uniform policies and guidelines for the administration
of the Disability Benefits Program. These Regulations are promulgated to assist
County employees and employees of participating agencies who participate in the
Disability Benefits Program, and to promote and implement efficient and
equitable practices consistent with Article VI, Chapter 33 of the Montgomery
County Code.
33.86.01.03 Funding
   (a)   The Executive Branch will establish a separate fund in which to
account for all financial transactions related to the administration of the
Disability Benefits Program. This fund will be accounted for on a basis
consistent with that of a self-insurance program.
33.86.01.04 Applicability
   (a)   County employees and employees of participating agencies will be
considered members of the Disability Benefits Program under Article VI, Chapter
33 of the Montgomery County Code if:
      (1)   they become members of the Montgomery County Employees' Retirement
System on or after May 15, 1986, or
      (2)   they are members of the Montgomery County Employees' Retirement
System before May 15, 1986 and have elected to become members of the Disability
Benefits Program by June 1, 1987.
   (b)   To be effective, election by a Montgomery County Employees' Retirement
System member to transfer from the Disability Retirement Program under Article
III, Chapter 33, to the Disability Benefits Program under Article VI, Chapter
33, must be made in writing and received by the Division of Employee Services,
Office of Personnel, no later than ninety (90) calendar days after approval of
these Regulations by the County Council.
   (c)   As required by Article VI, Chapter 33, the Chief Administrative
Officer or designee will conduct seminars for the purpose of informing
employees of the provisions of the Disability Benefits Program, the changes to
the Disability Retirement Program, and the option of changing programs
available to them. Written information on the available options will be
provided to each employee. In addition, individual counseling services may be
scheduled by the Division of Employee Services, Office of Personnel, within a
reasonable period of time upon request by an employee.
   (d)   Employees who are members of the Montgomery County Employees'
Retirement System prior to May 15, 1986, and who have not elected to become a
member of the Disability Benefits Program within ninety (90) calendar days
after approval of these Regulations by the County Council will be considered to
have elected to remain in the Disability Retirement System.
   (e)   An employee's election to transfer to the Disability Benefits Program
under Article VI of Chapter 33 is irrevocable.
33.86.01.05 Definitions
   (a)   The definitions for words contained in this Section will be construed
as being consistent with, supplementary, and additional to any definitions
contained in Article VI, Chapter 33 of the Montgomery County Code.
   (b)   For the purpose of the Montgomery County Disability Benefits Program
Regulations, the following words have the meanings indicated.
      (1)   Acceptable Level of Competence. Means an employee's performance of
the duties and responsibilities of the employee's position at a satisfactory or
equivalent rating level such as Met Requirements.
      (2)   Administrator. Means the entity which contracts with the County to
administer, as a third party administrator, the Disability Benefits Program
under Article VI, Chapter 33 of the Montgomery County Code.
      (3)   Alternative Placement. Means, under the provisions of the
Reasonable Accommodation Program (Administrative Procedure 4-22), the placement
of a disabled employee in another County position for which the employee is
qualified and for which an acceptable level of competence can reasonably be
expected.
      (4)   Compensable. Means, under the Workers' Compensation Program, an
accidental injury or occupational disease which meets the eligibility
requirements for payment of benefits.
      (5)   Cost of Living Adjustment (COLA). Means the annual adjustment made
to a member's disability benefits, based upon a percentage of the increase in
the Consumer Price Index for all Urban Consumers in the Washington D.C. Area.
      (6)   Credited or Creditable Service. Means the total number of years an
employee has been a member of the Montgomery County Employees' Retirement
System. Credited service, which is used to calculate disability benefits, also
includes the number of years which is earned under the Montgomery County Police
Relief and Retirement Fund, sick leave credits, service which is transferred,
and other credited service that is purchased by the employee for retirement
purposes. Credited service will also be used in calculating benefits when a
member reaches normal retirement date.
      (7)   Disability Leave. Means paid leave for a temporary total Disability
received as a result of an accidental injury or illness sustained directly in
the performance of duty as an employee when the injury or illness is deemed
compensable as provided by the Workers Compensation Law of the State of
Maryland.
      (8)   Employee. Means any individual employed by Montgomery County, or by
a participating agency or political subdivision, who actively participates in
the Montgomery County Employees' Retirement System.
      (9)   Final Earnings. Means for the purpose of calculating disability
benefits: (a) the highest regular salary of an employee for any consecutive 18
month period, less any shift pay differential; or (b) for an employee whose
salary has been reduced as a result of a disciplinary action, the regular
salary of the employee for the 18 month period immediately preceding the
disability.
      (10)   Long-Term Disability Insurance (LTD). Means an employee elected
group insurance benefit which provides an income replacement to full--time
employees who experience an illness or injury, whether work-related or not,
which prevents them from working for an extended period of time.
      (11)   Medical Re-Evaluation. Means a physical and/or mental examination
or series of examinations conducted subsequent to any initial examination to
determine whether a disability still exists or the extent of the disability has
changed.
      (12)   Member. Means an employee of the Montgomery County Government, or
of a participating agency, who is covered under and is actively participating
in the Montgomery County Employees' Retirement System, and (a) has elected to
participate in the Disability Benefits Program, or (b) has become a member of
the Montgomery County Employees' Retirement System on or after May 15, 1986.
      (13)   Non-Service Connected Disability. Means a condition of an employee
that is the natural and proximate result of an illness or injury unrelated to
the performance of duty as an employee which: (a) makes the employee incapable
of performing at prior capacity the duties and responsibilities of the position
performed prior to the illness or injury; (b) makes the employee unable to
engage in available employment commensurate with the employee's training,
education, and experience; (c) is not due to the willful negligence of the
employee; (d) is likely to be permanent; and (e) occurred subsequent to
enrollment in the Montgomery County Employees' Retirement System.
      (14)   Occupational Class. Means one or more positions which are
sufficiently similar as to type of work performed, difficulty and complexity of
duties, level of responsibility, and knowledge, skills and abilities required
to warrant the same classification assignment.
      (15)   Permanent Disability. Means a physical or mental incapacity of a
member which, based on medical and/or psychological evidence, is likely to
continue indefinitely.
      (16)   Position of Comparable Status. Means a position which is similar
in the level of responsibility and pay to the class assigned that was held by
the employee when the disability occurred.
      (17)    Prior Capacity. Means the average number of hours which the
employee worked and for which the employee was paid by the County immediately
prior to the occurrence of disability.
      (18)   Qualified. Means a determination that an employee meets the
minimum qualifications for a particular occupational class as well as any bona
fide position-specific requirements.
      (19)   Reasonable Accommodation. Means an effort made to make adjustments
for the impairment of an employee by structuring the job or the work
environment to allow that employee to perform the essential functions of the
employee's position. This effort may also include alternative placement of the
employee.
      (20)   Service Connected Disability. Means a condition of an employee
that is the natural and proximate result of an accidental injury which
occurred, an occupational disease incurred, or a condition aggravated while in
the performance of duty as an employee which: (a) makes the employee incapable
of performing at prior capacity the duties and responsibilities of the position
performed before the illness or injury; (b) makes the employee unable to engage
in available employment commensurate with the employee's training, education
and experience; (c) is not due to the willful negligence of the employee; and
(d) is likely to be permanent.
      (21)   Sick Leave. Means, for the purpose of these Regulations, earned,
paid leave granted to eligible employees for a period of absence due to illness
or injury, or that which is donated under the provisions of the Sick Leave
Donor Program.
      (22)   Social Security Disability. Means an income replacement program
provided by Federal Law.
      (23)   Temporary Disability. Means a physical or mental incapacity of a
member which, for the purpose of determining eligibility for benefits, cannot
be considered permanent based on medical and/or psychological evidence.
      (24)   Uniform Pay or Salary Plan. Means the general salary schedule
under which the member was covered at the time of disability determination.
      (25)   Willful Negligence. Means an intentional failure or reckless act
on the part of a member to exercise reasonable caution and care in the
performance of any function that could result in injury or illness.
      (26)   Workers' Compensation. Means a no-fault insurance program mandated
and governed by the State of Maryland to compensate workers for medical
expenses and lost earnings capacity resulting from an accidental injury on the
job or an occupational disease.
33.86.01.06 Application of Disability Benefits and Other Assistance Programs
   (a)    General
      (1)   As soon as possible after learning of the onset of an injury or
illness which may render an employee incapable of performing the duties and
responsibilities of the employee's position for a prolonged period of time, the
employee's department will advise the employee to seek guidance from the
Division of Employee Services, Office of Personnel.
      (2)   It is the responsibility of the employee to seek such assistance
promptly.
      (3)   If the employee fails or is unable to seek assistance from the
Division of Employee Services, Office of Personnel, the employee's department
or agency head may seek such assistance on behalf of the employee.
      (4)   Information may be obtained from the Division of Employee Services,
Office of Personnel, concerning the Disability Benefits Program, as well as
other benefit programs that may be available and for which the employee may be
eligible.
      (5)   Benefit programs for which an employee may apply include Workers'
Compensation and Disability Leave, Reasonable Accommodation/Alternative
Placement, Long-Term Disability Insurance, Social Security Disability, and the
Disability Benefits or Retirement Plan.
      (6)   Applications for County assistance programs will be processed
expeditiously. The County and the employee must cooperate to ensure that there
are no unnecessary delays.
   (b)   Workers' Compensation
      (1)   Workers' Compensation benefits are provided only to employees who
sustain accidental injuries or contract occupational diseases that arise out of
the course of employment.
      (2)   If an accidental injury or occupational illness is initially
determined by the Division of Risk Management, Finance Department/County Claims
Service to be compensable under the Workers' Compensation Law, the employee may
be placed on disability leave. Any sick leave used as a result of the injury or
illness prior to the determination may be recredited to the employee's leave
balance upon request of the employee's department. Disability leave will not be
granted if the disability is determined to be permanent.
      (3)   While on disability leave, the employee will be paid the difference
between the base County salary and the amount received under the Workers'
Compensation Law for the period of temporary disability.
      (4)   If an injury or illness is determined not to be compensable under
the Workers' Compensation Law, the employee may use accrued or donated sick
leave, annual leave, compensatory leave, or leave without pay in accordance
with established County leave procedures or in accordance with established
leave procedures of participating agencies.
      (5)   After the initial determination of compensability is made by Risk
Management/County Claims Service, a final determination is made by the State
Workers' Compensation Commission.
   (c)   Reasonable Accommodation/Alternative Placement (Employee Option)
      (1)   The Reasonable Accommodation Program (see Administrative Procedure
4-22) is a voluntary program which is available through the Office of Personnel
for employees who incur an injury or illness and who cannot, without some
modification of the job or work environment, perform the duties and
responsibilities of the employee's position.
      (2)   An employee is encouraged to pursue Reasonable Accommodation
instead of, or before, applying for benefits under the Disability Benefits
Program.
      (3)   Reasonable Accommodation is available also for employees who apply
for benefits under the Disability Benefits Program but who fail to meet
established eligibility requirements.
      (4)   The Office of Personnel may conduct alternative placement efforts
as part of the Reasonable Accommodation Program.
      (5)   The Reasonable Accommodation/Alternative Placement Program does not
apply to members of participating agencies.
   (d)   Long-Term Disability Insurance
      (1)   Long Term Disability insurance is a benefit provided to full-time
employees who participate in the County's group insurance program with six (6)
months active service who are disabled as determined by the County's insurance
carrier. A five (5) consecutive month waiting period from the date of injury or
onset of illness must be met prior to benefit commencement.
      (2)   An employee may qualify for long-term disability insurance benefits
whether or not an injury or illness is work related and whether or not the
employee is receiving other benefit assistance.
      (3)   Long Term Disability Benefits may be payable for a twelve (12)
month period after satisfaction of the five (5) month qualifying period
provided that the employee remains under the care of a physician and is unable
to perform his/her assigned duties and responsibilities.
         Beyond the first twelve (12) month period, the employee must remain
under the care of a physician and be totally disabled from any gainful
employment in order to continue to receive benefits.
         Benefits are not payable beyond twelve (12) months if the disability
is caused by mental illness or functional nervous disorder.
         Benefits may be reduced if other income is received.
   (e)    Social Security Disability Benefits
      (1)   In order to be eligible for Social Security disability benefits, an
employee must be mentally or physically disabled to the extent that the
employee is totally disabled from gainful employment.
      (2)   A disability must be expected to last at least twelve (12) months
or to result in death in order for benefits to be awarded. This determination
must be made by a qualified physician and must be approved by the State of
Maryland Department of Social Security Administration.
   (f)    Disability Benefits Program
      (1)   If an employee becomes ill or injured and is unable, as a result of
the illness or injury, to perform at an acceptable level of competence the
duties and responsibilities of his/her assigned position, the employee may make
application to the Division of Employee Services, Office of Personnel, for
benefits under the Disability Benefits Program.
      (2)   If an employee becomes disabled or incapacitated and is unable, as
a result of the illness or injury, to perform the duties and responsibilities
of the employee's assigned position, and has not made application for benefits
under the Disability Benefits Program, the Chief Administrative Officer or
designee or head of a participating agency must notify the employee that an
application for disability benefits should be made.
      (3)   The determination by the Chief Administrative Officer or designee
or head of a participating agency as to whether an employee should apply for
disability benefits will be made after the Chief Administrative Officer or
designee or head of a participating agency has reviewed the facts and
circumstances of the case and has consulted with the employee's department head
and/or supervisor and with the Division of Employee Services, Office of
Personnel.
      (4)   Upon receipt of notice to apply for disability benefits by the
Chief Administrative Officer or designee or head of a participating agency, the
employee will have seven (7) days within which to make an application for
disability benefits.
      (5)   If the Chief Administrative Officer or designee or head of a
participating agency notifies an employee that an application for disability
benefits should be made, and the employee fails to make application within
seven (7) calendar days, the Chief Administrative Officer or designee may
initiate an application on behalf of the employee and notify the employee
simultaneously.
33.86.01.07 Eligibility
   (a)    General
      (1)   Upon receipt of an application for disability benefits, the
Division of Employee Services, Office of Personnel, will review the application
to determine whether the applicant: (a) is a member of the Disability Benefits
Program, (b) meets credited service requirements where appropriate, and (c) is
not eligible for normal retirement.
      (2)   Eligibility requirements for benefits will be reviewed by the
Administrator before a determination of disability and any award of benefits
pursuant to the eligibility criteria in (b) below.
   (b)   Eligibility Criteria
      (1)   A member will be considered for service connected disability
benefits if the member is not eligible for normal retirement under the
Montgomery County Employees' Retirement System and the Administrator determines
that the injury or illness:
         (A)   is a natural and proximate result of an accident occurring, an
occupational disease incurred, or a condition aggravated while in the
performance of duty as a member;
         (B)   is likely to be permanent;
         (C)   is not due to the willful negligence of the member;
         (D)   makes the member incapable of performing the job that the member
performed prior to the injury or illness; and
         (E)   makes the member unable to engage in available employment
commensurate with the training, education, and experience of the member.
      (2)   A member will be considered for non-service connected disability
benefits if the member has five (5) years of credited service and is not
eligible for normal retirement under the Montgomery County Employees'
Retirement System and the Administrator determines that:
         (A)   the injury or illness was incurred other than in the performance
of duty as a member;
         (B)   the injury or illness is likely to be permanent;
         (C)   the member is not eligible for service connected disability
benefits;
         (D)   the injury or illness is not due to the willful negligence of
the member;
         (E)   the injury or illness makes the member incapable of performing
the job held at the time the injury or illness occurred;
         (F)   the injury or illness makes the member unable to engage in
available employment commensurate with the member's training, education and
experience; and
         (G)   the injury or illness occurred subsequent to enrollment in the
Montgomery County Employees' Retirement System. An injury or illness which
occurred prior to enrollment in the Montgomery County Employees' Retirement
System may be considered if the injury or illness has not affected the work
performance of the employee for five (5) consecutive years.
   (c)    Eligibility Assessment
      (1)   The member must provide to the Administrator, upon request, any
information or evidence available to the member, or within the member's
possession or control regarding the circumstances surrounding the occurrence of
an injury or illness.
      (2)   Upon request, the member must provide the Administrator with any
information or records regarding the member's training, education, and
experience.
      (3)   The member may be required by the Administrator to sign a written
release form to enable the Administrator to obtain medical information as
necessary.
      (4)   All special requests for additional information by the
Administrator must be provided to the member in writing. A copy of the written
request must also be forwarded by the Administrator to the Division of Employee
Services, Office of Personnel.
      (5)   The Administrator, with the concurrence of the Personnel Director
or designee, may terminate consideration of eligibility for disability benefits
if it is determined by the Administrator that the member has deliberately
falsified, withheld or failed to provide information requested by the
Administrator.
      (6)   Where the Administrator has terminated consideration of eligibility
as provided in subsection (c)(5) above, and where the member's department head
has determined that the member is not performing satisfactorily the duties and
responsibilities of the assigned position, the department may initiate
appropriate action including termination of employment as provided in the
Personnel Regulations. Such action may be appealed in accordance with the
Montgomery County Personnel Regulations, Administrative Procedure 4-4,
Grievance Procedure, or to the Merit System Protection Board as appropriate,
based on the action taken. Members of participating agencies will follow the
Grievance Procedure established for each participating agency.
      (7)   The medical findings and prognosis of the members treating
physician will be considered by the Administrator in determining eligibility
for disability benefits. Members may be required to submit to any other medical
and/or psychological testing and evaluations deemed necessary and appropriate
by the Administrator. The County will pay for other necessary medical tests.
      (8)   In instances where there is conflicting or inconclusive evidence as
to whether or not an injury or illness occurred in the performance of duty as
an employee, the Administrator may seek documentation as deemed necessary in
order to make a preliminary determination.
      (9)   The Administrator may waive the eligibility requirements in
subsections (b)(1)(B) and (b)(2)(B) above in situations where inconclusive or
conflicting medical evaluations are received, or under other extenuating
circumstances. The Administrator may approve benefits on a temporary basis for
one or subsequent one-year periods until it is determined that the disability
is permanent or no longer exists.
      (10)   In order to assess eligibility, training and experience gained
before and during employment with the County or a participating agency will be
considered by the Administrator in seeking other placement possibilities which
are commensurate with the training, education, and experience of the member.
      (11)   An available County position will be considered commensurate with
the member's training, education, and experience by the Administrator in
consultation with the Office of Personnel and the appropriate department, if
the job or the physical job environment can be reasonably restructured or
modified to accommodate the disabled member.
      (12)   In determining whether or not other available positions are
commensurate with a member's training, education, and experience, the
Administrator may consider positions at the same grade, or two grades above the
member's current grade.
      (13)   If, in determining eligibility for disability benefits, the
Administrator determines that another position is available, (whether or not
the position is in the member's department), the member may be placed in the
position on a non-competitive basis with the concurrence of the Chief
Administrative Officer.
      (14)   Upon making its decision with respect to eligibility for
disability benefits, the Administrator must inform the Personnel Director, the
member and the head of the participating agency, when applicable, in writing of
its decision to either award or deny benefits. If a decision has been made to
award benefits, the Administrator must specify the type and amount of benefit
which will be awarded. The written notice must specify the reasons for the
award or denial and must make specific reference to pertinent provisions of the
Montgomery County Code and/or the Disability Benefits Program Executive
Regulations.
33.86.01.08 Appeals
   (a)    Appeal to Administrator
      (1)   If the County or the member disagrees with the Administrator's
preliminary determination with respect to a claim for disability benefits, the
County, the member or the participating agency, where applicable, may request a
hearing before the Administrator.
      (2)   A hearing may be requested based on either the award or denial of
disability benefits.
      (3)   The decision rendered by the Administrator as a result of an appeal
must be made by a person(s) within the Administrator's organization other than
the same person(s) who rendered the preliminary determination.
      (4)   It is in the best interest of the County Government and the member
for hearings to be held as expeditiously as possible. The appeal process will
be conducted, therefore, in accordance with the time limits established below.
      (5)   A request for a hearing before the Administrator must be filed by
the County, the member, or the participating agency within fourteen (14)
calendar days following the receipt of notification of the Administrator's
preliminary determination. The request must be made in writing and must state
the specific reasons for disagreement with the Administrator's preliminary
determination and the relief requested. Requests for hearings filed later than
the required fourteen (14) days may not be considered. If no appeal is made,
the Administrator must provide a copy of the complete record to Division of
Employee Services, Office of Personnel, to be maintained in the employee/
member's file.
      (6)   Within seven (7) calendar days of receipt of the request for a
hearing, the Administrator must establish a hearing date on which the County,
the member, or the participating agency will present evidence and argument in
support of the appeal. The County or the member must be given at least twenty
(20) calendar days notice of the date set for the hearing.
      (7)   It is the responsibility of the Administrator to ensure the
impartiality of all hearings conducted.
      (8)   The Administrator must not consider any ex parte or private
communication from any persons, whether oral or written, which the
Administrator knows is, or reasonably may be, intended to unlawfully influence
the decision on the merits of an appeal.
      (9)   At the discretion of the Administrator, at any time before to the
hearing, any party or authorized representative may be allowed to review in the
Personnel Office the file compiled by the Administrator. A request to review
the file must be made by the employee or authorized representative fourteen
(14) days prior to the hearing date.
      (10)   It is the responsibility of the Administrator to inquire into the
facts and the law with regard to each issue presented as part of an appeal
filed.
      (11)   When an employee of the Administrator has any interest in a
decision which is, or reasonably may be, incompatible with, or in conflict with
any of his official duties or acts, the Administrator must publicly disclose
such interest. That employee must disqualify himself and not participate in the
decision or act affected unless, after disclosure, all interested parties
authorize the employee to continue in the appeal.
      (12)   The Administrator must notify the member of the member's right to
legal counsel at hearings scheduled as part of the appeal process.
      (13)   A complete record of hearings must be maintained by the
Administrator which will be used as the basis for subsequent reviews. Only
factual information and evidence offered and made part of the record of the
hearing will be considered in the determination of an appeal.
      (14)   Hearings will not be open to the public unless specifically
requested in advance in writing by either party and approved by the
Administrator.
      (15)   The Administrator will have the power to administer oaths and
examine all witnesses under oath in relation to any matter properly involved in
the hearing.
      (16)   The Administrator may require the attendance of witnesses and may
request documents under summons, subpoena or other process when considered
necessary for the proper administration and enforcement of the law and these
Regulations.
      (17)   Professional witnesses requested or required to be in attendance
by the Administrator will be reimbursed on a fee and expense basis in an amount
to be determined as usual and customary by the Administrator.
      (18)   Before rendering a decision concerning the appeal, the
Administrator must consider all written statements, oral testimony, medical
reports, and other evidence deemed appropriate.
      (19)   The Administrator must render a decision on the appeal (which will
either sustain, reverse, or modify the Administrators preliminary decision) no
later than fourteen (14) calendar days after the record is closed. The decision
will be presented in writing to the Personnel Director, to the member and to
the head of the participating agency, where applicable, and will provide
specific reasons for the decision. Where appropriate, specific references to
pertinent Montgomery County Code provisions, regulations, medical evidence or
other evidence on which the decision is based, must be provided by the
Administrator.
      (20)   The County or participating agency may have legal representation
present from the Office of the County Attorney for hearings conducted as part
of appeals filed to the Administrator.
      (21)   The County or participating agency will be responsible for the
payment of reasonable legal fees incurred by the member if: (1) the member
prevails in an appeal to the Administrator or (2) the County appeals the
preliminary determination by the Administrator and the member elects to have
legal representation present.
   (b)   Further Appeals
      (1)   The County or the member may appeal the final decision of the
Administrator to the Merit System Protection Board within fifteen (15) calendar
days from the date that written notification of the final decision of the
Administrator is received.
      (2)   The Administrator will provide the complete record, including the
transcript of the hearing, to the Merit System Protection Board and to the
Division of Employee Services, Office of Personnel.
      (3)   A member's position will be declared vacant upon a determination of
disability by the Administrator and will remain vacant during any appeal filed,
through the rendering of a decision by the Merit System Protection Board. If
the Chief Administrative Officer or head of a participating agency determines
that the position should be filled, authorization may be granted by the Chief
Administrative Officer to fill the position on a temporary basis, until the
appeal has been resolved.
      (4)   The decision of the Merit System Protection Board may be appealed
by the County or the member to a court of competent jurisdiction as provided in
the Maryland Rules of Procedure, Chapter 1100, Subtitle B.
      (5)   At any stage of the appeals process, should the member prevail,
disability benefits will be retroactive to the accrual date specified in
Section 8.(a)(1)* of these Regulations.
         *Editors note—see
33.86.01.08(a)(1)
33.86.01.09 Benefits
   (a)    Effective Date and Calculation
      (1)   Disability benefits will begin on the date that the member exhausts
all accrued and donated sick leave and compensatory leave in excess of eighty
(80) hours, or on the date that the application for disability benefits is
approved, whichever comes first.
      (2)   The annual amount of disability benefits for a service connected
disability will be calculated as follows:
      Two percent of final earnings multiplied by the number of years of
creditable service, up to thirty-six years, plus sick leave credits. Donated
leave may not be used for determining credited service for retirement. This
amount when calculated will not be less than sixty--six and two-thirds percent
of final earnings.
      (3)   The annual amount of disability benefits for a non-service
connected disability will be calculated as follows:
         Two percent of final earnings multiplied by the number of years of
creditable service, up to thirty-six years, plus sick leave credits. Donated
leave may not be used for determining credited service for retirement. This
amount when calculated will not be less than thirty-three and one-third percent
of final earnings.
      (4)   Benefits will be paid by the Administrator to all recipients on the
first day of each month. The Administrator may, with the approval of the
Personnel Director, change the day of the month on which the benefits will be
paid, upon the determination that such a change will benefit the Disability
Benefits Program as a whole.
      (5)   If there is any delay in beginning the payment of disability
benefits, the first payment will consist of the current monthly benefit, plus
any benefits which had accrued before the current month.
      (6)   A cost-of-living adjustment must be made annually to disability
benefit payments. The percentage adjustment will be equal to the annual
adjustment made to the Uniform Pay Plan for County employees or applicable
collective bargaining agreement. The effective date for the cost-of--living
adjustment will be the same effective date that is used for the adjustment to
the Uniform Pay Plan or applicable collective bargaining agreement.
   (b)   Benefit Reduction Schedule
      (1)   Disability benefits will be reviewed annually by the Administrator
and adjusted by the annual cost-of-living. Thereafter, disability benefits may
be reduced by the Administrator by income received by:
         (A)   The sum of wages earned and net earnings, minus net losses from
self-employment;
         (B)   Payments from other government group income maintenance
insurance coverage for the disability;
         (C)   Social Security Disability Benefits, including benefits payable
to dependents as a result of the disability;
         (D)   Any other government disability plan; and
         (E)   Workers' Compensation benefits.
      (2)    The amount of reduction will be determined as follows:
         (A)   The first $100 per month of income from a long-term disability
plan to which the member has contributed is exempt from reduction;
         (B)   The first $300 per month of income from employment is exempt
from reduction. If the salary of a member receiving non-service connected
benefits is equal to or greater than the salary the member may have received if
the original employment had not been interrupted, the first $300 per month of
income will not be exempt from reduction;
         (C)   Income from employment between $301 and $600 per month will
reduce disability payments at the rate of $1 in reduction for every $4 of
income;
         (D)   Income from employment above $600 per month will reduce
disability payments at the rate of $1 in reduction for every $2 in income;
         (E)   Income from (a) other government group income maintenance
insurance coverage, (b) Social Security, including benefits payable to
dependents on account of the disability, (c) any government disability plan,
and (d) Workers' Compensation will reduce disability payments at the rate of $1
in reduction for every $1 of income.
      (3)   Disability benefit recipients must notify the Administrator of any
income or change in income received from any of the sources above. In addition,
in order for the Administrator to determine the amount of reduction of
disability benefits, recipients must comply with requests by the Administrator
for information regarding income received from the sources listed above.
      (4)   Temporary disability benefits will be offset in accordance with the
reduction schedule listed above.
      (5)   If a member refuses to participate in retraining offered in
accordance with the Retraining and Employment Program and as specified in
Section 10* of these Regulations, disability benefits received by the member
will be reduced by one-half.
         *Editors note—see
33.86.01.10
      (6)   If a member refuses to accept one of two offers of employment under
the Retraining and Employment Program and as specified in Section 10* of these
Regulations, the amount that employment would have paid if accepted will be
offset from the disability benefits of the member in the same manner as income
from employment under subsection (b) above. The highest salary offered will be
that which is used in offsetting benefits.
         *Editors note—see
33.86.01.10
      (7)   If the employment offered by the County under the Retraining and
Employment Program as specified in Section 10* of these Regulations terminates
due to a voluntary separation by the employee or due to a loss of job through
disciplinary action, the member will continue to receive the amount of
disability benefits, which were offset by the income received from the
employment. If the employment offered by the County under the Retraining and
Employment Program terminates through no fault of the employee (e.g., layoff,
or physically or mentally unable to perform the job), the disability benefits
will be restored in accordance with Section 9** of these Regulations to
facilitate employment.
         *Editors note—see
33.86.01.10
         **Editors note—see
33.86.01.09
      (8)   Any reduction made to disability benefits will be effective sixty
(60) days after the Administrator receives notice of changes in the recipient's
income. Any reduction in benefits which accrues due to a delay in implementing
the reduction will be deducted from the recipient's next benefit payment. If
the accrued reduction is greater than the next benefit payment, the amount will
continue to be deducted from the recipient's subsequent payments. In cases of
severe hardship, the Administrator may modify the period for the repayment of
an accrued reduction.
      (9)   The County Executive will review the reduction formula by May 15,
1988, and recommend changes to the dollar amount of offsets to the County
Council in writing within ninety (90) days if revisions are deemed necessary to
accommodate changes in general income levels. Subsequent reviews will be made
every two (2) years thereafter.
   (c)   Re-evaluation and Termination of Benefits
      (1)   An eligible recipient will continue to receive disability benefits
unless the Administrator determines that the member has:
         (A)   recovered from the disability;
         (B)   failed to provide the Administrator with information that the
Administrator requires; or
         (C)   became eligible for normal retirement.
      (2)   The Administrator may require a member receiving benefits under the
Disability Benefits Program to undergo an annual medical examination during the
five (5) year period following the initial receipt of benefits, and once in
every subsequent three (3) year period until normal retirement date.
      (3)   When medical re-evaluations are required by the Administrator to
determine if a member's disability still exists or has changed, the County
Government will be responsible for costs associated with the medical re-
evaluations.
      (4)   If it is determined, after review of the medical evaluations, that
a member's medical condition has changed or no longer exists, the Administrator
may modify or discontinue benefit awards accordingly and initiate retraining as
appropriate. The Administrator may hold a hearing in order to make such a
determination.
      (5)   Should a member refuse to submit to examinations required by the
Administrator as part of the re-evaluation process, the Administrator may
reduce or discontinue benefits.
      (6)   A member will continue to receive disability benefits under the
Disability Benefits Program until the member becomes eligible for normal
retirement under the Montgomery County Employees' Retirement System. At that
time, the member will return to the Montgomery County Employees' Retirement
System and receive normal retirement benefits.
      (7)   Benefits for disability benefit recipients will be calculated at
normal retirement using the following formula:
         (A)   Two percent of current salary multiplied by years of credited
service up to a maximum of thirty-six years, plus sick leave credits. Years of
credited service of less than a full year will be prorated.
      (8)   During the period of time that elapses from when a member is
determined to be disabled to when the member is eligible for normal retirement,
the salary schedule that was in effect at the time of disability determination
may have changed. Therefore, the salary that the member held at the time of
disability determination, plus cost-of-living adjustments, will be considered
the member's current salary and will be used to calculate retirement benefits
when the member returns to the Montgomery County Employees' Retirement System.
Annual performance increments will be included in the calculation of current
salary, provided that the member's supervisor has certified that the member's
performance was satisfactory at the time of the injury or illness.
      (9)   Any changes in salary other than cost-of-living adjustments and
annual performance increments (reallocations, reclassifications, performance
awards) that the member may have received had the member continued original
employment, will not be considered in computing current salary as used in
calculating normal retirement benefits.
      (10)   For the purpose of calculating benefits at normal retirement date,
members who are receiving disability benefits, who are employed in the County
or in a participating agency, and who contribute to the Montgomery County
Employees' Retirement System will receive year-for-year credited service for
each full year of employment, regardless of whether the disability is
determined to be service or non-service connected.
      (11)   Members who are receiving disability benefits, who are employed
outside of the County and who are not contributing to the Montgomery County
Employees' Retirement System, will receive credited service for the purpose of
calculating benefits at normal retirement date, unless the member is covered
under another retirement plan which is considered by the Administrator to be
comparable to the Montgomery County Employees' Retirement System.
      (12)   For the purpose of calculating benefits at normal retirement date,
members who were determined by the Administrator to be disabled and
unemployable as a result of a service connected injury or illness, will receive
a year of credited service for each full year of receipt of benefits. Years of
credited service of less than a full year will be prorated.
      (13)   For the purpose of calculating benefits at normal retirement date,
members who were determined by the Administrator to be disabled and
unemployable as a result of a non-service connected injury or illness will
receive half a year of credited service for each full year of receipt of
benefits. Years of credited service of less than a full year will be prorated.
33.86.01.10 Retraining and Employment Program
   (a)    General
      (1)   It is the goal of the Retraining and Employment Program to return
disabled members to the workforce as soon as possible. Any employment offered
to such members must be commensurate with the training, education, experience,
and physical and mental capabilities of the member.
      (2)   The Administrator is responsible for maintaining the integrity of
the Retraining and Employment Program.
   (b)   Participation
      (1)   All members who receive disability benefits under the Disability
Benefits Program will participate in the Retraining and Employment Program
unless exempted by the the Chief Administrative Officer based on medical
evidence that would preclude successful completion of retraining.
      (2)   As specified in Section 9* of these Regulations, a member's
disability benefits will be reduced if the member refuses to participate in the
Retraining and Employment Program as determined by the Administrator.
         *Editors note—see
33.86.01.09
   (c)    Retraining
      (1)   The Administrator will evaluate each recipient of disability
benefits under the Disability Benefits Program to determine whether the member
is able to participate in retraining.
      (2)   The Administrator must take into consideration all pertinent
factors, including vocational, medical, and psychological, in making the
determination to recommend a program for retraining a member.
      (3)   The Administrator will make a written recommendation on the
member's ability to participate in retraining to the Office of Personnel within
thirty (30) calendar days of the determination of disability.
      (4)   If the member is determined by the Administrator to be incapable of
participating in retraining, due to the nature and extent of the disability,
the Administrator will provide an estimate, based on medical evidence, of the
anticipated date of recovery sufficient to restore ability to participate in a
retraining program.
      (5)   The Administrator will re-evaluate the medical status of all
disability benefit recipients under the Disability Benefits Program who are not
participating in retraining at least twice each year until such time as each
member is placed in a retraining program or is declared permanently
unemployable.
      (6)   If the Administrator recommends that the member participate in
retraining, the Administrator will, in coordination with the member and under
the direction of the Office of Personnel, develop an individualized program for
retraining.
      (7)   The Administrator will conduct a thorough vocational assessment in
order to develop an individualized retraining program for each participant.
      (8)   The Administrator must, whenever possible, identify at least two
options for retraining from which the member may choose only one.
      (9)   The retraining program as developed by the Administrator and the
member will use available community educational and training resources and will
be formulated to provide a marketable skill that will enable the member to
compete effectively for employment upon completion of the program.
      (10)   The retraining program for a member will not exceed two years,
except under unusual circumstances where the Chief Administrative Officer may
approve retraining beyond two years.
      (11)   The cost for each individual retraining program will not exceed an
amount considered reasonable as determined by the Administrator, subject to the
approval of the Chief Administrative Officer or designee.
      (12)   The Administrator will provide to the member and to the Office of
Personnel a comprehensive written plan for an individualized retraining program
for the member within thirty (30) calendar days of determination by the
Administrator that the member is able to participate in retraining.
      (13)   The member must respond in writing within five (5) calendar days
stating that the plan has been reviewed and agreed upon and that the member's
responsibilities under the program have been described and understood.
      (14)   The member and the institution used in the retraining program may
be required by the Administrator to provide information regarding the member's
participation in the retraining program.
      (15)   If the member who is participating in a retraining program is
determined by the Administrator to be physically or mentally unable to continue
in that program, the Administrator will consider alternative retraining options
for the member.
      (16)   The Administrator will provide to the Office of Personnel, on a
monthly basis, a status report for each member in retraining with
recommendations, if any, for modifications to the retraining plan for each
member.
   (d)   Employment
      (1)   Before the completion of retraining, the Administrator will begin
employment efforts for the member.
      (2)   If the member is determined by the Administrator to be employable
upon completion of the retraining program, the Administrator will commence
specific placement efforts.
      (3)   If the member is determined by the Administrator to be unemployable
after training, the Administrator will review the member's medical condition,
as well as the member's performance during training. Based on its findings, the
Administrator will make a recommendation for retraining or determination of
unemployability.
      (4)   When a member is determined to be ready for employment, whether or
not as a result of retraining, the Administrator will: (1) advise the member in
writing within seven (7) calendar days of the determination, and (2) notify the
member that the member is required to participate in the employment program.
The notification will advise the member that a maximum of two job offers will
be made and that refusal by the member to accept one of the job offers will
result in the termination of efforts to obtain employment for the member, and
reduction of the member's benefits as specified in Section 9* of these
Regulations.
         *Editors note—see
33.86.01.09
      (5)   At the same time, the Administrator will notify the Office of
Personnel in writing of the member's eligibility for employment. This
notification will include a current vocational assessment, as well as
certification as to the member's medical and psychological limitations and
capabilities. The Administrator also will identify potential classes of
positions for which the member may be eligible.
      (6)   The Administrator will conduct job searches concurrently inside and
outside the County Government. Priority will be given to placement within the
County Government.
      (7)   The Administrator will work closely with the Office of Personnel to
facilitate the identification of and placement into available positions within
the County Government.
      (8)   The member will be entitled to priority consideration for available
County Government positions at, or two grades above, the grade of the position
held by the member at the time the member was determined to be disabled.
      (9)   If, in considering a member for a specific position, either the
prospective employer or member raises questions regarding physical or medical
qualifications, such questions will be resolved through the use of the
employer's normal employment practices.
      (10)   If a member receives consideration for a position inside or
outside the County Government, and is then disqualified due to medical
limitations raised by the member or the prospective employer, the member will
not be considered to have refused a job offer.
      (11)   The Administrator will be responsible for initiating and
conducting an appropriate search of job vacancies outside the County Government
immediately upon determining that a member is ready for employment,
      (12)   Upon selection of the member for an appropriate position, the
Administrator will relay the offer of employment to the member. If the member
accepts an offer of employment with the County Government, the member must
forward a written statement of acceptance to the Administrator, who will advise
the Office of Personnel immediately, for notification to the selecting
official. In the case of employment offered outside of the County Government,
acceptance of the offer will be made in writing by the member and the
Administrator will notify the prospective employer.
      (13)   A member who accepts employment outside of the County Government
will have non-competitive reappointment rights in the County Government to a
job equal to or lower than the one held at the time of the determination of
disability. There will be no restriction on the time limit within which a
member may exercise these rights.
      (14)   If a member is offered and refuses any job, the Administrator will
attempt to secure the member's refusal in writing and will give the member the
opportunity to submit reasons for the refusal in writing. The Administrator
will review any reasons submitted by the member, will make a final
determination, and will provide the member with specific reasons as to whether
or not the offer of employment was commensurate with the training, education,
experience, and physical and mental capabilities of the member.
      (15)   If the member refuses a job within the County Government, the
refusal and reasons will be communicated to the Office of Personnel immediately
and the Office of Personnel will inform the selecting official.
      (16)   The Administrator will communicate the member's refusal and
reasons, as appropriate, to any outside employer.
      (17)   A member will be provided a maximum of two offers of employment
which are commensurate with the training, education, experience, and physical
and mental capabilities of the member.
      (18)   Upon a member's refusal of the second employment offer, the
Administrator will immediately notify the Office of Personnel of the member's
ineligibility for continuation in the employment program, and will provide the
Office of Personnel with documentation regarding the member's refusals.
      (19)   The Chief Administrative Officer or designee will review the
member's file and will advise the Administrator in writing within seven (7)
calendar days of a final decision on terminating the member's eligibility for
employment consideration.
      (20)   If the decision is to terminate the member's participation in the
employment program, the Office of Personnel will advise the member in writing
within seven (7) calendar days of the reduction of benefits under the
Disability Benefits Program.
      (21)   If the member has accepted a position under the employment
program, but is determined to be physically or mentally unable to perform the
duties within the first six (6) months of employment, or a period thereafter
not to exceed twelve (12) months based on medical documentation, the department
head or outside employer will notify the Administrator in writing of the
member's inability to perform the job duties. The Administrator will obtain and
certify any available medical documentation, as well as documentation of the
identified performance deficiencies, before making any adjustment in benefits.
      (22)   The Administrator will notify the member of the employer's notice
of deficiency and will allow the member seven (7) calendar days to respond in
writing. The member is required to cooperate with the Administrator in the same
manner as set forth in Section 7* of these Regulations.
         *Editors note—see
33.86.01.07
      (23)   The Administrator will issue a decision in writing to both the
employer and the member no later than fourteen (14) calendar days after receipt
of the members response to the notice of performance deficiency. The decision
will include the Administrators reasons for determining whether or not the
condition for which disability benefits were awarded is the cause of the
deficiencies.
      (24)   A member determined to be incapable of performing the duties and
responsibilities of the position due to the condition for which disability
benefits were awarded will be returned to the Disability Benefits Program as of
the date of the Administrators decision. A new assessment may be made, with
full entitlements to retraining and employment consideration as appropriate.
Any additional training which would exceed an aggregate of two years must be
approved by the Chief Administrative Officer.
      (25)   Benefits will be denied if the Administrator determines that the
performance deficiencies are not the result of the condition for which
disability benefits were awarded. Any further action to correct the
deficiencies or to remove the member from the position will be the
responsibility of the employer, subject to all regulations and legal
obligations without reference to the members previous participation in the
Disability Benefits Program.
      (26)   A members entitlement to employment consideration continues until
such time as the member: (1) recovers from the disability; (2) accepts a
position; (3) fails to accept one of the two job offers made; (4) is deemed
medically and/or psychologically unemployable; or (5) becomes eligible for
normal retirement under the Montgomery County Employees Retirement System.
(Administrative History: Reg. No. 13-86 (Method 1); Dept.: Human Resources)
