***** MONTGOMERY COUNTY CODE CHAPTER 33, ARTICLE VII. COUNTY COLLECTIVE
BARGAINING. SEC 33-103 LABOR RELATIONS ADMINISTRATOR — REGULATIONS *****
COMCOR 33.103.01 Collective Bargaining Regulation and Procedure
33.103.01.01 Prohibited Practices
      1.   (a)   A written charge of a prohibited practice must be filed with
the Labor Relations Administrator within 6 months of the incident giving rise
to the charge, or within 6 months of the date on which the charging party knew
or should have known of the matter that is the subject of the charge.
         (b)   A charge must contain the following:
            1.   The name, address, and telephone number of the person making
the charge (the charging party) and any representative of record;
            2.   The name, address, and telephone number of the person against
whom the charge is made (the charged party);
            3.   A clear and concise statement of the facts constituting the
prohibited practice, a statement of the sections of the Code alleged to have
been violated, the names and addresses of the individuals involved, and the
time and place of occurrence of the particular acts;
            4.   A statement that the alleged prohibited practice is not a
dispute that should be submitted under a negotiated grievance procedure or a
matter governed by the Law Enforcement Officers’ Bill of Rights, Article 27,
Sections 727-734D, Annotated Code of Maryland;* and
         * Editor’s note—Sections 3-101 through 3-113 of Title 3, Law
Enforcement, of the Public Safety Article of the Maryland Code.
            5.   The nature of the relief requested.
         (c)   The charge may be accompanied by supporting documents, including
copies of relevant correspondence, other written material, and settlement
proposals.
         (d)   A copy of the charge and any supporting documents must be mailed
simultaneously to the charged party and to the Personnel Director for
Montgomery County, or to the certified representatives, as appropriate.
      2,   (a)   The charged party must file an answer within 15 days of the
date of the charge except for good cause shown as determined by the Labor
Relations Administrator. The answer must contain the name, address, and
telephone number of any representative of record.
         (b)   The answer must specifically admit, deny, or explain each of the
allegations of the charge unless the charged party lacks sufficient knowledge
to do so, in which case the answer must so state. The answer must specifically
state whether the charge is a dispute that should be submitted under a
negotiated grievance procedure or is a matter governed by the Law Enforcement
Officers’ Bill of Rights.
         (c)   The answer may be accompanied by supporting documents, including
offers of settlement.
         (d)   A copy of the answer and any supporting documents must be mailed
to the charging party and any representative of record.
      3.   Upon the earlier of receipt of an answer to a charge or a period of
20 days from the date of the charge, the Labor Relations Administrator must
begin whatever independent investigation the Labor Relations Administrator
determines is necessary. The independent investigation may include, but is not
limited to, one or more of the following actions:
         (a)   Initiate fact-finding by investigation of documents and
interview of parties and witnesses.
         (b)   Appoint an investigator to carry out the independent
investigation under the direction of the Labor Relations Administrator.
         (c)   Engage the parties in an effort to settle the matter at issue.
      4.   If the charge has not been resolved within 10 days of receipt of the
answer or within 5 days of the date on which the answer was due if no timely
answer has been filed, the Labor Relations Administrator shall take one of the
following actions:
         (a)   Summarily dismiss charges which are insufficiently supported in
fact or in law to warrant a hearing, or
         (b)   Issue a notice of hearing.
      5.   Written notice of the hearing shall be given by certified mail or
personal service, to all parties not less than 30 days nor more than 60 days
before the hearing. The notice shall contain the following information:
         (a)   The time, place, and date of the hearing.
         (b)   That the parties may be represented by counsel or represent
themselves.
         (c)   That the parties have the opportunity to present and cross-
examine witnesses and present supporting documents.
         (d)   That the hearing is subject to the pre-hearing procedures in
Section 2A-7 of the Administrative Procedure Act.*
            *Editor’s note—Section 2A-7 of the Montgomery County Code
         (e)   That the parties may request a continuance of the hearing by
written request if made not less than 5 days before the date of the hearing.
         (f)   That a verbatim record and transcript of the hearing will be
made.
         (g)   That there is a right, subject to the provisions of the state
public information law, to inspect and copy at the expense of the requesting
party documents of any party, administrative authority, or investigating
governmental agency involved where such inspection is not otherwise prohibited
by law.
      6.   (a)   At any time prior to the hearing, the parties may submit to
the Labor Relations Administrator a stipulation of facts.
         (b)   The hearing will be conducted pursuant to the Administrative
Procedures Act contained in Section 2A-8 of the Montgomery County Code.
         (c)   The parties will have the opportunity to submit post-hearing
briefs within 15 days after the conclusion of the hearing, or such other time
as determined by the Labor Relations Administrator.
      7.   Where the ordinary processing of a charge would cause injury to any
party, due to time constraints, the Labor Relations Administrator may for good
cause grant an emergency hearing. Where an emergency hearing is ordered by the
Labor Relations Administrator, the Labor Relations Administrator may suspend or
alter any provision in these regulations or grant temporary injunctive relief
as necessary to avert undue injury. In such case, the Labor Relations
Administrator must notify all parties of the action taken and make every
reasonable effort to provide substantive due process of law to all parties.
      8.   (a)   All decisions of the Labor Relations Administrator except
rulings on preliminary matters or on motions or objections must be in writing,
based on evidence of record and must contain findings of fact, conclusions of
law, and an appropriate decision and order. However, any decision consented to
by the parties need only be reflected by a written order.
         (b)   All decisions must be based upon a preponderance of the evidence
in the record.
         (c)   All decisions should be issued within 45 days after the close of
the record. However, the Labor Relations Administrator may extend the time for
decision for an additional period upon written notice to all parties.
         (d)   All decisions must be sent simultaneously to all parties.
         (e)   Where rehearing or reconsideration is permitted by law, any
request for rehearing or reconsideration must be filed within 10 days from a
final decision. Thereafter a rehearing or reconsideration may be approved only
in the case of fraud, mistake or irregularity. Any request for rehearing or
reconsideration must be in writing, and must provide supporting reasons, with
copies served on all parties of record. Any decision on a request for rehearing
or reconsideration not granted within 10 days following receipt of the request
in accord with subsection (c) of this section will be deemed denied. Any
request for rehearing or reconsideration will stay the time for any
administrative appeal until the request is denied or in the event that the
request is granted such further time as a subsequent decision is issued. A
request for reconsideration or rehearing does not stay the operation of any
order unless the Labor Relations Administrator expressly provides otherwise.
         (f)   Where appropriate, informal disposition may be made of any
contested case by stipulation, agreed settlement, consent order, or default.
      9.   If the Labor Relations Administrator determines that the charged
party has committed a prohibited practice, the Labor Relations Administrator
may issue an order requiring the charged party to stop the prohibited practice.
The Labor Relations Administrator may take affirmative action to remedy the
violation, including reinstatement with or without back pay, making the
employee whole for any loss relating to County employment suffered as a result
of the prohibited practice, or withdrawing or suspending the authority of the
employee organization to negotiate or continue an agency shop provision or a
voluntary dues or service fee deduction provision.
      10.   Any party aggrieved by a final decision in a case governed by this
section may appeal the decision to the Circuit Court for Montgomery County,
Maryland, in accord with the provisions of the Maryland Rules governing
administrative appeals. The court has the power to affirm, reverse, or modify
the decision or remand the case for further proceedings as justice may require.
The filing of an appeal does not stay the order of the Labor Relations
Administrator. Any party to the proceeding in the Circuit Court may appeal the
Circuit Court decision to the appellate courts of Maryland pursuant to the
applicable provisions of the Maryland Rules.
33.103.01.02 Election Certification and Decertification Procedures
      1.   (a)   An employee organization must file a petition for
certification as the representative of a unit for the purpose of collective
bargaining with the Labor Relations Administrator.
         (b)   The petition must include the following:
            1.   The name and affiliation, if any, of the employee
organization, its address, telephone number, and a statement of its desire to
be certified;
            2.   The signature of the representative of the petitioner,
including the title and telephone number of the representative.
            3.   The uncoerced signatures of 30 percent of the employees within
the unit expressing their desire to be represented by the employee organization
for purposes of collective bargaining.
            4.   Name, address, and telephone number of the previously
certified representative, if any, the date of the certification, and the
expiration date of any applicable agreement, if known to the petitioner; and
            5.   Names, addresses, and telephone number of any other interested
employee organizations, if known to the petitioner.
         (c)   A copy of the petition, including a copy of the signatures of
the supporting employees on the petition, must be sent to the Personnel
Director for Montgomery County.
      2.   (a)   Once an employee organization has been certified, any petition
for decertification must be filed by an employee in the unit with the Labor
Relations Administrator.
         (b)   The petition must include the following:
            1.   The name, address, and telephone number of the employee;
            2.   The uncoerced signatures of 30 percent of the employees in the
unit alleging that the employee organization presently certified is no longer
the choice of the majority of the employees in the unit;
            3.   Name, address, and telephone number of the certified
representative, the date of the certification, and the expiration date of any
applicable agreement, if known to the petitioner; and
            4.   Name, address, and telephone number of any other interested
employee organization, if known to the petitioner.
         (c)   A copy of the petition, not including the names of the
supporting employees, must be sent to the Personnel Director for Montgomery
County and the certified representative.
      3.   (a)   If a lawful collective bargaining agreement is in effect, any
petition for certification or decertification may be filed between September 1
and September 30 of any year, but not sooner than 22 months after an election
has been held.
         (b)   If a lawful collective bargaining agreement is in effect, a
petition filed under this section must not be entertained unless it is filed
during September of the final year of the agreement.
      4.   Upon receipt of a copy of the petition for certification or for
decertification, the Personnel Director must furnish the Labor Relations
Administrator and all known interested parties with the following:
         (a)   Name, address, and telephone number of any employee organization
that represents the employees in the unit;
         (b)   A copy of all relevant correspondence;
         (c)   A copy of any existing or recently expired collective bargaining
agreement covering the unit described in the petition; and
         (d)   a current alphabetized list of employees included in the unit
together with their job classifications.
      5.   (a)   Upon the request of the Labor Relations Administrator, the
Personnel Director must post notices in places where notices are normally
posted affecting the employees in the unit.
         (b)   The notice must set forth:
            1.   The name of the petitioner;
            2.   The description of the unit; and
            3.   A statement that all interested parties are to give a written
statement to the Labor Relations Administrator expressing their views within 10
days after the notice is posted.
         (c)   The notice must remain posted for 10 days. The notice must be
posted conspicuously and not be covered by other material, altered, or defaced.
      6.   (a)   Any party challenging the validity of any petition must file a
challenge with the Labor Relations Administrator within 10 days after the
initial date of posting of the notice of the petition.
         (b)   The challenge must be supported with evidence including signed
statements of employees and any other written evidence.
         (c)   The Labor Relations Administrator must investigate the challenge
and then take appropriate action.
      7.   (a)   Any employee organization seeking to intervene in a proceeding
for certification must file a petition with the Labor Relations Administrator
within 10 days after the initial date of posting of the notice of petition.
         (b)   A petition to intervene must include the following:
            1.   The name and affiliation, if any, of the employee
organization, its address, telephone number, and a statement of its desire to
be certified;
            2.   The signature of the representative of the petitioner,
including the title and telephone number of the representative; and
            3.   The uncoerced signatures of 10 percent of the employees within
the unit signifying their desire to be represented by the employee organization
for purposes of collective bargaining.
         (c)   An incumbent certified representative will be considered an
intervenor in an election unless it files with the Labor Relations
Administrator a written disclaimer of any representation interest for the
employees in the unit.
      8.   All petitions will be considered filed when received by the Labor
Relations Administrator.
      9.   (a)   The Labor Relations Administrator must determine the adequacy
and validity of the signatures of the employees supporting a petition.
         (b)   If the Labor Relations Administrator determines that a petition
is properly supported and timely filed, an election will be held.
         (c)   At the direction of the Labor Relations Administrator all
interested parties must meet after the expiration of the 10 day posting period
and must use their best efforts to secure agreement on election procedures and
a date for the election. However, the election must not be held before 5 days
after the 10 day posting period expires, nor later than October 20 of any year.
      10.   (a)   All elections must be conducted under the supervision of the
Labor Relations Administrator and must be conducted by secret ballot at the
time and place that the Labor Relations Administrator directs. The Labor
Relations Administrator may select and retain the services of an agency of the
State of Maryland responsible for conducting labor elections, or a similarly
neutral body, to assist in conducting the election.
         (b)   The election ballots must contain, as choices to be made by the
voter, the names of the petitioning or certified employee organization, the
name of any intervenor, and a choice that the employee does not desire to be
represented by any of the named employee organizations.
         (c)   The employer and each party to the election may be represented
by observers selected in accordance with restrictions that the Labor Relations
may prescribe.
         (d)   Observers may challenge for good cause the eligibility of any
person to vote in the election. Challenged ballots must be impounded pending
either agreement of the parties as to the validity of the challenge or the
decision of the Labor Relations Administrator as to the validity of the
challenge. When the number of challenges is not determinative, the challenged
ballots must be destroyed.
         (e)   After the polls have been closed, the valid ballots cast must be
counted by the Labor Relations Administrator in the presence of the observers.
         (f)   The Labor Relations Administrator must immediately serve upon
the employer and each of the parties a report certifying the results of the
election. If an employee organization receives the votes of a majority of the
employees who voted, the Labor Relations Administrator must certify that
employee organization as the exclusive agent.
         (g)   If no employee organization receives the votes of a majority of
the employees who voted, the Labor Relations Administrator must not certify a
representative. Unless a majority of the employees who vote choose “no
representative”, a runoff election must be conducted. The runoff elections must
contain the names of the 2 employee organizations that received the largest and
second largest number of votes in the original election.
      11.   (a)   The certification of results by the Labor Relations
Administrator is final unless within 7 days after service of the report and
certification, any party serves on all other parties and files with the Labor
Relations Administrator objections to the election. Objections must be verified
and must contain a concise statement of facts constituting the grounds for the
objections. The Labor Relations Administrator must investigate the objections
and, if substantial factual issues exist, hold a hearing. Any such hearing
shall be conducted pursuant to paragraphs 5 through 7 of Section 1* of this
regulation.
            * Editor’s note—
33.103.01.01
         (b)   If no substantial factual issues are raised by the objection,
the Labor Relations Administrator may determine the matter without a hearing.
The Labor Relations Administrator may invite, either by rule or by invitation,
written or oral argument to assist in determining the merits.
         (c)   Within 10 days after the close of the record or within 10 days
after objections were filed, where no hearing has been held or arguments
submitted, the Labor Relations Administrator must issue a written finding that:
            1.   The election was conducted in substantial conformity with
Section 33-106* and the certification of results initially issued constitutes a
final decision, or
               * Editor’s note—Section 33-106 of the Montgomery County Code.
            2.   The election was not conducted in substantial conformity with
Section 33-106,* and order that another election be held.
               * Editor’s note—Section 33-106 of the Montgomery County Code.
33.103.01.03 Unit Determination and Objections
      1.   In the event a new class is created by the county, the Personnel
Director must place the class in one of three units or state that the class
falls within one of the exceptions to the definition of employee contained in
Section 33-102(4) of the Montgomery County Code. The Personnel Director must
act within 60 days of the date on which the class was created. Within 7 days of
this decision, the Personnel Director must serve copies of the decision on each
certified representative and publish the decision in the Montgomery County
Register.
      2,   In the event the duties and responsibilities of an existing class
are substantially changed, the Personnel Director must review the revised class
and place it is the same or a different unit, or state that the revised class
falls within one of the exceptions to the definition of employee contained in
Section 33-102(4) of the Montgomery County Code. The Personnel Director must
act within 60 days of the date on which the revisions to the class were
approved. Within 7 days of this decision, the Personnel Director must serve
copies of the decision of each certified representative and publish the
decision in the Montgomery County Register.
      3.   Any individual or certified representative disagreeing with the
decision of the Personnel Director may, within 10 days of publication, file
objections to the decision with the Labor Relations Administrator.
         (a)   These objections must contain the following:
            1.   The name, address, and telephone number of the person filing
the objection (the objecting party) and any representative of record,
            2.   The identity of the class and a copy of the decision of the
Personnel Director regarding that class,
            3.   A clear and concise statement of the basis for the objection,
and
            4.   The relief requested.
         (b)   The objection may be accompanied by supporting documents,
including copies of relevant correspondence.
         (c)   A copy of the objection and any supporting documentation must be
mailed simultaneously to the Personnel Director, and to any interested
certified representative.
      4.   Within 20 days from the receipt of an objection, the Labor Relations
Administrator must take one of the following actions:
         (a)   Summarily dismiss objections which are insufficiently supported
in fact or in law to warrant a hearing, or
         (b)   Issue a notice of hearing.
      5.   Any hearing must be conducted pursuant to Paragraph 5 through 7 of
33.103.01.01 of this regulation.
      6.   The Labor Relations Administrator must issue a decision on the
placement of the class. The decision must conform to paragraph 8 of
33.103.01.01 of this regulation and will be deemed a final decision.
      7.   Any individual or certified representative may make a written
request that the Personnel Director review a class if it is alleged that the
duties and responsibilities for the class have changed. If the Personnel
Director refuses to conduct the review, or fails to conduct the review within a
reasonable period of time, the individual or certified representative may file
an objection with Labor Relations Administrator, as provided in paragraphs 3
through 6 above.
(Administrative History: Reg. No. 43-93 (Method 1); Dept.: Personnel;
Supersedes Reg. No. 43-89)
***** MONTGOMERY COUNTY CODE CHAPTER 33, ARTICLE VIII. EMPLOYEES RETIREMENT
SAVINGS PLAN, SEC. 33-122 ADMINISTRATION REGULATIONS *****
COMCOR 33.122.01 Participation of Agencies in Retirement Savings Plan
Disability Benefits Plan and Severance Pay Plan
33.122.01.01 Purpose
1.0   To establish the conditions under which certain agencies may participate
in the Retirement Savings Plan, the Disability Benefits Plan and the Severance
Pay Plan.
33.122.01.02 Definitions
2.0   Adoption Agreements - The agreements required by Code Section 33-114(b)
(2) that must be executed by each agency to permit the participation of the
agency in the Retirement Savings Plan, Disability Benefits Plan, and Severance
Pay Plan. All adoption agreements must be executed in a form satisfactory to
the Chief Administrative Officer, and must be executed before the beginning of
the plan year during which the agency's participation will begin, except for
the first plan year.
   Board of Investment Trustees - The Board established under Article III,
Section 33-59, of the County Code, and vested under Article VIII, Section 33-
125, of the County Code with the powers and duties to manage the Retirement
Savings Plan trust fund.
   Disability Benefits Plan Participant - Any employee of the County who
participates in the Retirement Savings Plan, or any other employee who
participates in the Retirement Savings Plan and whose employing agency also
participates in the Disability Benefits Plan.
   Participating Agency - For the Retirement Savings Plan, any agency that has
executed an adoption agreement to participate in the Retirement Savings Plan
established in Division 1 of Article VIII in chapter 33 of the County Code and
whose participation has been approved by the Chief Administrative Officer. For
the Disability Benefits Plan, any agency that has executed an adoption
agreement to participate in the Retirement Savings Plan and the Disability
Benefits Plan, and whose participation has been approved by the Chief
Administrative Officer. For the Severance Pay Plan, any agency that has
executed an adoption agreement to participate in the Retirement Savings Plan
and the Severance Pay Plan, and whose participation has been approved by the
Chief Administrative Officer.
   Regular Earning - Gross pay for actual hours worked exclusive of overtime.
Gross pay must be used to determine benefits even if the County implements a
pick-up plan under Section 414 of the Internal Revenue Code. Gross pay must be
used to determine benefits even if a participant has agreed to a reduction of
earnings under:
      (a)    the County's deferred compensation plan under Section 457 of the
Internal Revenue Code; or
      (b)   any other benefit program sponsored by the County permitted by the
Internal Revenue Code.
   Retirement Savings Plan Participant - Any employee of the County or of a
participating agency who participates in the Retirement Savings Plan.
   Severance Pay Plan Participant - Any County employee who participates in the
Retirement Savings Plan, or any other employee who participates. in the
Retirement Savings Plan and whose employing agency also participates in the
Severance Pay Plan.
33.122.01.03 Submission of Information
3.0   Code Section 33-114(b)(2)(B) requires each participating agency to submit
any information and execute any form or document that the Chief Administrative
Officer deems prudent for purposes of maintaining the governmental or qualified
plan status of the Retirement Savings Plan within the meaning of the Internal
Revenue Code. The Chief Administrative Officer will make a formal written
request for any needed information. Each participating agency must respond
within 30 calendar days, unless the Chief Administrative Officer needs the
information on an expedited basis or unless the Chief Administrative Officer
grants an extension.
33.122.01.04 Notification
4.0   Code Section 33-114(b)(2)(C) requires each participating agency to notify
tile Chief Administrative Officer of its intent to adopt an employee benefit
plan before adopting any benefit plan which has an impact on the computation of
any benefit or any benefit limitation in any benefit plan. The participating
agency must notify the Chief Administrative Officer of its intent to adopt any
retirement plan at least 30 days before adoption.
33.122.01.05 Penalties
5.0   Code Section 33-114(b)(3) permits the Chief Administrative Officer to
treat a participating agency as having withdrawn from the Retirement Savings
Plan if the participating agency does not submit any information, does not
execute documents necessary to administer and maintain the plan as requested by
the Chief Administrative Officer, does not qualify as a participating agency,
or fails to adhere to the terms of the plan.
33.122.01.06 Retirement Savings Plan
6.0   Participant Contributions. Code Section 33-116(1) requires each
participating agency to deduct 3% of regular ear-nings that are less than or
equal to Social Security wage base and 6% of regular earnings that exceed the
Social Security wage base each plan year from each participant during each
payroll period. All participant contributions must be submitted directly to the
Board of Investment Trustees on a payroll basis. In no event may payroll
deductions be submitted less frequently than on a monthly basis. The method of
transfer of participant contributions from the participating agency to the
Retirement Savings Plan must be approved by the Board of Investment Trustees.
6.1   Employer Contributions.
   (a)   Code Section 33-117(a) requires each participating agency to
contribute to the Retirement Savings Plan in quarterly installments on behalf
of each agency employee who is a Group I or Group II participant. (Participant
Groups I and II are described in Section 33-115(b) of the County Code.) Each
participating agency must contribute an amount equal to 6% of each Group I
participant's regular earnings, and an amount equal to 10% of each Group II
participant's regular earnings. All employer contributions must be completed
each payroll period and submitted directly to the Board as soon as
administratively feasible. In no event may employer contributions be submitted
later than 5 business days after the end of each month. The method of transfer
of employer contributions from the participating agency to the Retirement
Savings Plan must be approved by the Board of Investment Trustees.
   (b)   Each quarter, the Board will report to the Chief Administrative
Officer the total forfeitures of employer contributions accumulated during that
quarter. The Chief Administrative Officer will consult with the Board as to
whether the forfeitures should be used for operating expenses or used to reduce
the County contributions. In no event will forfeitures be used to reduce County
contributions if all incurred operating expenses have not been paid. If
forfeitures are used to reduce employer contributions, the reduction of the
contribution will be allocated among the County and the participating agencies
on a per participant basis.
7.0   Payment of Operating Expenses. Code Section 33-122(c) requires a
participating agency to pay any amounts necessary to cover the agency's
respective contributions and operating expenses of the Retirement Savings Plan.
Participating agencies will contribute an amount specified by the Board which
will be used to pay their respective shares of the operating expenses of the
Retirement Savings Plan. The agency will submit the expense payment at the time
employer contributions are submitted, and the amount of the payment will be
based on a percentage of regular earnings of participating employees. The
percentage amount will be determined annually by the Board, and will be based
on expenses incurred. The percentage amount will not be an employer
contribution.
33.122.01.08 Disability Benefits Plan
8.0   An agency that adopts the Retirement Savings Plan is not required to
participate in the Disability Benefits Plan. However, if a participating agency
wishes to participate in the Disability Benefits Plan, it must sign an adoption
agreement as well as fund the benefits for its employees and pay its share of
the operating expenses. The allocation of operating expenses among the
participating agencies will vary depending on how many participants each agency
has participating in the disability benefits plan when compared to the
aggregate number of participants. The Chief Administrative Officer will bill
the participating agencies on a quarterly basis.
33.122.01.09 Severance Pay Plan
9.0   A participating agency that adopts the Retirement Savings Plan is not
required to adopt the Severance Pay Plan. Only agencies that use the Countys
payroll system may participate in the Severance Pay Plan and such agencies that
wish to participate in the Severance Pay Plan must sign adoption agreements.
Each agency will be required to fund the benefits for its employees and to pay
its share of administrative costs and operating expenses. The allocation of
operating expenses among the participating agencies will vary depending upon
how many participants each agency has participating in the Severance Pay Plan
when compare to the aggregate number of participants. The Chief Administrative
Officer will bill the participating agencies on a quarterly basis.
(Administrative History: Reg. No. 32-95 (Method 2); Dept.: Human Resources)
***** MONTGOMERY COUNTY CODE CHAPTER 33, ARTICLE VIII. EMPLOYEES RETIREMENT
SAVINGS PLAN, SEC. 33-132 TIME AND FORM OF PAYMENT REGULATIONS *****
COMCOR 33.132.01 Disability Benefits for Certain Retirement Savings Plan
Participants
33.132.01.01 Purpose
1.0   This regulation provides for a method of distribution for benefits
provided under the Disability Benefits Plan in Division 2 of Article VIII in
Chapter 33 of the County Code.
33.132.01.02 Definitions
2.0   Administrator - The Chief Administrative Officer. The Chief
Administrative Officer may contract with an entity to assist in the
administration of the Disability Benefits Plan.
   Participant - Any employee of the County or a participating agency who
satisfies the eligibility requirements of the Disability Benefits Plan.
   Participating Agency - Any agency that participates in the Retirement
Savings Plan, uses the County payroll system, elects to participate in the
Disability Benefits Plan, and whose participation is approved by the Chief
Administrative Officer.
33.132.01.03 Eligibility
3.0   An employee of the County or of a participating agency is eligible to
participate in the Disability Benefits Plan if the employee:
   (a)   is a participant in the Retirement Savings Plan under Division 1 of
Article VIII of Chapter 33 of the County Code;
   (b)   is regularly scheduled to work 20 or more hours per week; and
   (c)   incurs an initial non-service connected disability as defined in
Section 33-128(h) of the County Code, an initial service connected disability
as defined in Section 33-128(i), a continued non-service connected disability
as, defined in Section 33--128(b), a continued service connected disability for
a non-public safety employee as defined in Section 33-128(c), or a continued
service connected disability for a public safety employee as defined in Section
33-128(d).
33.132.01.04 Role of Administrator
4.0   Upon an application being filed by a participant, or by the Chief
Administrative Officer on behalf of a participant, the Administrator must
determine:
   (a)   if the participant is eligible to receive a benefit;
   (b)   the type of benefit (initial or continued, non-service connected or
service connected), if any, to which the participant is entitled;
   (c)   the amount of the benefit, if any, to which the participant is
entitled; and
   (d)   the effective date of the disability.
33.132.01.05 Effective Date of Disability
5.0   The effective date of the disability is the date immediately following
the first to occur of:
   (a)   the date the application is approved by the Administrator; or
   (b)   the date the participant exhausts all accrued sick leave and accrued
compensatory time in excess of a total of 80 hours.
   The Office of Human Resources must determine the date of the exhaustion of
the sick leave and compensatory time in excess of a total of 80 hours.
33.132.01.06 Commencement of Benefits
6.0   The designee of the Administrator will commence distribution payments
within 40 days after the last of the following events to occur:
   (a)   the date the participant exhausts all accrued sick leave and
compensatory time in excess of 80 hours;
   (b)   the date the disability determination is made; or
   (c)   the date the participant correctly completes all necessary
distribution forms to receive disability benefits.
33.132.01.07 Distribution of Benefits
7.0   All distributions will be made on a monthly basis retroactive to the
effective date determined under Section 5.0. The disability benefits must be
paid to the participant directly. All federal and state income taxes must be
withheld from the disability benefits paid. To the extent that federal and
state employment taxes apply, they must also be withheld.
33.132.01.08 Source of Funds
8.0   The County must pay the benefits under this plan from general assets of
the County or the participating agency. Assets of the Retirement Savings Plan
may not be used to pay benefits under this plan. No trust fund or custody
account may be established to pay the benefits under this plan. Any
participating agency must pay the costs of any benefits and any expenses
incurred due to the participation of its employees.
(Administrative History: Reg. No. 34-95 (Method 2); Dept.: Human Resources)
***** MONTGOMERY COUNTY CODE CHAPTER 33, ARTICLE VIII. EMPLOYEES RETIREMENT
SAVINGS PLAN, SEC. 33-140 PLAN ADMINISTRATION REGULATIONS *****
COMCOR 33.140.01 Severance Pay for Certain Participants in the Retirement
Savings Plan and the Guaranteed Retirement Income Plan
33.140.01.01 Purpose
1.0   The Severance Pay Plan will pay severance benefits to employees of
Montgomery County ("County") and certain employees of participating agencies
upon an employee's separation from service pursuant to the terms and conditions
of this plan.
33.140.01.02 Definitions
2.0   Final Earnings - The weekly rate of regular earnings of a participant as
of the last day of active service.
   Participant - Any employee of the County or a participating agency who
satisfies the eligibility requirements of the Severance Pay Plan.
   Participating Agency - Any agency that participates in the Retirement
Savings Plan and the Guaranteed Retirement Income Plan, uses the County payroll
system, elects to participate in the Severance Pay Plan, and whose
participation is approved by the Chief Administrative Officer.
   Regular Earnings - Gross pay for actual hours worked exclusive of overtime.
Gross pay must be used to determine benefits even if the County implements a
pick-up plan under Section 414 of the Internal Revenue Code. Gross pay must be
used to determine benefits even if a participant has agreed to a reduction of
earnings under:
      (a)   the County's deferred compensation plan under Section 457 of the
Internal Revenue Code; or
      (b)   any other benefit program sponsored by the County permitted by the
Internal Revenue Code.
   Separation from service or separated from service - The loss of a
participant's job through affirmative administrative action of the County or
the participating agency excluding dismissal for cause. Separation from service
does not include the voluntary decision by a participant to leave the service
of the County or the participating agency.
33.140.01.03 Eligibility
3.0   An employee of the County or of a participating agency is eligible to
participate in this plan upon the employee's separation from service if the
employee is then a participant in the Retirement Savings Plan or the Guaranteed
Retirement Income Plan under Division 1 of Article VIII of Chapter 33 of the
County Code.
33.140.01.04 Severance Benefits
4.0   Severance benefits will be paid as follows:
   0 to 1 years of service completed       no benefit
   over 1 to 5 years of service completed    6 weeks of the participants final
earnings
   over 5 to 7 years of service completed    8 weeks of the participants final
earnings
   over 7 to 9 years of service completed    10 weeks of the participants final
earnings
   over 9 years of service completed      12 weeks of the participants final
earnings
33.140.01.05 Distribution of Benefits
5.0   All benefits must be paid on a bi-weekly basis commencing after the
participant separates from service with the County or the participating agency.
The first payment will be made on the date that the participant would have
received payment of regular earnings had the participant not separated from
service. The severance benefits must be paid to the participant directly. All
federal and state income taxes must be withheld from the severance benefits
paid. To the extent that federal or state unemployment taxes apply, they must
be withheld from the severance benefits paid.
33.140.01.06 Source of Funds
6.0   The County must pay the benefits under this plan from general assets of
the County or the participating agency. Assets of the Retirement Savings Plan
or Guaranteed Retirement Income Plan may not be used to pay benefits under this
plan. Any participating agency must pay the costs of any benefits and any
expenses incurred due to the participation of its employees.
33.140.01.07 Appeals
7.0   An eligible County employee who is denied severance pay may appeal the
final decision of the Chief Administrative Officer by noting an appeal to the
Merit System Protection Board. All appeals must be in writing and must be filed
within 10 working days of the date on which the employee receives the decision.
The Merit System Protection Board may overturn the decision of the Chief
Administrative Officer only if the Board finds that the decision was arbitrary
and capricious.
(Administrative History: Reg. No. 16-09 (Method 2); Dept.: Human Resources;
Supersedes Reg. No. 33-95)
See also COMCOR
33.122.01 Participation of Agencies in Retirement Savings Plan Disability
Benefits Plan and Severance Pay Plan
CHAPTER 33B. PESTICIDES — REGULATIONS
COMCOR
33B.00.01   Pesticides
COMCOR 33B.00.01 Pesticides
33B.00.01.01 General Provisions
      A.   Authority. In accordance with the authority conferred under Chapter
33B, Section 33B-5, of the Montgomery County Code, 2024, as amended
(hereinafter referred to as the “Code”), the County Executive hereby
promulgates this regulation to implement County law pertaining to public
education and safety measures required of retail sellers of pesticides as set
forth in Chapter 33B of the Code.
      B.   Applicability. This regulation applies to all pesticide retailers
that are subject to Chapter 33B of the Code.
      C.   Definitions. The definitions of the terms used in this regulation
are provided in Chapter 33B, Section 33B-1, of the Code. For purposes of this
regulation, the following additional words and phrases will have the meaning
respectively ascribed to them in this regulation:
         Director of Environmental Protection - The Director of the Montgomery
County Department of Environmental Protection or the Director’s designee.
         Director of Health and Human Services - The Director of the Montgomery
County Department of Health and Human Services or the Director’s designee.
         Food Service Facility - Any enterprise that prepares or sells food or
drink for human consumption on or off the premises. Food service facility
includes any restaurant, coffee shop, retail market, cafeteria, short-order
café, luncheonette, tavern, sandwich stand, soda fountain; and any food service
facility in an industry, institution, hospital, club, school, church, catering
kitchen, or camp.
         Landscaped Environment - An area of land covered by a lawn or altered
from its natural state by a playground, mulched recreation area, or other
improvement that is subject to the pesticide use restrictions under Section
33B-10 of the Code.
         Non-bulk Pesticides - Any pesticide distributed, sold, offered for
sale, packaged, or repackaged in containers designed for less than 10 gallons
of liquid or less than 56 pounds of dry weight.
         Pesticide Producer Establishment - Any place assigned an establishment
number by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency where a pesticide or device
or active ingredient used in creating a pesticide is produced, or held, for
distribution or sale.
         Pesticide Retailer - A person that sells at retail non-bulk pesticides
or non-bulk quantities of a material that contains a pesticide.
         Properly Labeled - The written, printed, or graphic matter that
appears on or is attached to a pesticide, or its immediate container, and the
outside container or wrapper of any retail package of pesticide contains
sufficient instructions for use and caution to satisfy the requirements of
state and federal pesticide labeling laws.
         Waterbody Environment - Any area of land managed by the Parks
Department within 25 feet of a waterbody that is subject to the pesticide use
restrictions under Section 33B-14 of the Code.
33B.00.01.02 Display and Storage of Pesticides
      A.   A pesticide retailer must ensure that all pesticides, whenever
displayed or stored in a retail establishment, are physically separated from
food, medicine, beverages, or feed. The retailer must display or store the
pesticides across the aisle from any food, medicine, beverages, or feed or
place a solid, nonporous, physical barrier between those products and any
pesticide. The retailer must take other reasonable precautions if necessary to
prevent a pesticide from contaminating any product that is likely to be
ingested by a human or a domestic animal. Reasonable precautions may include
storing pesticide products in a locked container.
      B.   A pesticide display or storage area must contain only pesticide
containers that are properly labeled and are free of leaks, cracks, tears, or
open seams.
33B.00.01.03 Pesticide Spills
      A.   A pesticide retailer must promptly clean up any spilled pesticide
product upon discovery of the spill.
      B.   Disposal
         1.   A pesticide retailer must not dispose of a pesticide that escapes
from its container or packaging except in accordance with applicable state and
federal laws.
         2.   A pesticide retailer must not dispose of a pesticide by
discharging or dumping the pesticide or the pesticide container or packaging
into a sewer, ditch, lake, or any other area that may release the pesticide
into ground or surface waters.
      C.   Repackaging
         1.   A pesticide retailer may repackage a pesticide that escapes from
its container for return to the distributor of that product if:
            a.   the retailer has an agreement that provides for the return of
spilled pesticides; and
            b.   the procedures used by the retailer to prepare the product for
its return to the distributor comply with applicable state and federal laws.
         2.   A pesticide retailer must not repackage a pesticide for sale to
customers unless the retailer is registered with the U.S. Environmental
Protection Agency as a pesticide producer establishment.
33B.00.01.04 Inspections
      A.   The Director of Health and Human Services must routinely inspect
food service facilities for compliance with County pesticide laws in the
regular course of performing any food safety inspection required under Chapter
15 of the Code.
      B.   The Director of Environmental Protection must investigate each
complaint alleging a violation of County pesticide laws by a retailer other
than a food service facility and may conduct any other on-site visit necessary
to achieve compliance with the laws.
33B.00.01.05 Public Education
      A.   A pesticide retailer must make written materials on general
pesticide use and safety available to each purchaser of non-bulk pesticides at
each site where pesticides are available for purchase. Notice of the
availability of the written materials must be prominently displayed at those
sites in a conspicuous place as near to the point of sale as practicable.
      B.   Although the written materials displayed under this Section need not
be product- specific, the materials must:
         1.   be obtained from or have the prior approval of the Department of
Environmental Protection; and
         2.   include information that advises the general public about
opportunities for consumers to consider recommended alternative pest control
measures.
33B.00.01.06 Invasive Species - Landscaped Environments
      The following table lists invasive species designated by the Executive as
detrimental to a landscaped environment under Section 33B-5(c) of the Code. A
landscaped environment includes any area of land covered by a lawn or altered

improvement that is subject to the pesticide use restrictions under Section
33B-10 of the Code. A person may apply a registered pesticide to control these
designated species in a landscaped environment. Registered pesticides may only
be applied directly to these species when they are present, and must not be
used in anticipation of these species being present or applied to any area of a
landscaped environment where they are not present.
