***** ARTICLE I. IN GENERAL, SEC. 52-7 TAX ANTICIPATION CERTIFICATES FOR COUNTY
PROPERTY TAXES — REGULATIONS *****
COMCOR 52.07.01 Department of Finance
52.07.01.01 General
      In general, Section 52-7 of the Montgomery County Code, 1984, as amended,
provides for the County Executive to issue tax anticipation certificates for
County property taxes. The certificates may be issued in denominations of $50,
$100, $250 and $500. At no time in any fiscal year may the certificates issued
exceed 5% of County property taxes levied for the previous fiscal year. These
sections allow for the sale and issuance of the certificates at the discretion
of the County Executive at any County office or any State or National Bank in
the County. These certificates are not negotiable and do accrue interest. They
are transferable to the successor or assignee in ownership of the property for
which the certificate was purchased.
52.07.01.02 Definitions
      The following word, phrases and terms when used in connection with this
section shall have the following meanings:
         A.   "Director" means the Director of Finance of Montgomery County,
Maryland.
         B.   "Owner of Record of property" is the owner listed on the
assessment records of the State Department of Assessments and Taxation as of
the date of finality or semi-annual date of finality, if applicable.
         C.   "Parcel Identifier" is the District, Sub-District and Tax Account
Number of the property.
         D.   "Fiscal Year" means a 12 month period from July 1, through the
next succeeding June 30.
         E.   "Redeemed" as used in this regulation shall mean the act of
surrendering the tax anticipation certificate to the Division of Revenue to be
applied as payment against the real property tax bill. Interest shall be
calculated on the certificate and both the principal amount of the tax
anticipation certificate(s) as well as the accrued interest shall be deducted
from the total tax bill with any balance due on the tax bill being collected
from the taxpayer in the form of cash or check.
52.07.01.03 Eligibility Requirements
      Any owner of record of property in Montgomery County which is subject to
County property taxes may purchase a tax anticipation certificate under this
section. A tax certificate is not negotiable however, a tax certificate holder
may transfer the certificate to the successor or assignee in ownership of the
property for which the certificate was purchased.
52.07.01.04 Purchase of Certificates
      Certificates may be purchased at the Division of Revenue, Department of
Finance at 101 Monroe Street, Rockville, Maryland 20850 anytime during normal
business hours. They may also be purchased at any State or National Bank having
an office in the County that agrees to participate in the program and is so
designated by the Director. A list of participating banks will be maintained by
the Division of REvenue and provided to the public as requested. The Division
of Revenue shall include with the annual tax billing notice of participating
banks as well as a brief description of the program. Certificates may be
purchased in $50, $100, $250, and $500 denominations.
      At the time of purchase, the purchaser must provide the Division of
Revenue, or participating Bank the following information:
         A.   Name as listed in the property tax records
         B.   Current address including zip code
         C.   Social Security Number or taxpayer identification number
         D.   Certification in form required by the Division of Revenue that
the Social Security Number given is correct and that the taxpayer is not
subject to back-up withholding
         E.   Parcel Identifier of the real property
      The Division of Revenue must cease sale of tax anticipation certificates
at anytime that the total sales for a fiscal year are equal to 5% of the County
property tax levy for the previous fiscal year.
52.07.01.05 Transfer of Certificates
      A tax anticipation certificate is not negotiable. In the event that a
certificate holder transfers the property, the certificate holder may also
transfer the tax anticipation certificate to the successor or assignee in
ownership of the property for which the certificate was purchased. The transfer
must be registered at the Division of Revenue as follows:
         A.   The original certificate holder must surrender the certificate to
the Division of Revenue with the following information:
            (1)   The name, address and taxpayer identification number of the
transferee.
            (2)   The date of transfer for calculation of accrued interest.
            (3)   A certification from the transferee that the taxpayer
identification number provided is correct and that the transferee is not
subject to back-up withholding.
      The Division of Revenue will treat the surrendered certificate as
redeemed on their records, pay the original certificate holder the appropriate
amount of accrued interest earned on the certificate for the holding period
prior to the property transfer and issue a new certificate to the transferee.
52.07.01.06 Accrual of Interest
      Interest shall accrue on all tax anticipation certificates from the date
of issuance until the date of redemption. Interest shall be at the rate of four
percent (4%) per annum, non-compounding based on a 365 day year. The interest
earned on the tax anticipation certificates is taxable for income tax purposes,
therefore the County will prepare and distribute a from 1099INT to each
recipient in accordance with current Internal Revenue Service Regulations.
52.07.01.07 Loss of Tax Anticipation Certificates
      In the event that a taxpayer destroys or loses a tax anticipation
certificate, then the taxpayer must immediately notify the Division of Revenue
of the loss or destruction of the certificate. The certificate may be replaced
only upon the taxpayer providing the Division of Revenue an indemnity bond in
the form prescribed by the Division of Revenue approved by the County Attorney.
Any cost associated with the Indemnity Bond shall be borne by the taxpayer.
52.07.01.08 Legal Consequences
      The purchase of a tax anticipation certificate by a property owner is not
a payment of property tax but rather a mechanism whereby a taxpayer can
accumulate funds to be applied to the payment of the tax bill. The purchase of
a tax anticipation certificate by a property owner does not affect the time or
manner of a tax sale of the property for which the certificate is purchased if
the property tax is not paid as required by law. The purchase of a tax
anticipation certification does not affect or in any manner stay the
accumulation of interest and penalties on delinquent taxes.
52.07.01.09 Revision of Regulations
      These regulations are subject to revision as the need arises and as
approved by the County Executive for Montgomery County. Any revision to the
regulations must be made in accordance with Method (2) of Section 2A-15 of the
Montgomery County Code, 1984.
(Administrative History: Reg. No. 49-90 (Method 2); Dept.: Finance; Supersedes:
Reg. No. 33- 86AM)

***** ARTICLE I. IN GENERAL, SEC. 52-14 FUEL-ENERGY TAX — REGULATIONS *****
COMCOR 52.14.01 Fuel Energy Tax for Agricultural Producers
52.14.01.01 Purpose
      These regulations establish procedures for identification and
certification of agricultural producers within Montgomery County under Bill 34-
03 and 52-14 of the Montgomery County Code.
52.14.01.02 Definitions
      A.      “Certified Agricultural Producer” means a ratepayer that is
engaged in the business of agriculture in the production of an agricultural
commodity in Montgomery County. An agricultural commodity means livestock,
horses, poultry, field crops, including nursery stock, bulbs and flowers; and
other agricultural products having a domestic or foreign market.
52.14.01.03 Applications for Certification as an Agricultural Producer
      A.      Agricultural producers will apply for certification as follows:
      (1)      The Department of Economic Development will mail out a one-page
application to all of the owners of agriculturally assessed property (as
defined in § 8-209 of the Tax-Property Article of the Annotated Code of
Maryland) in the County to answer and then return.
      (2)      Any agricultural producer that does not own land in the County
(for example, a tenant farmer) will also be given an opportunity to apply and
return the application.
      (3)      The applicant will be asked to indicate from a list of items at
least one agricultural program and/or service that pertains to their farm.
52.14.01.04 Eligibility Criteria for Certification as an Agricultural Producer
      A.      In order to qualify as a Certified Agricultural Producer, an
applicant must be enrolled in at least one of the following Agricultural
Programs and/or Services:
            (1)      Any producer with property encumbered by the following
easement programs:
                  (a)      Agriculture Easement Program (AEP); or
                  (b)      Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation
(MALPF); or
                  (c)      Montgomery Rural Legacy Program (RLP); or
                  (d)      Maryland Environmental Trust (MET); or
                  (e)      Legacy Open Space (LOS).
            (2)      Any producer enrolled with the Montgomery Soil
Conservation District.
            (3)      Any producer enrolled in the Maryland Nutrient Management
Program.
            (4)      Any producer enrolled with the United States Department of
Agriculture and Farm Service Agency.
            (5)      Any producer enrolled with the Cooperative Extension
Service.
            (6)      Any producer enrolled as a member of the Montgomery County
Farmers Market Association.
            (7)      Any producer approved as a Certified Organic grower by the
Maryland Department of Agriculture.
            (8)      Any producer enrolled in a Forest Conservation Management
Agreement.
52.14.01.05 Verification that Agricultural Producers Meet the Eligibility
Criteria
      A.   The Department of Economic Development will verify to the Department
of Finance that the applicant meets one of the eligibility criteria listed in
Section 4, prior to approving the applicant’s Certification of Agricultural
Producer.
      B.   The Department of Economic Development will keep all applications
for each Certified Agricultural Producer and update the records bi-annually.
      C.   The Department of Economic Development will transmit a list of
Certified Agricultural Producers to the Department of Finance and the
Department of Finance will transmit this list of all Certified Agricultural
Producers to all of the fuel/energy suppliers in Montgomery County.
      D.   In the event the Department of Economic Development cannot determine
eligibility based upon enrollment in agricultural programs and services as
outlined in 42.14.01.04, A.1. through A.7., the Department will determine
eligibility based upon evidence of production provided by the applicant and
verified by the agricultural agencies identified in 52.14.01.04. For example, a
Schedule F (Profit and Loss from Farming) filed with the Internal Revenue
Service (IRS) would serve as evidence of production
(Administrative History: Reg. No. 33-03 (Method 2); Dept.: Finance.)
Editor’s note—2015 L.M.C., ch. 36, § 6, states, in part: Reference to the
Department of Economic Development in COMCOR 52.14.01 (Fuel Energy Tax for
Agricultural Producers) is a reference to the Department of Finance except that
reference to the Department of Economic Development in Section 52.14.01.05.A
(Verification that Agricultural Producers Meet the Eligibility Criteria) is a
reference to the Office of Agriculture.
2015 L.M.C., ch. 36, § 8, also states, in part: All other provisions of this
Act take effect 180 days after the Montgomery County Economic Development
Corporation is designated under Section 30B-2.
***** ARTICLE I. IN GENERAL, SEC. 52-18C RESIDENTIAL REAL PROPERTY TAX DEFERRAL
— GOVERNMENT-INITIATED REZONINGS — REGULATIONS *****
COMCOR 52.18C.01 Administrative Guidelines for Tax Deferral on Residential
Property Rezoned as a Result of Government-Initiated Change
** 52.18C.01.01 General **
      Section 52-18C of the Montgomery County Code, 1984, provides that a
portion of the County's annual real property tax levied on residential property
may be deferred. To qualify, the taxpayer must own and occupy, as his or her
principal place of residence, property that has been rezoned to a higher
intensity use as the result of a government initiated change.
      The amount of tax deferral is equal to that portion of the County's
annual real property tax levy on the residential property determined by
multiplying the taxable assessment attributable to the government-initiated
rezoning by the applicable tax rates. The tax deferral is a first lien on the
property until paid and is a personal liability of the owner of record.
Interest accrues on the annual tax deferrals at the rate specified in Section
14-603 of the Tax-Property Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland.
      Applications must be submitted to the Director of Finance no later than
September 1 of the first year in which the taxpayer wishes to participate in
the program. Once approved for deferral no further applications are required.
      Deferred taxes may accumulate as long as there is strict compliance with
the conditions set forth in 52.18C.01.04 herein. However, at no time may the
accumulated deferral, including accrued interest thereon, exceed 50% of the
current full cash value of the property or a lesser amount elected by the
taxpayer by written notice to the Director of Finance. Whenever these is
noncompliance with any of the conditions set forth in this Regulation, the
accumulated amounts so deferred become due and payable immediately.
** 52.18C.01.02 Definitions **
      The following words, phrases and terms when used in connection with this
requlation shall have the following meanings:
         A.   Residential Real Property - includes the taxpayer's principal
place of residence, as well as property owned by the taxpayer's adjacent to the
residence provided that it is unimproved and not assessed on the basis of
agricultural use. The total land area for which deferral is sought cannot
exceed ten acres.
         B.   Tax Year - is a 12 month period which begins July l and ends June
30.
         C.   Real Property Tax Deferral - is that portion of the County's
annual real property tax levy on the residential property determined by
multiplying the taxable assessment attributable to the government-initiated
rezoning by the applicable tax rates.
         D.   Current Full Cash Value - is the total value of the property as
determined by the State Department of Assessments and Taxation under the
Triennial Assessment System.
** 52.18C.01.03 Eligibility Requirements **
      To qualify for the tax deferral the following requirements must be met:
         A.   The property must be owned in fee simple by the taxpayer, and
         B.   The taxpayer must have occupied the property as his or her
principal place of residence for at least 24 months immediately prior to the
effective date of the zoning resolution for which the tax deferral is sought.
** 52.18C.01.04 When Tax Deferrals Become Due and Payable **
      When any one of the conditions listed below exist, the tax deferral
amount becomes due and payable with interest at the rate set forth in Section
14-603 of the Tax Property Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland.
         A.   The taxpayer ceases to occupy the property as his principal place
of residence.
         B.   The property becomes subject to tax sale.
         C.   The use of the property changes.
         D.   The taxpayer ceases to own the property in fee simple.
** 52.18C.01.05 Tax Deferral Computation **
      The amount of real property tax which may be deferred includes all taxes
levied by the County consisting of:
      (1)   General County tax:
      (2)   Washington Suburban Transit District tax:
      (3)   Fire District tax:
      (4)   Advance Land Acquisition tax
      (5)   Metropolitan District tax:
      (6)   Regional District tax:
      (7)   Recreation District tax;
      (8)   Washington Suburban Sanitary District tax:
      (9)   Storm Drainage District tax;
      (10)   Suburban District tax: and
      (11)   Urban District tax.
      Not subject to deferral are State, Municipal District, and Parking Lot
District taxes or special charges such as refuse charges and front foot benefit
charges.
      The following determinations are required to compute the deferred tax
amounts.
         A.   The taxable assessment of the property as rezoned.
         B.   The assessment increase resulting directly from the government-
initiated change in the zoning classification to a higher intensity use. In
calculating this increase, information supplied by the Supervisor of
Assessments shall be utilized to determine the taxable assessment had the
property retained its former zoning.
         C.   The total area of the real property for which deferral is sought.
         D.   The eligible tax rates applicable to the property.
         E.   The date of the zoning resolution.
      The amount of the tax deferral is determined by multiplying the
assessment increase attributable to the rezoning action as determined in B by
the tax rates identified in D.
** 52.18C.01.06 Processing Tax Deferrals **
      When applications are received by the Director of Finance, the Division
of Revenue will approve or deny the application and notify the applicant
accordingly. If approved, the Revenue Division will calculate the amount of the
tax deferral and a Deferred Tax Certificate will be issued. This certificate
must be returned at the time of payment of the non-deferred portion of the tax
bill. If the real property taxes have already been paid, the Director of
Finance shall refund, without interest, the amount of the tax deferral to the
taxpayer.
** 52.18C.01.07 Records **
      The Director of Finance shall maintain such records as necessary to
properly identify the real property accounts eligible for tax deferral, to
annually calculate the deferral, to accumulate the total deferral, and to
collect the tax deferral when due.
** 52.18C.01.08 Revision of Regulations **
      These regulations are subject to revision as the need arises and as
approved by the County Executive for Montgomery County. Any revision to the
regulations must be made in accordance with Method (2) of Section 2A-15 of the
Montgomery County Code, 1984.
   (Administrative History: Reg. No. 50-90 (Method 2); Dept.: Finance;
Supersedes: Reg. No. 34- 86AM)
***** ARTICLE I. IN GENERAL, SEC. 52-18F RESIDENTIAL REAL PROPERTY TAX REFERRAL
— GENERAL — REGULATIONS *****
COMCOR 52.18F.01 Residential Real Property Tax Deferral Program
** 52.18F.01.01 General **
      Section 52-18F of the Montgomery County Code 1984, as amended, provides
that for the taxable year beginning July 1, 1990 and thereafter, a property
owner may defer payment of a certain amount of Montgomery County property taxes
due on residential real property occupied by the owner as the owner's principal
residence if the owner meets the requirements of the Section. The amount of
taxes that may be deferred for any one year is the amount that County taxes due
exceeds the amount of County property taxes paid in the prior taxable year,
adjusted by any change in the Consumer Price Index. Interest accrues on the
deferred taxes at the rate of 9% per year.
** 52.18F.01.02 Definitions **
      For purposes of Section 52-18F of the Montgomery County Code, the
following terms have the meanings indicated:
         A.   Combined Gross Income means the combined gross income of all
owners and all individuals who reside in the dwelling, with the exception of
any individual who is considered a dependent under Section 152 of the Internal
Revenue Code or any individual paying reasonable fixed charges for rent or room
and board.
         B.   Gross Income means total income from all sources for the calendar
year immediately preceding the taxable year, whether or not included in the
definition of gross income for Federal or State tax purposes. Gross income
includes, but is not limited to, benefits under the Social Security or Railroad
Retirement Act, the aggregate of gifts in excess of $300, alimony, support
money, nontaxable strike benefits, public assistance received in cash grants,
pensions, annuities, unemployment insurance benefits, workmen's compensation
benefits, the net income received from a business, rental or other endeavor,
and any rent on the dwelling, including the rent from a room or apartment. A
loss from business, rental or other endeavors may not be used in the
determination of gross income. The term does not include any income tax refund
received from the State or the Federal Government.
      Editor’s note­This regulation does not contain a Sec. 3.
** 52.18F.01.04 Processing Applications **
      The Division of Revenue in the Department of Finance is responsible for
processing all applications received under this program. Upon receipt of an
application, the Division of Revenue will:
         A.   Review the application to determine that all parts of the
application have been completed and that required documentation has been
attached.
         B.   Calculate the amount of taxes that may be deferred based on the
information provided by the property owner.
         C.   Notify all mortgagees or beneficiaries under any deed of trust of
a tax payment deferral and of the amount of tax to be deferred.
         D.   Prepare an agreement to be signed by the property owner or owners
and the Director of Finance or his designee (Attachment B).
         E.   Record the Agreement in the land records of the County at the
expense of the property owner.
         F.   Refund, to the taxpayer, without interest, the amount of the
allowable tax deferral, if the full real estate tax, bill has already been
paid.
         G.   Include with the taxpayer's annual property tax bill the
cumulative amount of tax deferral and accrued interest.
** 52.18F.01.05 Effective Date **
      This regulation becomes effective 30 calendar days after the County
Council approves the Regulation or 90 calendar days after the Council receives
the Regulation if the Council takes no action within 60 days of receipt.
(Administrative History: Reg. No. 52-92 (Method 2); Dept.: Finance; Supersedes:
Reg. No. 55-90)

***** ARTICLE I. IN GENERAL, SEC. 52-18I (formerly § 52-18H) PROPERTY TAX
CREDIT — LEASED PROPERTY — RELIGIOUS ORGANIZATIONS — REGULATIONS *****
COMCOR 52.18I.01 Tax Credit for Property Leased by Religious Organizations
** 52.18I.01.01 General **
      Section 52-18H of the Montgomery County Code provides a credit against
County ad valorem property taxes, including special service area taxes, up to
the amount of property taxes imposed by the County, for that portion of
property that is leased, occupied, and used by a religious organization
exclusively for public religious worship, educational purposes, or office space
necessary to support or maintain public religious worship or educational
purposes, and for which the religious organization is contractually liable
under the lease agreement. The tax credit is available only if the owner and/or
lessor of the property reduces, by the amount of the tax credit, the amount of
the taxes for which the religious organization is contractually liable.
      Section 52-18H(b) provides that the tax credit may be granted beginning
with the tax year starting on July 1, 1995 and each tax year thereafter. In
order to obtain the tax credit, the owner of the property must apply for the
tax credit by the first day of April which precedes the tax year in which the
tax credit is used on forms prescribed by the Department of Finance.
      The Director of Finance through the Division of Revenue administers
Section 52-18H.
** 52.18I.01.02 Definitions **
      a)   "Educational Purposes" - means teaching, training or instructional
activities conducted by a religious organization for the benefit of the general
public or members of the religious organization in any area of learning.
Educational purposes does not mean day-care or child care activities or summer
camps or other recreational activities not exclusively educational in nature.
      b)   "Lease" - means a valid written agreement pursuant to which the
religious organization is the named lessee, and under which the religious
organization is liable for payment of the County ad valorem property taxes
applicable to that portion of the property leased by the religious
organization.
      c)   "Lessee" - means the religious organization to whom the property is
leased.
      d)   "Lessor" - means the person who has leased the property to a
religious organization. The lessor may also be the owner.
      e)   "Making of a Profit" - means the conduct of any activity on the
leased property by the religious organization or agent of the religious
organization, where the amount charged exceeds the cost incurred by the
religious organization of providing the goods, service or activity, and which
is not substantially related to the exercise or performance by the religious
organization of its religious or educational purpose. Fund raising activities
are not profit making. Subleasing, licensed use or third-party use of the
leased property for a charge is an activity for profit.
      f)   "Occupied" - means physical presence in and exclusive right of
possession of the leased property during the entire term of the lease.
      g)   "Office Space Necessary to Support or Maintain Public Religious
Worship or Educational Purposes" - means office space used exclusively for and
necessary to the support and maintenance of public religious worship or
educational purposes, not including a parsonage.
      h)   "Owner" - means the person with legal title to real property, which
is leased to a religious organization, and the person who is liable for the
taxes. The owner may or may not be the lessor under the lease with the
religious organization.
      i)   "Public Religious Worship" - means the exercise and performance of
any rite and ceremony engaged in by any religious denomination, church or sect,
which is open to the general public.
      j)   "Religious Organization" - means an organization that is certified
or qualified under Section 501(c)(3) or (d) of the United States Internal
Revenue Code.
      k)   "Use" - means actual and exclusive use by the religious
organization.
** 52.18I.01.03 Application Date **
      In order to be eligible for the tax credit, the owner must apply for the
tax credit each year by the first day of April which precedes July 1 of the tax
year in which the tax credit is to be used.
** 52.18I.01.04 Application and Approval Process **
      An application for the tax credit must be submitted to the Revenue
Division (Revenue) of the Department of Finance, on the forms prescribed by the
Department. The application must be signed by the owner and by the lessor, if
the lessor is not the owner of the real property, and by the religious
organization which is or will become the lessee. The application must be
accompanied by the following:
      a)   a copy of the executed lease;
      b)   a letter from the Internal Revenue Service indicating that the
religious organization is a tax- exempt organization under Section 501(c)(3) or
(d) of the United States Internal Revenue Code; and
      c)   any other supporting information, documentation or certifications
required by Revenue.
      Revenue must issue a voucher to the owner of the real property equal to
the amount of the tax credit determined to be due, and enter on the tax account
of the property the amount of the credit, the tax year to which the credit
applies, and the name of the religious organization leasing the property.
      The owner must return the voucher with the property tax bill along with
an affidavit signed by the owner and by the lessor, if the lessor is not the
owner, and the religious organization leasing the property, stating that the
amount of the taxes for which the religious organization was contractually
liable has been reduced by the amount of the tax credit shown on the voucher.
** 52.18I.01.05 Determination of the Tax Credit for a Lease of Less than the
Entire Property **
      If the religious organization leases, occupies and uses only a portion of
a property, then the amount of the tax credit is limited to the percentage of
the property that the religious organization leases, occupies and uses.
      If the religious organization's lease specifies that the property is
leased, occupied and used only on specified dates, days and times, then the
amount of the credit is a percentage of the tax for the entire taxable year
determined by dividing the number of days during which the property is leased,
occupied and used by the number of days during the taxable year.
** 52.18I.01.06 Duration of Tax Credit **
      The tax credit is granted for only one tax year and must be reapplied for
each year by the first day of April which precedes July 1 of the tax year in
which the tax credit is to be used.
** 52.18I.01.07 Termination of Tax Credit **
      Any tax credit granted for any tax year will terminate during that tax
year immediately upon the occurrence of any of the following events:
      a)   the religious organization no longer occupies the property;
      b)   the property is no longer exclusively used by the religious
organization for public religious worship, educational purposes, or office
space necessary to support or maintain public religious worship or educational
purposes;
      c)   the property is leased, occupied or used for the purpose of making a
profit;
      d)   the religious organization ceases to be contractually liable for
real property taxes on that portion of the property leased by the religious
organization.
      The religious organization, the owner, and the lessor, if the lessor is
not the owner, must immediately notify Revenue upon the occurrence of any of
these events.
** 52.18I.01.08 Tax Due Upon Termination of Tax Credit **
      Upon termination of the tax credit, Revenue must issue a bill for the tax
due. The tax due must equal the amount of the tax credit multiplied by the
percentage of the tax year during which the property was not eligible for the
tax credit.
      The tax is due and payable from the date of termination of the tax
credit. Interest and penalty accrues from the date of the termination of the
credit at the rates which are charged on overdue real property taxes.
** 52.18I.01.09 Severability **
      If a court holds that any part of this regulation is invalid, the
invalidity does not affect other parts.
** 52.18I.01.10 Effective Date **
      This regulation becomes effective upon approval of the County Council.
(Administrative History: Reg. No. 2-95 (Method 2); Dept.: Finance)
COMCOR 52.18M.01 Payment in Lieu of Taxes
** 52.18M.01.01 Information Required in a Request for a PILOT  **
      A property owner requesting a PILOT must submit the following information
to the Director of Housing and Community Affairs:
      A.   Property Information.
         1.   Street address of the property.
         2.   Legal description of the property or property tax account number.
      B.   Property owner information.
         1.   Name of property owner, or community housing development
organization, where applicable.
         2.   Legal status of property owner (individual, corporation, etc.),
including tax status (nonprofit or for profit) under state law.
         3.   Copy of document legally establishing property owner’s business
entity, if applicable.
         4.   Tax identification number.
      C.   Project information.
         1.   Total number of rental housing units on the property.
         2.   Total number of rental housing units that are considered to be
affordable as a result of financial support or regulation, in whole or in part,
by a public agency.
         3.   Length of time the affordable housing units will be subject to
rent restriction.
         4.   Description of the source or authority which requires that rent
restriction be applied to the affordable housing units.
         5.   Projected cash flow for the property for the length of the
proposed PILOT agreement.
         6.   Copy of the proposed regulatory agreement or other document that
establishes rent restrictions on the affordable housing units.
** 52.18M.01.02 Eligibility Criteria and Amount of PILOT Allowed **
      When authorized by state law and upon the recommendation of the Director
of Housing and Community Affairs, the Director of Finance may agree to accept a
negotiated payment in lieu of real property taxes (PILOT), including special
area taxes, that would otherwise be levied on a qualifying housing development.
The eligibility criteria to qualify for a PILOT, and the maximum amount of
PILOT that may be allowed are as follows:
      A.   Group homes.
         1.   The property owner must have nonprofit tax status under state
law.
         2.   The group home must be constructed or substantially rehabilitated
using public agency support as described in Section 7-503 or Section 7-505 of
the Tax-Property Article of the Maryland Annotated Code.
         3.   The group home must provide housing to special populations as
described in the section on group homes in the County Housing Policy, 2001 and
as amended.
         4.   The PILOT allowed for each affordable rental housing unit is an
amount equal to the average Montgomery County homeowner tax credit authorized
under Section 9-104 of the Tax-Property Article of the Maryland Annotated Code.
      B.   Affordable rental housing units owned or controlled by the Housing
Opportunities Commission.
         1.   The property must be owned by the Housing Opportunities
Commission or under the control of the Commission.
         2.   The PILOT may allow up to a 100 percent reduction of the real
property tax liability.
      C.   Rental housing with MPDUs.
         1.   The project must be for new housing that is subject to the
moderately priced dwelling unit program under Chapter 25A of the Montgomery
County Code.
         2.   The reduction allowed by the PILOT is the amount needed to make
the project financially feasible with the moderately priced dwelling units
provided onsite.
      D.   Rental housing with project-based Section 8 units.
         1.   The property must have project-based rental units developed under
the federal Department of Housing and Urban Development Section 8 program.
         2.   The original HUD contract for the project-based Section 8 housing
must have expired or be about to expire, and the property owner is voluntarily
renewing the contract.
         3.   The reduction allowed by the PILOT is equal to the financial loss
to the property owner created as a result of the property owner’s participation
in the Section 8 program.
      E.   Affordable elderly housing.
         1.   The affordable elderly housing must meet the requirements of
Section 7-502 or Section 7-503 of the Tax- Property Article the Maryland
Annotated Code.
         2.   The PILOT may allow up to a 100 percent reduction of the real
property tax liability.
      F.   Other rental housing.
         1.   The affordable rental housing must be constructed or
substantially rehabilitated using public agency support as described in Section
7-503, Section 7-505 or Section 7-506.1 of the Tax-Property Article of the
Maryland Annotated Code.
         2.   Except as allowed in Subsection 3, the PILOT allowed is: a) for
each affordable rental housing unit is equal to the average Montgomery County
homeowner tax credit authorized under Section 9-104 of the Tax-Property Article
of the Maryland Annotated Code; or b) the percentage reduction in real property
taxes allowed by the PILOT is 80 percent in the first through fifth years, 70
percent in the sixth year, 60 percent in the seventh year, 50 percent in the
eighth year, 40 percent in the ninth year, and 30 percent in the tenth year,
thereafter the PILOT expires.
         3.   The PILOT may allow up to a 100 percent reduction of the real
property tax liability for a property in which a HUD-designated community
housing development organization is the owner, developer, or sponsor of the
project.
** 52.18M.01.03 Severability **
      Each provision of these regulations is severable and if any provision,
clause, sentence, section, word, or part is held illegal, unconstitutional, or
inapplicable to any person or circumstance such illegality, invalidity,
unconstitutionality, or inapplicability will not affect or impair any of the
remaining provisions, clauses, sentences, sections, words, or parts of this
regulation or its application to other persons or circumstances.
** 52.18M.01.04 Effective Date **
      This regulation becomes effective 30 days after approval by the County
Council.
(Administrative History: Reg. No. 27-06 (Method 1) effective April 22, 2003;
Dept.: Housing and Community Affairs; Supersedes: Reg. No. 18-02AM, which
superseded Temp. Reg. No. 18-02T)
***** ARTICLE I. IN GENERAL, 52-18O HOME COMPUTER TELECOMMUTING INCENTIVE —
REGULATIONS *****
COMCOR 52.18O.01 Home Computer Telecommuting Incentive Personal Property
Business Tax Credit
52.18O.01.01 Purpose
   These regulations establish the procedure to determine and verify the tax
credit against the Montgomery County personal property tax under Bill 6-04 and
Section 52-18O of the Montgomery County Code.
52.18O.01.02 Definitions
      A.   “Telecommuting” means an employee who conducts regular business on
behalf of the employer but whose physical location when exercising such duties
is the employee’s residence instead of the employer’s place of business.
      B.   “Tax credit” means a non-transferable credit against the Montgomery
County personal property tax of the employer (Taxpayer).
      C.   “Tax credit amount” means that the tax credit may not exceed fifty
(50) percent of the cost of each new home computer or laptop, which the
aggregate tax credit allowed for each taxpayer in any tax year may not exceed
$2,000.
      D.   “Calendar year” means Tax Year and applies to the period July 1 -
June 30.
52.18O.01.03 Application
      •   The Taxpayer must submit an application on a form provided by the
Department of Finance, Division of Treasury at the address listed on page 1 of
this document*,
         *Editor’s note—255 Rockville Pike, Suite L-15, Rockville, MD 20850
      •   The Taxpayer must provide proof of purchase for the computer, and
document the date of purchase and cost of the new computer,
      •   The Taxpayer must provide the name and address of the telecommuting
employee for whom the computer was purchased,
      •   The Taxpayer must list the type of computer, name of the computer,
series, and serial number,
      •   The Taxpayer must certify that the computer will be used exclusively
for telecommuting purposes,
      •   The Taxpayer must certify that the telecommuting employee works no
less than thirty (30) percent at home for any tax year. This represents at
least 78 days for a full-time employee, and
      •   Failure to complete the application or provide supporting
documentation will result in denial of the tax credit application.
52.18O.01.04 Limitation
   The tax credit may either reduce or eliminate the personal property tax of
the Taxpayer. Therefore, any excess or “unused” tax credit in that tax year may
not be applied to any other tax year.
52.18O.01.05 Eligibility Requirements
      •   The telecommuting employee works no less than 30 percent at home for
the tax year,
      •   The computer must be purchased after December 31, 2005 to be eligible
for the tax credit,
      •   The computer must be used for telecommuting,
      •   The Taxpayer must apply for the tax credit within twelve (12) months
following the purchase of the new home computer or laptop, and
      •   The tax credit must be applied in either the tax year in which the
purchase occurred or the next tax year.
52.18O.01.06 Administration
   The Montgomery County Department of Finance (Department) will administer
this tax credit. The Department will allow for each tax credit in the order in
which the application for the tax credit is received by the Department. After
the funding limit is reached for that tax year, all credit applications are
automatically denied and are deemed ineligible. A credit application amount
that is in excess of the funding limit balance for that tax year will be denied
eligibility in its entirety and does not result in a partial credit amount.
52.18O.01.07 Funding Limit
   The funding limit of the tax credit allowed in each tax year must not
exceed:
      •   $100,000 in tax year 2006
      •   $175,000 in tax year 2007
      •   $250,000 in tax year 2008, and
      •   starting in tax year 2009, the Council must set future year funding
limits for this tax credit program. However, if no action is taken, the prior
tax year funding limit is assumed. For example, if no action is taken for tax
year 2009, the tax year 2008 funding limit applies.
52.18O.01.08 Reapplication of Tax Credit
   If a Taxpayer is denied a tax credit because the funding limit was reached
for that tax year, the Taxpayer must re-apply for the credit with the
Department if they want to receive a tax credit in the following tax year.
52.18O.01.09 Reporting
   The County Executive or designee must submit an annual report to the County
Council describing the cost of the program and number of telecommuting
employees under this tax credit. The report will be made available no later
than September 30th of each year.
(Administrative History: Reg. No. 8-06 (Method 2); Dept.: Finance)
***** MONTGOMERY COUNTY CODE CHAPTER 52, ARTICLE I. IN GENERAL, SEC. 52- 18T
DESIGN FOR LIFE TAX INCENTIVES – ACCESSIBILITY FEATURES — REGULATIONS *****
COMCOR 52.18T.01 Design for Life Tax Incentives – Accessibility Features
52.18T.01.01 Definitions
   The definitions in this section clarify the words and phrases used in
Sections 52-18T and 52-18U of the Montgomery County Code.
   “Accessible” means design of features described in Sections 52-18T and 52-
18U of the Montgomery County Code and meeting the clearances and specifications
provided to allow for movement with mobility aids.
   “Accessible bedroom” means a bedroom that may be accessed by an accessible
route.
   “Accessible circulation path” means an interior way of passage from one room
to another that can accommodate a wheelchair or other mobility aid.
   “Accessible door” means a primary accessibility entry door that provides a
clear width opening of 32 inches or more.
   “Accessible kitchen” means a kitchen that can accommodate a wheelchair or
other mobility aid and meets the specifications in Section 52-18T of the
Montgomery County Code for a usable kitchen.
   “Accessible route” means an interior or exterior circulation path at least
36 inches wide that provides a clear width of walking surface from a no step
building entrance to at least one usable powder room or bathroom and one other
room that can accommodate visitation. The accessible route shall extend from a
vehicular drop off or parking to a no step building entrance.
   “Agreement” means the School Impact Tax Credit Agreement between the
Department of Permitting Services and the property owner to construct or
contribute to the cost of building a single family residence that meets Level I
Accessibility Standard as defined in Section 52-18U(a) of the Montgomery County
Code.
   “Alternative design” means the use of designs, products, or technologies
such as an elevator, lift or stair glide unit as alternatives to those
prescribed, provided they result in substantially equivalent or greater
accessibility, usability or visitability.
   “Building entrance” means any entrance that allows passage to the visit-able
portion of the building (front door, back door, side door, deck or through the
garage door on an accessible route.)
   “Building permit” means any permit required by the Department, City of
Gaithersburg, or City of Rockville.
   “Date of submission of application” means the date that the application is
stamped in and accepted by the Department.
   “Existing residence” means an owner’s principal residence when an
accessibility feature is installed in a previously constructed one or two
family dwelling or an apartment/condominium unit in multi-family dwellings.
   “Department” means the Department of Permitting Services or its designee.
   “Full bathroom” means a bathroom that contains at least one sink, one
toilet, and a shower or tub which can accommodate a wheelchair or other
mobility aid and meets the specifications in Section 52-18T of the Montgomery
County Code for a bathroom on the accessible level.
   “Main living space” means the area of the residence that includes a room
that can accommodate visitation. (Minimum floor area should be 70 sq. ft.)
   “Owner’s Principal Residence” means the residence for which the “Occupancy”
box for the property’s real property tax bill reads “Principal Residence”.
   “Permanent Additions” include permanent modifications for accessibility
features to existing or new construction.
   “Reasonable costs to install the accessibility features or permanent
modifications” include any required permit or inspection fees.
   “Seller” includes a builder, developer, real estate agent, real estate
broker, or homeowner.
   “Sensory disability” means an impairment of one of the senses including
visual or hearing impairments.
   “Single family residence” includes one and two family dwellings, townhouses
and duplexes covered by IRC.
   “Usable powder room” means a room containing at least one sink and one
toilet and large enough to accommodate a clear space 2 feet 6 inches by 4 feet
within the room to position a wheelchair or other mobility aid clear of the
path of the door as it is closed.
   “Usable bathroom” means a room containing at least one sink, one toilet and
a shower or tub and large enough to accommodate a clear space 2 feet 6 inches
by 4 feet within the room to position a wheelchair or other mobility aid clear
of the path of the door as it is closed.
52.18T.01.02 Application for Tax Credit for Accessibility Features
   A.   An applicant for a property tax credit for accessibility features may
submit one tax credit application each tax year.
   B.   The following documents must be submitted with the tax credit
application:
      1.   Copy of the building permit which includes accessibility features;
      2.   Contracts, receipts, or invoices which demonstrate the cost or
amount of money spent on the purchase and installation of accessibility
features including any required permit or inspection fees; and
      3.   Other subsidies.
         (a)   Copies of applications for any other subsidy from governmental,
quasi-governmental, or non-profit entities providing tax credits or grants for
accessibility features and receipts for any subsidies received; or
         (b)   An affidavit that no other subsidies for accessibility features
have been received by the applicant or previous owner of the property.
   C.   Properties in the City of Rockville and City of Gaithersburg.
   In addition to the required documents in subsection B, applicants whose
properties are located in the City of Rockville or the City of Gaithersburg
must also submit a signed affidavit from the applicable City that all necessary
inspections have been completed and that the City verifies that the
accessibility features have been installed in accordance with the building
permit issued.
52.18T.01.03 Processing of Accessibility Features Building Permit Applications
   The Department will fast track the processing of all building permit
applications for accessibility features. The Department will review the
building permit application in accordance with procedures in effect at the time
of application.
52.18T.01.04 Certification of Tax Credit for Accessibility Features
   A.   The Department will review the application for Tax Credit for
Accessibility Features to verify:
      1.   That the accessibility features as shown on the building permit were
constructed in compliance with the Montgomery County Code and the Maryland
Accessibility Code. The Department shall prepare The Design for Life Guidelines
as an aid.
      2.   The amount of the credit requested is in compliance with Section 52-
18T of the Montgomery County Code;
      3.   Eligible costs were incurred within 12 months before the property
owner submitted the application;
      4.   Eligible costs were paid by the applicant and not, or will not be,
reimbursed by any entity;
      5.   Applicant is the homeowner as listed on Maryland State Tax
Assessment records; and
      6.   That the request for tax credit is less any subsidy received from a
governmental, quasi-governmental, or non-profit entity for the feature.
52.18T.01.05 Limits on Amounts of Credits Granted
   A.   The Department of Finance must keep a list of all credits granted
pursuant to Section 52-18T of the Montgomery County Code in the order in which
the Department certifies the credit. The certification date for a particular
property is the date when the Department completes its certification pursuant
to Section 51.18T.01.04.
   B.   If the total of all tax credits granted under Section 52-18T exceeds
$100,000, subsequent tax credits must be carried over to the next tax year.
(Administrative History: Reg. No. 3-14 (Method 2); Orig. Dept.: Permitting
Services)
See also COMCOR 52.18U.01 Design for Life Tax Incentives – Level I and Level II
Accessibility Standards
See also COMCOR 52.93.01 Development Impact Tax for Public School Improvements
– Credits; Purpose and Intent

Accessibility Standards

52.18U.01.02 Application for Tax Credit for Level I or Level II Accessibility
Standard
   A.   An applicant for a property tax credit for Level I or Level II
accessibility standard may submit one tax credit application each tax year.
   B.   The following documents must be submitted with the tax credit
application:
      1.   Copy of the building permit which includes accessibility features;
      2.   A copy of the Impact Tax Credit Certification Agreement for the
property;
      3.   Contracts, receipts, or invoices which demonstrate the cost or
amount of money spent on the purchase and installation of accessibility
features including any required permit or inspection fees; and
      4.   Other subsidies.
         (a)   Copies of applications for any other subsidy from governmental,
quasi-governmental, or non-profit entities providing tax credits or grants for
accessibility features and receipts for any subsidies received; or
         (b)   An affidavit that no other subsidies for accessibility features
have been received by the applicant or previous owner of the property.
   C.   Amended application.
   If the property does not receive a credit in accordance with the Agreement
and Section 52-93 of the Montgomery County Code, then the current property
owner may submit an amended application. The costs incurred may relate back to
the date of the building permit for the new single family residence even though
those costs were not incurred within 12 months prior to the filing of the
amended application.
52.18U.01.03 Processing of Level I and Level II Applications
   The Department will fast track the processing of all building permit
applications for accessibility features which will meet Level I or Level II
Accessibility Standard. The Department will review the building permit
application in accordance with procedures in effect at the time of application.
52.18U.01.04 Certification of Tax Credit for Level I or II Accessibility
Standards
   A.   The Department will review the application for Tax Credit for Level I
or Level II Accessibility Standards to verify:
      1.   That the accessibility features meeting Level I or Level II
Accessibility Standards, as shown on the building permit were constructed in
compliance with the Montgomery County Code and the Maryland Accessibility Code.
The Department shall prepare The Design for Life Guidelines as an aid.
      2.   The amount of the credit requested is in compliance with Section 52-
18U of the Montgomery County Code;
      2.   Eligible costs were incurred within 12 months before the property
owner submitted the application;
      3.   Eligible costs were paid by the applicant and not, or will not be,
reimbursed by any entity;
      4.   Applicant is the homeowner as listed on Maryland State Tax
Assessment records; and
      5.   That the request for tax credit is less any subsidy received from a
governmental, quasi-governmental, or non-profit entity for the feature.
52.18U.01.05 Design For Life Builder/Homeowner and Project Certification
Program
   A.   The Design For Life Builder/Homeowner and Project Certification Program
is a clearinghouse for architects, builders and developers who have achieved
the Level I and II Accessibility Standards certifications for property tax
credits and credits to Development Impact Taxes for School Improvements.
   B.   The Department will design, develop, administer and evaluate this
program in collaboration with its partners: Commission on People with
Disabilities; Maryland National Capital Building Industry; Montgomery County
Builders Association; National Association of The Remodeling Industry, Potomac
Valley Architect’s Association; Montgomery County Board of Realtors; Department
of Health and Human Services; and Department of Finance.
   C.   Certification. Architects, builders and projects may apply for
platinum, gold, silver or bronze certification based upon the number of units
or projects that have achieved Level I or II Accessibility Standards.
Participation in the certification program is voluntary.
      1.   Bronze - if at least 5% of the single family residences built in the
project meet Level I or Level II;
      2.   Silver - if at least 10% of the single family residences built in
the project meet Level I or Level II;
      3.   Gold - if at least 25% of the single family residences built in the
project meet Level I or Level II;
      4.   Platinum - if at least 30% of the single family residences built in
the project meet Level I or Level II.
   D.   The Department will recommend annual awards from the County Executive
and County Council to those persons or companies receiving bronze, silver,
gold, and platinum certifications.
52.18U.01.06 Limits on Amount of Credits Granted
   A.   The Department of Finance must keep a list of all credits granted
pursuant to Section 52-18U of the Montgomery County Code in the order in which
the Department certifies the credit. The certification date for a particular
property is the date when the Department completes its certification pursuant
to Section 51.18U.01.04.
   B.   If the total of all tax credits granted under Section 52-18T exceeds
$500,000, subsequent tax credits must be carried over to the next tax year.
(Administrative History: Reg. No. 3-14 (Method 2); Orig. Dept.: Permitting
Services)

***** MONTGOMERY COUNTY CODE CHAPTER 52, ARTICLE I. GENERAL, SEC. 52-24A
PAYMENTS IN LIEU OF TAXES FOR CERTAIN PROPERTY LEASED FROM WMATA – REGULATIONS
*****
COMCOR 52.24A.00 Payments in Lieu of Taxes for Certain Property Leased from
WMATA
52.24A.00.01 General Provisions
   a.   Authority. In accordance with the authority conferred under Chapter 52
Taxation, Article I, General of the Montgomery County Code, the County
Executive hereby promulgates this regulation to administer and implement the
Housing at Metrorail Stations Act (“Act”) in Montgomery County, Maryland.
   b.   Applicability. The Act requires the Director of Finance to negotiate a
PILOT for qualified development on Washington Metropolitan Area Transit
Authority (“WMATA”) property. The PILOT must exempt 100% of the real property
tax that would otherwise be levied for a period of 15 years but must not
include an exemption for any tax levied under an applicable special taxing area
law.
52.24A.00.02 Definitions
The definitions of terms used in this regulation are set out in Chapter 52,
Section 52-24A, of the County Code. For purposes of this regulation, the
following words and phrases have the following meanings unless the context
clearly indicated otherwise:
   a.   Area median income or “AMI” means the median household income for the
Washington, DC, metropolitan area as estimated by the U.S. Department of
Housing and Urban Development.
   b.   Covenant period means a period of 15 years during which each affordable
unit in the qualifying development must be maintained as affordable housing
under the requirements of Section 52-24A of the County Code and this
regulation.
   c.   Developer means a business entity that:
      1.   is in good standing with the State of Maryland;
      2.   leases land from WMATA at a metro station; and
      3.   builds, owns, or manages a qualifying development on the leased
land.
   d.   Property means one or more parcels of real property which contain a
qualifying development pursuant to Chapter 52-24A of the County Code.
52.24A.00.03 PILOT Agreement
For a developer to receive an abatement for property taxes on the leased
property, as calculated at 100% of the County’s real property tax due on the
leased property for a period of 15 years, a developer must enter into a PILOT
with the County. The PILOT must include the following requirements:
   a.   The developer must not use a contractor or subcontractor for any part
of the qualifying development if they have three (3) or more final penalties
totaling at least $5,000 each, for violations of applicable wage and hour laws
over the past three (3) years.
   b.   The developer must ensure that 25% of the workers constructing the
qualifying development are residents of Montgomery County.
   c.   The property must contain a qualifying development pursuant to 52-24A
of the County Code.
   d.   The qualifying development must be more than 8 stories above ground and
located on land owned by WMATA and leased to the developer by WMATA.
   e.   At least 50% of the square footage of the qualifying development must
consist of residential apartment units located in high rise residential
apartment buildings.
   f.   At least 25% of the qualifying development’s Moderately Priced Dwelling
Units (“MPDUs”) required under Chapter 25A of the County Code must be
maintained and rented to persons or households whose income is not more than
50% of the area median income (“AMI”).
   g.   The developer must execute, and the County must record among the land
records, a covenant to maintain the affordable housing required under Section
52-24A of the County Code and these regulations which runs with the land for 15
years from the date that the qualifying development receives a use and
occupancy permit for residential units. If the use and occupancy permit is
issued on a per building or per floor basis, separate covenants will be
recorded to accurately reflect the commencement date of the covenants. At the
Director’s discretion, the affordable housing covenant required under this
subsection g. may be included as part of the MPDU covenant required under
Chapter 25A; however, nothing in Section 52-24A or these regulations alters the
MPDU requirements and procedures under Chapter 25A of the County Code.
   h.   The developer must notify the Director of the addition, sale, transfer,
assignments, or other termination of the property as a qualifying development
not less than thirty (30) days prior to the effective date of any such event.
   i.   The developer must provide annually verified compliance certificates on
a form approved by the Director, and supporting documentation, to the Director
every year during the covenant period. Supporting documentation includes: (i)
rent rolls, (ii) household income certifications, (iii) financial audits, and
(iv) any other documentation that the director deems necessary to ensure the
developer’s compliance with Section 52-24A of the County Code and this
regulation.
   j.   The developer must permit the County to examine its books and records
upon reasonable notice and during normal business hours. The developer must
retain its books and records for a period of five (5) years after the
expiration of the covenant period.
   k.   The developer must comply in all respects with the provisions of
Section 7-501 of the Tax-Property Article and Section 52-24A of the County
Code.
52.24A.00.04 Compliance Reporting
   a.   Quarterly Developer Compliance Report. From the commencement of
construction and until the issuance of a certificate of occupancy, the
developer will submit to the County, on a calendar quarter basis or any
applicable portion thereof, certified payroll reports for all contractors and
subcontractors on the qualifying development. The certified payroll reports
must list, for each employee on the qualifying development’s payroll: a unique
employee/position identifier number; the employee’s initials; annual salary or
hourly rate, as applicable; and zip code of residence. The general contractor
must certify as to the accuracy of the information provided.
   b.   Annual Company PILOT Certification. For the duration of the PILOT
Agreement, the developer must provide an annual certification to the Director,
signed by an appropriately authorized officer of the company, certifying that:
      1.   a minimum of 50% of the leasable square footage of the qualifying
development consists of high-rise residential apartment units; and
      2.   at least 25% of the qualifying development’s MPDUs required under
Chapter 25A of the County Code are maintained or rented to persons or
households at 50% of the AMI.
   c.   Repayment of Unpaid Taxes. If during the term of the PILOT the
developer, or its successor or assign, fails to comply with the provisions of
the PILOT, this regulation, or Section 52-24A of the County Code at any point
during a tax levy year: upon the County’s demand, the developer must
immediately repay to the County the amount of any and all taxes, plus
applicable interest for unpaid property tax and penalties, which would have
been otherwise due and payable on the property for that tax levy year but for
this PILOT Agreement.
The annual certification must be received by January 31 of each year following
the calendar year being certified. The annual certification should be sent to:
Michael J. Coveyou, Director
Montgomery County Department of Finance
101 Monroe Street, 15th Floor
Rockville, Maryland 20850
52.24A.00.05 Severability
If a court holds that a portion of this regulation is invalid, the other
portions remain in effect.
52.24A.00.06 Effective Date
This regulation must be submitted to the Council and takes effect upon approval
by the County Council.
(Administrative History: Reg. No. 6-21 (Method 1); Orig. Dept.: Finance)
***** ARTICLE VI. HISTORIC PRESERVATION TAX CREDIT, SEC. 52-41 TAX CREDIT
GENERALLY — REGULATIONS *****
COMCOR 52.41.01 Administrative Guidelines for Real Property Historic
Preservation Tax Credit
52.41.01.01 General 
      Sections 52-41 through Sections 52-45 of the Montgomery County Code 1984,
provide for a tax credit against County Real Property Taxes based upon the
amount expended by a taxpayer for restoration and preservation of any historic
resource. This regulation establishes the qualifications and procedures for
application for this tax credit.
      The amount of the tax credit is ten percent (10%) of the amount expended
by the taxpayer for restoration and/or preservation of any structure or
building located on property classified as an historic site or an historic
resource located within an historic district as defined in this regulation. Any
excess credit above the tax amount for the approved year may be carried forward
to as many as five (5) subsequent tax years; provided, however, that if the
property is removed from the Master Plan for Historic Preservation, then any
unused portion of the tax credit accumulated by the taxpayer shall immediately
lapse.
      Applications are to be submitted to the applicable County or municipal
historic preservation commission on or before the first day of April of the
year before the tax year in which a tax credit is used.
52.41.01.02 Definitions
      The following word, phrases and terms when used in connection with this
regulation shall have the following meanings:
         A.   "Historic site" means any individual historic resource that is
significant and contributes to the historical, architectural, archeological or
cultural values and within the Maryland-Washington Regional District and which
has been so designated on the master plan for historic preservation.
         B.   "Historic district" means a group of historic resources which are
significant as a cohesive unit and contribute to the historical, architectural,
archeological or cultural values within the Maryland-Washington Regional
District and which has been so designated in the master plan for historic
preservation.
         C.   "Historic resource" means a district, site, building, structure
or object, including its appurtenances and environmental setting, which is
significant in national, state or local history, architecture, archeology or
culture.
         D.   "Appurtenances and environmental setting" means the entire
parcel, as of the date on which the historic resource is designated on the
master plan and structures thereon, on which is located an historic resource,
unless reduced by the Commission, and to which it relates physically and/or
visually. Appurtenances and environmental settings shall include, but not be
limited to, walkways and driveways (whether paved or not), vegetation
(including trees, gardens, lawns), rocks, pasture, cropland and waterways.
         E.   "Master Plan for Historic Preservation" is an amendment to the
general plan for the Maryland-Washington Regional District approved and adopted
by the Montgomery County Planning Board of the Maryland-National Capital Park
and Planning Commission. Such plan shall designate historic sites and historic
districts and describe their boundaries: it shall propose means for the
integration of historic preservation into the planning process; and it shall
suggest other measures to advance the goals of historic preservation.
         F.   "Historic Area Work Permit" means a permit issued by the Director
of the Department of Environmental Protection authorizing work on a historic
site or a historic resource located within a historic district.
         G.   "Ordinary Maintenance Expenses" means expenses defined in Section
24A-6 of the Montgomery County Code 1984, and the regulations and guidelines
adopted pursuant thereto.
         H.   "Director" means the Director of Finance of Montgomery County
Maryland.
         I.   "Tax Year" means a 12-month period which begins on July 1, and
ends the following June 30.
52.41.01.03 Eligibility Requirements
      To qualify for the credit all of the following requirements must be met:
         A.   The property subject to the credit must be an historic site or in
an historic district on a County or municipal master plan or zoning map.
         B.   Work performed is the subject of an approved County historic area
work permit or municipal certificate of approval; or the work performed is for
ordinary maintenance expenses as defined in guidelines adopted under Section
24A-6 and exceeds one thousand dollars ($1,000).
         C.   The amounts expended are not for new construction including new
structures on any historic site or any historic district, or a new addition
constructed as part of, or next to, an existing structure of historic,
architectural, or cultural value regardless of the architectural compatibility
of the addition.
         D.   The work is done by a contractor licensed to work in the County,
and a bill for such service has been received and paid by the taxpayer.
         E.   The expenditures were incurred by the taxpayer after September
21, 1979.
52.41.01.04 Applications and Due Dates
      Every property owner seeking a tax credit under this program must submit
an application supplying all such information and supporting documentation as
required by the Director. This application must be submitted on or before the
first day of April immediately preceding the taxable year for which a tax
credit is sought.
      This application must be submitted to the Montgomery County Historic
Preservation Commission (MCHPC) or the appropriate municipal historic
preservation commission. The application must include receipts and an oath or
affirmation by the taxpayer that the receipts are for qualified expenses under
section 52-42 of the Montgomery County Code, 1984.
      The applicable County or municipal historic preservation commission must
transmit all applications to the Director with a certificate that the property
is an historic site or in an historic district on the applicable County or
municipal master plan or zoning map.
      The Director may require additional information and-documentation from
the taxpayer, and may reject all or part of the claimed expenses for lack of
adequate documentation or if the claimed expenses do not qualify under section
52-42. The Director must notify the taxpayer of the Director's decision on the
application. An applicant filing an incomplete application shall be contacted
and requested to supply the missing or incomplete information. If the applicant
fails or refuses to supply the information requested within 30 days of the
request, the application shall be deemed disapproved and the applicant notified
accordingly.
52.41.01.05 Determination and Duration of Tax Credit
      The tax credit shall be ten percent (10%) of the expenses approved by the
Director. The resulting credit shall be applied to the County real property
taxes for the next tax year after the year in which the work or any part is
completed. The credit will not be applied to State of Maryland taxes, Municipal
taxes and special improvement charges, as well as other service charges such as
refuse charges and front foot benefit charges.
      Any unused credit may be carried forward to as many as five (5)
subsequent tax years. If the property is removed as an historic site or
excluded from an historic district on the applicable County or municipal master
plan or zoning may, any unused tax credit must lapse.
52.41.01.06 Appeal Rights
      Any taxpayer applicant aggrieved by the decision of the Director may
appeal to Maryland Tax Court as provided by law.
52.41.01.07 Processing Tax Credits
      When applications are received, reviewed and approved, the tax credit
amount will be calculated and a Historic Preservation Tax credit Certificate
will be issued. This certificate must be returned at the time of the payment of
the balance of the tax bill. The director will be responsible for reissuance of
a tax credit certificate in order for the taxpayer to use a carry-over tax
credit in a subsequent taxable year.
52.41.01.08 Penalties
      A person must not knowingly file a false or fraudulent application to
obtain a tax credit under this section. A violation of this section is a class
A violation.
      In addition, a taxpayer who violates Sections 52-41 through 52-46 of the
Code must pay the County any taxes and interest offset by the tax credit and
the County's fees and costs in any action to enforce Sections 52-41 through 52-
46.
52.41.01.09 Revision of Regulations
      These regulations are subject to revision as the need arises and as
approved by the County Executive for Montgomery County. Any revision to
regulations must be made in accordance with Method (2) of Section 2A-15 of the
Montgomery County Code, 1984.
   (Administrative History: Reg. No. 51-90 (Method 2); Dept.: Finance;
Supersedes: Regulation No. 35-86)

***** ARTICLE VII. DEVELOPMENT IMPACT TAX, SEC. 52-47 DEFINITIONS — REGULATIONS
