COMCOR 53.12.01 Standards for Wheelchair Accessible Taxicab Vans
53.12.01.01 Purpose
   The purpose of this regulation is:
      A.   To ensure maximum safety for all passengers.
      B.   To establish uniform special equipment as required by Chapter 53,
Section 53-12(b)(2) of the Montgomery County Code.
      C.   To ensure compliance with Subpart B, Section 38.23 through Section
38.25 of the implementing Federal regulation issued by the United States
Department of Transportation for The Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990,
P.L. 101-336. A copy of the Federal Regulation is attached and included as part
of this Executive Regulation.
53.12.01.02 Definitions
   The following definitions apply for this document:
      A.   ADA - Americans with Disabilities Act
      B.   Board - The act of entering a taxicab.
      C.   Disembark - The act of leaving a taxicab.
      D.   Deploy - The operation of a ramp or lift from a stowed position to a
position for use.
      E.   DOT - Montgomery County Department of Transportation.
      F.   Licensee - Person owning a wheelchair accessible taxicab van who has
a Passenger Vehicle License.
      G.   Lift- A mechanical device used to elevate a passenger to the level
of the cab floor and to lower the passenger to ground level.
      H.   Mobility Aid - A device used by an individual to assist with the
capability of movement.
      I.   Operator - Person licensed to drive a taxicab who provides taxicab
service to people with disabilities who are seated in a mobility aid.
      J.   Passenger - Person with a disability who is transported in a
wheelchair accessible van who rides in the cab seated in a wheelchair.
      K.   PVL - Passenger Vehicle License issued by DOT allowing a wheelchair
accessible van to be operated as a taxicab in Montgomery County.
      L.   Ramp - An inclined device with a continuous surface connecting the
floor of the taxicab to the ground used for a passenger to enter or exit a
taxicab.
      M.   Securement Device - A device anchored to a vehicle and used to limit
the movement of a wheelchair when the vehicle is in motion.
      N.   Supplier - Any agent or company selling vehicles or other equipment
to an operator.
      O.   Utility Aid - A device used to provide mobility assistance to a
passenger.
      P.   Vehicle - Taxicab passenger van used to transport people with
disabilities.
      Q.   Wheelchair - A seating arrangement that is positioned on three or
more wheels, may be powered or unpowered, and is used to assist people with
disabilities.
53.12.01.03 Operating Procedures
      A.   Before working in any job relating directly to people with
disabilities, any driver or other employee must complete the training program.
The licensee is responsible for providing driver training.
      B.   Before boarding or disembarking, the driver must bring the vehicle
to a complete stop and turn off the engine. The driver must put a vehicle with
manual transmission in gear and a vehicle with automatic transmission in Park
and set the parking brake.
      C.   When using a wheelchair ramp to board or disembark a passenger, the
driver must deploy the wheelchair ramp to a level, which is an unobstructed
sidewalk if physically possible, and must make sure that the ramp is firmly
attached to the vehicle.
      D.   The wheelchair ramp must be used only by passengers and the person
providing assistance. A driver may carry a folding wheelchair in the vehicle
for a semi-ambulatory person, at the passenger’s request.
      E.   The driver must assist a passenger up and down the ramp. The driver
must assist all people in boarding and disembarking the vehicle as reasonably
requested.
      F.   Before starting the vehicle, the driver must fasten a passenger’s
wheelchair firmly in the wheelchair securement device according to
manufacturer’s instructions.
      G.   The driver must use reasonable care in all aspects of the vehicle’s
operation.
53.12.01.04 Wheelchair Spaces
Each vehicle must have at least one wheelchair space. The wheelchair
orientation must be forward-facing or rear facing with a padded barrier.
53.12.01.05 Equipment Requirements
Prior to the placement of wheelchair accessible vehicles in revenue service,
all vehicles must meet, at a minimum, the approved requirements of the ADA and
the implementing Regulations. The supplier must provide clear written and/or
photographic instructions on the use of all ramps, lifts, and wheelchair
securement devices at the time of vehicle or equipment delivery.
      A.   General. All vehicles must have a level-change mechanism or boarding
device (lift or ramp). They must also provide a minimum of two side windows in
the passenger compartment.
      B.   Door Height. For vehicles of 22 feet in length or less, the overhead
clearance between the top of the door opening and the raised lift platform, or
highest point of a ramp, must be a minimum of 56 inches.
      C.   Interior Height. For vehicles of 22 feet in length or less, the
minimum interior height from lift to securement location must be 56 inches.
      D.   Securement Devices. A securement device that meets all requirements
must be supplied for each vehicle as follows:
         (1)   Usability. It is the licensee’s responsibility to insure that
the securement devices are maintained and are available for use at all times.
         (2)   Force to Be Restrained. The securement system and the attachment
to the vehicle must restrain a force in the forward longitudinal direction of
up to 2,500 pounds per tie down leg or clamping mechanism and a minimum of
5,000 pounds total for each mobility aid.
         (3)   Type of Securement Device. The securement device must be readily
fastened and released by either the driver or the passenger.
         (4)   Location and Size - The securement system must be placed as near
to the accessible entrance as practical and must have a clear floor area of 30
inches by 48 inches.
         (5)   Limiting Nominal Movement. When the wheelchair is properly
positioned and the securement device is fastened according to manufacturer’s
instructions, the securement device must limit the movement of an occupied
wheelchair to no more than 2 inches in any direction when the vehicle is in
normal operation.
         (6)   Wheelchairs to be Accommodated. Securement devices must
accommodate common wheelchairs and other mobility aids.
         (7)   Storage. When not being used for securement, the securement
device must be stored in such a way that it does not interfere with passenger
movement, does not present any condition that would be hazardous in normal
operations or in a crash environment, is reasonably protected from vandalism,
and is readily accessible when needed.
      E.   Surfaces
         (1)   Interior - All aisles, steps, floor areas where people walk and
floors in the securement location must have slip resistant surfaces.
         (2)   Contrast - All step edges, thresholds, boarding edges of ramps
and lift platforms must have a band of color(s) running the full width of the
step or edge which contrasts from the step tread and riser, or lift or ramp
surface. The colors may be either light-on-dark or dark-on-light.
         (3)   Lighting - Stepwells and doorways, including doorways in which
lifts or ramps are installed, must have at least 2 foot-candles of illumination
measured on the step tread, lift, or ramp, when deployed at the vehicle floor
level. Doorways must have light(s) which, when the door is open, provide at
least 1 foot-candle of illumination on the street surface for a distance of 3
feet. Lights must be shielded to protect the eyes of passengers.
      F.    Passenger Belt Requirements. The passenger belts must be easily
accessible and in good working order. Belts must not be used in lieu of
securement devices.
         (1)   Passengers. Separate from the wheelchair securement system, a
passenger belt system consisting of a lap and shoulder belt must be available
for the use of each occupant. The shoulder belt must be a minimum of 86 inches
in length and the second belt must be a minimum of 43 inches in length. Safety
belts must not be used as a securement device.
         (2)   Other Persons. Seat belts must be available for each person
riding in the vehicle who is not using a wheelchair.
         (3)   Compliance with FMVSS. The lap and shoulder belts must comply
with Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) 209, and the anchorages must
comply with FMVSS 210.
      G.   Lifts. Lifts must meet the following requirements:
         (1)   Installation. Lifts must be installed on the rear or the right
side of the vehicle.
         (2)   Design Load.
            (a)   Working parts, which can be expected to wear and on which the
lift depends for support of the load, must have a safety factor of at least
six. Non-working parts must have a safety factor of at least three.
            (b)   Must have the capacity to lift 600 pounds.
         (3)   Controls - Must be interlocked with the vehicle brakes,
transmission or door, or provide other appropriate mechanism or system, to
ensure that the vehicle cannot be moved when the lift is not stowed and that
the lift cannot be deployed unless the interlocks or systems are engaged.
         (4)   Platform
            (a)   Surface - must be free of any protrusions over 1/4 inch high
and must be slip resistant. The platform must have a minimum clear width of 28
1/2 inches at the platform, a minimum clear width of 30 inches measured from 2
inches above the platform, and a minimum clear length of 48 inches measured
from 2 inches above the surface of the platform to 30 inches above the surface
of the platform.
            (b)   Entrance - the entrance ramp must not exceed a slope of 1:8,
for a maximum rise of 3 inches.
            (c)   Gaps - Any openings between the platform surface and the
raised barriers must not exceed 5/8 inch in width. When the platform is at
vehicle floor height, gaps between the forward lift platform edge and the
vehicle floor must not exceed 1/2 inch horizontally and 5/8 inch vertically.
            (d)   Barriers - Must be equipped with barriers to prevent any of
the wheels of a wheelchair or mobility aid from rolling off the platform during
its operation. The side barriers must be at least 1 1/2 inches high.
            (e)   Edge - The boarding edge must have a band of color(s) running
the full width of the edge which contrasts from the ramp surface.
            (f)   Deflection - The platform must not deflect more than 3
degrees in any direction.
            (g)   Movement - The platform must not move at a rate exceeding 6
inches per second during lowering and lifting an occupant, and must not exceed
12 inches per second during deploying or stowing.
         (5)   Handrails - Platforms must be equipped with handrails on two
sides at least 8 inches long with the lowest portion a minimum of 30 inches
above the platform and the highest portion a maximum of 38 inches above the
platform. The handrails must be capable of withstanding a force of 100 pounds.
         (6)   Emergency Operation -
            (a)   Must have a manual back-up system.
            (b)   Must have provision to prevent deploying, falling, or folding
any faster than 12 inches per second or dropping a passenger in the event of a
power or equipment failure.
         (7)   Storage - Must lock in place when not in use so that it cannot
open and cause danger to passengers during the ride.
         (8)   Usability. It is the licensee’s responsibility to insure that
the lift is maintained and is available for use at all times. Failure to
provide revenue service to a passenger due to a non-working lift is grounds for
suspension or revocation of the PVL.
      H.   Ramps. A ramp that meets the following requirements:
         (1)   Usability. It is the licensee’s responsibility to insure that
the ramp is maintained and is available for use at all times. Failure to
provide revenue service to a passenger due to a non-working or unavailable ramp
is grounds for suspension or revocation of the PVL.
         (2)   Road Grades. The ramp must operate when the vehicle is on level
ground on road grades up to 7 percent or 4 degrees.
         (3)   Ramp Structure.
            (a)   Capacity. A ramp more than 30" long must be designed to
support a load of 600 pounds. Ramps shorter than 30" must be designed to
support a load of 300 pounds.
            (b)   Structural Safety Factor. The structural safety factor must
be at least 3 based on the ultimate strength of the construction material. The
structural safety factor is the ultimate strength of the material divided by
the working stress.
         (4)   Ramp Tests.
            (a)   Static Load Test. A design load of 600 pounds with a safety
factor of 3 (1800 pounds) must be applied through the centroid of a test pallet
placed in the center of the ramp. The test pallet must be 48 inches long and
the full width of the ramp. The load must remain on the ramp not less than 2
minutes. After the load is removed, an inspection must be made to determine
whether fractures have occurred.
            (b)   Ramp Attachment. When in use for boarding or alighting, the
ramp must be firmly attached to the vehicle so that it is not subject to
displacement when loading or unloading a heavy power mobility aid.
         (5)   Boarding Directions. The ramp must be designed so that a
passenger can use it facing either toward or away from the vehicle.
         (6)   Ramp Slope. The ramp must have the least slope practicable and
must not exceed 1:4 when deployed to ground level. If the height of the vehicle
floor from which the ramp is deployed is 3 inches or less above a 6 inch curb a
maximum slope of 1:4 is permitted; if the height of the vehicle floor from
which the ramp is deployed is 6 inches or less, but greater than 3 inches,
above a 6 inch curb, a maximum slope of 1:6 is permitted; if the height of the
vehicle floor from which the ramp is deployed is 9 inches or less, but greater
than 6 inches, above a 6 inch curb, a maximum slope of 1:8 is permitted; if the
height of the vehicle floor from which the ramp is deployed is greater than 9
inches above a 6 inch curb, a slope of 1 :12 must be achieved. Folding or
telescoping ramps are permitted provided they meet all structural requirements.
         (7)   Ramp Design.
            (a)   Barriers. Each side of the ramp must have a 2-inch edge
barrier prevent mobility aid wheels from slipping off.
            (b)   Surface. The surface of the ramp must:
               1.   be continuous
               2.   be slip resistant in all weather conditions.
               3.   not have protrusions from the surface greater than 1/4 inch
high.
               4.   have a clear width of 30 inches.
               5.   accommodate both four-wheel and three-wheel mobility aids.
            (c)   Threshold. The entryways of the ramp must not have a vertical
displacement (bump or drop off) greater than 1/4 inch.
            (d)   Force Required to Deploy or Stow. No more than 20 pounds must
be required to deploy or stow the ramp. One person must be able to deploy or
stow the ramp without assistance.
            (e)   Storage. A compartment, securement system, or other method
must be provided to ensure that:
               1.   ramps stowed in the passenger area do not impinge on a
passenger’s wheelchair or mobility aid or pose any hazard to passengers in the
event of a sudden stop or maneuver.
               2.   if the ramp is stowed in the passenger compartment, all
exposed edges or other hazardous protrusions on the stowed ramp are padded with
energy-absorbing material to minimize injury to passengers.
      I.   Maintenance and Inspection.
         (1)   Frequency. All ramps, lifts, and securement devices must be
maintained at a minimum as often as the manufacturers’ suggested schedule, to
ensure that the equipment meets the requirements of this regulation.
         (2)   Schedule and Documentation. The licensee must develop a schedule
for maintenance a d inspection and must develop records to document adherence
to the prescribed schedule. This schedule and documentation must be submitted
in advance to DOT for approval. The schedule and all records must be available
for inspection by DOT at any time. Copies of the schedule and inspection
records must be submitted to DOT during the PVL renewal process each year.
      J.   Vehicle Marking. All vehicles must permanently display the
international symbol of accessibility on each side door or body, and on the
rear door of body of the taxicab.
53.12.01.06 Training
      A.   Instructions from Supplier. The licensee must obtain instructions on
the use of ramps, lifts, or securement devices at the time of vehicle or
equipment delivery.
      B.   Personnel Training. The licensee is responsible for the training of
operators.
         (1)   Training Plan. Prior to the placement of the vehicle in revenue
service, the licensee must develop and submit for approval to DOT a training
plan sufficient to ensure that:
            (a)   the operator can operate all ramps, lifts, or wheelchair
securement devices, and any other necessary equipment safely;
            (b)   the operator is knowledgeable about this regulation and that
they follow all operating procedures required;
            (c)   the operator is knowledgeable about and sensitive to the
needs of people with disabilities regarding their rides in a taxicab;
            (d)   when picking up and discharging passengers the operator
provides curb to curb service;
            (e)   the operator pays close attention to any requests from the
passenger for assistance and follow directions carefully;
            (f)   at the passenger’s destination, the operator escorts the
passenger to the door of the building if there are obstructions, such as
construction, located between the vehicle and the building door, if requested
to do so by the passenger.
         (2)   Training Process.
            (a)   the licensee must require all new operators to go through the
training program before they provide taxicab service to passengers. Reservation
intake and dispatch staff must receive disability awareness sensitivity
training.
            (b)   the training must include disability awareness sensitivity,
use of equipment, interaction between driver and passenger, and special driving
skills.
            (c)   the licensee must periodically retrain all operators who work
directly with people with disabilities.
            (d)   the licensee must submit the name of the assigned operator
and the date that operator was trained, during the Passenger Vehicle License
renewal process. PVL’s must not be renewed if the operator has not been trained
or if training documentation is not submitted.
            (e)   DOT may require that the licensee submit a report listing the
names of all operators trained to drive accessible taxicabs from July 1 - June
30. This report, if requested, is due no later than July 30 each year. Failure
to submit the report is grounds for suspension or revocation of the Passenger
Vehicle License.
            (f)   failure to provide trained operators is grounds for
revocation of the PVL.
53.12.01.07 Effective Date
   This regulation will become effective thirty days after the deadline for
comments published in the Register.
      A.   Vehicles purchased after the effective date of this regulation must
meet the requirements of this regulation.
      B.   Vehicles for which a solicitation has been let must meet the
requirements of this regulation immediately, to the extent feasible and not
precluded by contract.
      C.   All existing and new vehicles must meet the requirements of
53.12.01.05 H (l)-(7). Wheelchair Ramp Design and
53.12.01.05 J. Vehicle Marking no later than 90 days after this regulation
becomes law.
      D.   All licensees must meet the requirement of
53.12.01.06 B. Personnel Training no later than 180 days after this regulation
becomes law.
53.12.01.08 Responsibility of Licensee
      A.   A licensee must not permit a vehicle to operate in the County if it
does not meet the requirements of this regulation.
      B.   A licensee must not permit an operator who does not meet the
requirements of this regulation to drive a vehicle.
      C.   Violation of the regulation is grounds for the revocation of all
accessible PVLs held by the licensee.
(Administrative History: Reg. No. 104-92AM (Method 3); Orig. Dept.: Public
Works and Transportation)

COMCOR 53.17.01 Taxicab Rates
53.17.01.01 Taxicab Rates
The
      A.   Rate for One Passenger:
         Rate for the Initial Charge                     $4.00
         For each one-fifth mile                     $ .50
         Night surcharge per trip (between 10 p.m. and 5 a.m.)         $1.00
      B.   Waiting and Traffic Delay Time:
         Rate for time beginning five minutes after the time the taxicab was
called for
         and for, time when the taxicab is stopped, or has slowed to a speed of
less
         than thirteen miles per hour. The extra time it may take to assist a
person
         with disabilities may not be charged as waiting time.         $28
      C.   Additional Passengers:
         Rate for more than one passenger in the same party. There is no charge
for
         a personal care attendant accompanying a person with disabilities for
mobility
         purposes. There is no charge for children younger than five years of
age when
         accompanied by an adult. All other passengers must pay the additional
         passenger charge.                           $1.00
      D.   Personal Service for Loading Items:
         Charge for any service provided by the driver in loading suitcases,
         parcels, or other personal effects at the request of the
passenger.         $1.00
      E.   Pick-up and Delivery:
         Charge for pickup and delivery service performed at the request of the
         passenger.                              $2.00
      F.    Snow Emergency:
         Charge in the event a snow emergency is declared by the State for
         the County.                               $2.50
      G.   Service Animal:
         Service animal traveling with a person with disabilities must be
         accommodated at no additional charge.                  $0.00
      H.   Tolls and Surcharges:
         Any toll or surcharge, as required, during the course of the trip.
         As Required
53.17.01.02 Fuel Surcharge
   Surcharges become effective in the amounts listed below when the average
price of regular unleaded gasoline, based on the American Automobile
Association Maryland Metropolitan Area Averages, Washington (Maryland Only) are
in place for 30 consecutive days. The surcharges are rescinded or return to the
prior surcharge when prices fall below the price point for 30 consecutive days
as follows:
         Gas Cost   Surcharge
         $5.00      $0.50
         $5.50      $1.00
         $6.00      $1.50
         $6.50      $2.00
53.17.01.03 Additional Passengers for County Grant Trips
The additional passenger rate for County grant trips is the rate for more than
one passenger in the same party when all the passengers are paying for the trip
with the grant funds or grant funded fare media. The purpose of the rate is to
encourage taxicab drivers to participate in transit initiatives funded by
grants to the County.
The rate for each additional passenger for County Grant trips      $5.00
53.17.01.04 Effective Date
This regulation will take effect on February 1, 2026.

***** ARTICLE II. TAXICAB LICENSE, SEC. 53-44A FLEET TAXICAB COMPANY LICENSES —
REGULATIONS *****
COMCOR 53.44A.01 Comparative Ranking System for Issuance of Taxicab Fleet
Passenger Vehicle Licenses
** 53.44A.01.01 **
      Comparative Ranking System/Criteria               Points
      A.   Knowledge and Experience             20
Familiarity with Maryland state laws and regulations for the operation of a
business. Experience operating a taxicab business. Summary information on past
years service and projection for next year of service for total fleet and new
licenses, and prior history of compliance with the code.
      B.   Customer Service                  20
Customer service, including service to persons with disabilities, customer
complaints, past levels of performance, no shows or late service, driver
training programs, calls not served, number and method of providing service for
calls unable to serve, development and participation in innovative services and
Department of Public Works and Transportation contractual services. Also the
geographic areas of service, existence of growth in the area and willingness to
serve in additional areas will be considered.
      C.   Business Plan                     20
Financial and managerial resources to operate and maintain the taxicabs and the
ability to comply with the code. Level of capitalization, projected costs, and
projected equipment purchases, and technological innovations.
      D.   Vehicle Fleet Plan                  20
Current fleet number, age, and quality. Maintenance plan and record of
maintenance of existing vehicles. Compliance with required vehicle inspections
and meter checks.
      E.   Demonstration of need                   20
Summary of productivity and operating data, including number of daily trips and
response time.
      Maximum Total Points                     100
** 53.44A.01.02 Selection **
The availability of fleet Passenger Vehicle Licenses will be advertised in at
least two newspapers of general distribution, once a week, for two weeks. All
requests for licenses must be received by the closing date as published.
If the available number of fleet licenses is insufficient to satisfy requests
from all qualified applicants, the Director may require all persons to submit
an application on a form approved by the Department.
The Director will appoint a Qualification and Selection Panel of three persons
to review each applicant’s submission utilizing the comparative ranking system.
Each member of the panel will assign points based on the quality of each
applicants’ submission from zero to twenty for each of the criteria, with zero
indicating a poor rating and twenty indicating the highest rating. The points
of all three panelists will be totaled for each applicant. Applicants with
total points of 225 or less will not be considered qualified. Applicants with
points greater than 225 will be eligible to receive licenses.
The highest ranked company will receive the most licenses. The remaining
qualified applicants will receive licenses, in priority ranking, until all
available licenses are exhausted. No company will be awarded licenses in excess
of the number requested in the application.
** 53.44A.01.03 Failure to Place Licenses in Revenue Service **
Licensees must place the Passenger Vehicle Licenses in revenue service within
six months of the date the license was awarded. The authorization to place a
taxicab in service expires if the vehicle is not placed in service within the
six month period.
(Administrative History: Reg. No. 45-97 (Method 3); Orig. Dept.: Public Works
and Transportation)

COMCOR 53.223.01 Taxicab Participation in User-Side Subsidy Programs
53.223.01.01 Background Information
Montgomery County Code Section 53-223 requires that a regulation be established
to define participation by taxicab fleets or associations in the County’s user-
side subsidy programs.
53.223.01.02 Participation Requirements
   1.   Taxicab fleets or associations that hold 30 or more taxicab Passenger
Vehicle Licenses (PVLs) must participate in the County’s user-side subsidy
programs.

Licenses (PVLs) are encouraged to participate in the County’s user-side subsidy
programs but are not required to participate.

approving the regulation or on a later date specified in the regulation. If the
Council takes no action of approval or disapproval, the regulation becomes
automatically effective 61 days after the Council received it, or on any later
deadline set by regulation.

***** ARTICLE II. TAXICAB LICENSES, DIVISION 5. TAXICAB VEHICLES, SEC. 53-228
REGARDING THE CALCULATION OF TIME WHEN PLACING OR REMOVING A VEHICLE FROM
SERVICE AS IT CONCERNS THE AGE OF THE VEHICLE — REGULATIONS *****
**** COMCOR 53.228.01 Calculation of Time When Placing or Removing a Vehicle
From Service as it Concerns the Age of the Vehicle ****
53.228.01.01 Purpose
The purpose of the regulation is to instruct how time will be calculated for
the purpose of placing taxicab vehicles in service and removing taxicab
vehicles from service as well as to establish the calendar day and month for
the beginning and the end of each model year.
53.228.01.02 Regulations
a.   A model year begins on September 1 and ends on August 31 of each calendar
year.
      b.   A new model year motor vehicle is considered to have no age (zero
years old in its first model year).
      c.   A new model year motor vehicle is considered one year old after
August 31.
d.   A motor vehicle may be placed in service when it is up to and including
five years old.
e.   A vehicle must be taken out of service when it is not safe and reliable
regardless of the model year.
53.228.01.03 Model Year Charts
Attached to this regulation are two Model Year Charts which describe the year
(s) in which certain vehicles can be placed into revenue service and the year
(s) in which certain vehicles must be removed from revenue service.
The purpose of the first chart attached as Exhibit “A” is to demonstrate the
application of this regulation for traditional gas-powered vehicles that are
not hybrid, electric, or wheelchair accessible sedans for model years 2015
through 2030 (the “Model Year Chart for Traditional Vehicles”). The inclusion
of the Model Year Chart for Traditional Vehicles is for demonstration purposes
and does not suggest that this Regulation has a termination date.
The purpose of the second chart attached as Exhibit “B” is to demonstrate the
application of this regulation for electric, hybrid, and wheelchair accessible
vehicles from 2013 through 2030 (“Model Year Chart for Electric, Hybrid and
Wheelchair Accessible Vehicles”). The inclusion of the Model Year Chart for
Electric, Hybrid and Wheelchair Accessible Vehicles is for demonstration
purposes and does not suggest that this Regulation has a termination date.
53.228.01.04 Effective Date
This regulation becomes effective when the Council adopts a resolution
approving the regulation or on a later date specified in the regulation. If the
Council does not approve or disapprove the proposed regulation with 60 days
after receiving it, or by any subsequent deadline set by resolution, the
regulation is automatically approved.
(Administrative History: Reg. No. 5-25 (Method 2); Orig. Dept.: Dept. of
Transportation; Supersedes: Reg. No. 25-07)

***** ARTICLE V. ACCESSIBILITY, SEC. 53-506 NUMBER OF ACCESSIBLE TAXICAB
LICENSES — REGULATIONS *****
COMCOR 53.506.01 Temporary Replacement of Accessible Taxicabs
53.506.01.01 Background Information
      Montgomery County Code Section 53-506(c) requires that the Department
must consider the recommendations of the Taxicab Services Advisory Committee to
establish a regulation to allow the temporary replacement of accessible
vehicles with sedans. The Commission on People With Disabilities and the
Department of Health and Human Services were also consulted.
      Section 53-506(a) requires that the overall number of accessible taxicab
licenses must not be less than 5% of the total of available County taxicab
licenses. The regulation proposes to require taxicab fleets or associations to
maintain a level of at least 8% accessible taxicab motor vehicles.
      Accessible taxicab service utilization declined significantly in FY 2000
when the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority (WMATA) reduced the
participation of County contract taxicab service. The number of trips reported
for FY 2000 was 65,100. The industry reported only 11,250 accessible taxicab
trips for FY 2007.
53.506.01.02. Purpose
      The purpose of the regulation is to define a policy to allow the
temporary replacement of accessible taxicabs with sedan motor vehicles.
53.506.01.03. Regulation
      A.   Taxicab fleets or associations may temporarily replace licenses that
are assigned to accessible vehicles with sedan motor vehicles to achieve 8% of
the total number of licenses held by the fleet or association.
      B.   In order for licensees to benefit from the privilege of reducing the
number of accessible taxicabs, the fleet or association must provide a plan,
approved by the Director, for improved accessible customer service that is
available 24 hours per day and 7 days per week.
      C.   Taxicab fleets or associations that do not currently hold any
licenses that are assigned to accessible vehicles are not required to place
accessible motor vehicles in service in order to achieve the 8% level until
they receive additional licenses either by award or transfer.
      D.   Taxicab fleets or associations that do not currently hold licenses
assigned to accessible vehicles or have some licenses but the number is below
the required 8% are not required to place additional accessible motor vehicles
in service until they receive additional licenses either by award or transfer.
For each newly awarded or transferred license, however, these taxicab fleets or
associations must place one accessible motor vehicle in service until the 8%
level is achieved.
      E.   Once the 8% level is reached, taxicab fleets or associations must
maintain the number of accessible taxicab motor vehicles at 8% or higher of the
total number of licenses held by the fleet or association.
      F.   Individual licensees that hold licenses that are assigned to
accessible vehicles may temporarily replace accessible taxicabs with sedan
motor vehicles.
      G.   All taxicab fleets or associations are required to have a minimum of
one accessible vehicle.
53.506.01.04 Effective Date
      This regulation becomes effective when the Council adopts a resolution
approving the regulation or on a later date specified in the regulation. If the
Council takes no action of approval or disapproval, the regulation becomes
automatically effective 61 days after the Council received it, or on any later
deadline set by regulation.
(Administrative History: Reg. No. 29-07 (Method 2); Orig. Dept.: Public Works
and Transportation)

***** ARTICLE VIII. TRANSPORTATION SERVICES IMPROVEMENT FUND REQUIREMENTS, SEC.
53-801 — REGULATIONS *****
COMCOR 53.801.01 Transportation Services Improvement Fund
53.801.01.01 Background Information
   In 2015, the Maryland General Assembly passed legislation regulating
Transportation Network Companies (TNC), including ride-hailing services such as
Uber and Lyft. The legislation (which is codified at § 10-401, et seq of the
Public Utilities Article) created a new regulatory framework in which TNCs in
the State must operate. In addition to its regulatory function, the legislation
also authorizes a county or municipality to impose an assessment on TNC trips
that originate within the county or municipality. Pursuant to the State’s
enabling legislation, Montgomery County has imposed a 25 cent assessment fee
(or “surcharge”) on TNCs for each trip originating in the County. All revenue
generated from the imposed assessments and disbursed by the State to the County
are placed in a Transportation Services Improvement Fund (referred to hereafter
as “the Fund”) and must be used for transportation purposes that are specified
in § 53-801 of the Montgomery County Code.
   Section 53-801 of the Montgomery County Code requires the County Executive
to establish, by regulation, procedures for disbursing monies from the Fund.
The monies from the Fund are to be used to ensure the continued viability of
accessible service throughout the County for persons with disabilities,
eligible senior citizens, and persons of limited income.
53.801.01.02 Purpose
   The purpose of this regulation is to:
      (a)   establish programs to offset the increased costs of owning and
operating accessible vehicles for which taxicab Owners and Drivers may be
eligible for disbursement from the Fund;
      (b)   establish incentive programs for improving or expanding
transportation options for persons with disabilities, eligible senior citizens,
and persons of limited income, for which taxicab Owners and Drivers may be
eligible for distributions from the Fund; and
      (c)   establish rules and procedures for distributing monies from the
Fund to eligible applicants who desire to participate in the authorized
programs.
53.801.01.03 Regulation
      (a)   Applicants must use an application form provided by the Department,
complete the form fully, and agree to all terms contained in the application.
      (b)   The application must provide that a person who makes a false
statement to any questions on the application form will be denied disbursement
from the Fund, and that funds already disbursed based on false information must
be returned to the County.
      (c)   Applicants must submit all required documentation to the Department
to qualify for the distribution or reimbursement from the Fund.
      (d)   The Fund provides many programs of opportunity for reimbursement or
distribution of monies to eligible applicants. In order for an eligible
applicant to qualify for any reimbursement or distribution of monies from the
Fund, the applicant must have satisfied all reporting requirements required by
this Regulation or the County Code. The County must not disburse any monies
from the Fund to an applicant if the applicant is not in compliance with the
reporting requirements of any program provided for in this Regulation in which
the applicant has participated.
      (e)   Fleets and Associations seeking disbursements from the Fund must
provide dispatch system data to the Montgomery County Department of
Transportation (MCDOT) as necessary to verify reported trip information.
      (f)   Fleets and Associations participating in programs defined in this
Regulation must work with MCDOT to disseminate program information and
opportunities related to the Fund to drivers.
      (g)   The application must provide that a recipient of monies disbursed
from the Fund must agree to return those monies to the County if the
recipient’s PVL or Taxicab Driver Identification Card is revoked, suspended, or
denied by the County within five years of disbursement from the Fund.
53.801.01.04 Definitions
      (a)   Accessible Taxicab – means a taxicab that is a wheelchair
accessible vehicle that the Department has authorized to transport passengers
with disabilities.
      (b)   Association – means individual licensees who join together to form
a business entity to provide taxicab service utilizing a single trade name
consisting of a minimum of six licenses.
      (c)   Department – means the Montgomery County Department of
Transportation (MCDOT).
      (d)   Driver – means an individual authorized to operate a taxicab under
Chapter 53 of the Montgomery County Code who has been issued a Montgomery
County Taxicab Driver Identification Card.
      (e)   Fleet – means any entity that holds in its own name six or more
licenses.
      (f)   License – means a Passenger Vehicle License issued by Montgomery
County.
      (g)   Licensee – means an individual or fleet to whom the Director of the
Montgomery County Department of Transportation (MCDOT) has issued a Passenger
Vehicle License (PVL) to provide taxicab service.
      (h)   Owner – means a Licensee who has been issued and holds a valid PVL
to provide taxicab services in Montgomery County with a specified motor
vehicle, and:
         (1)   is listed with the state motor vehicle agency as holding legal
title to the specific motor vehicle for which the PVL was issued;
         (2)   is a conditional vendee or lessee of the vehicle for which the
PVL is issued that is the subject of an agreement for conditional sale or
lease, if the conditional vendee or lessee has assumed liability, and is
authorized to pay judgments and accept any legal notice or service of process,
with respect to the vehicle; or
         (3)   acts as the agent of the registered owner for all purposes,
including acceptance of liability, payment of judgments and other legal
obligations, and receipt of any legal notice of process.
      (i)   Passenger Vehicle License (PVL) – means a County-issued license to
provide taxicab service using a specified motor vehicle.
      (j)   Taxicab Service – means carrying one or more passengers for
compensation between points chosen by the passenger:
         (1)   regardless of how or when engaged, for a fare that is based on
the distance traveled, time elapsed, or both, except as expressly authorized in
this Chapter; or
         (2)   after being engaged by hail from a street, or from a parking
lot, taxi stand, or other location where the vehicle is waiting for a request
for service.
53.801.01.05 Reimbursements and Distributions
   In this Regulation, reimbursements and distributions are based on:
      (a)   the increased costs incurred by Drivers and Owners of Accessible
Taxicabs;
      (b)   the need to incentivize operation of Accessible Taxicabs;
      (c)   the desire to maintain an adequate number of licensed Drivers
providing Accessible Taxicab services; and
      (d)   the need to incentivize taxi services for Call-n-Ride customers
requiring short trips.
   These reimbursements and distributions are broken down into three
categories: a) Accessible Taxicab Ownership, b) Accessible Taxicab Operating/
Driver Expenses, and c) Taxicab Service Incentives, and will be disbursed from
the Fund as provided below. All disbursements are subject to the availability
and appropriation of monies in the Fund.
      (a)   Accessible Taxicab Ownership
         Background
         The cost to purchase a larger vehicle and convert it to an Accessible
Taxicab is significantly more than that of a standard sedan. In 2022, it was
estimated that the costs to convert a vehicle was between $21,000 and $40,000
depending on the type of vehicle and extent of the modifications. Additionally,
the cost to maintain these vehicles is higher due to the additional systems
associated with the lifts and increased wear on brakes and transmissions. The
Fund will reimburse a portion of these costs to encourage the operation of
Accessible Taxicabs in the County.
         Funding Opportunities
         To address the higher initial costs and ongoing maintenance costs of
Accessible Taxicabs, up to $45,000 per eligible vehicle may be available for
reimbursement as set forth in this Regulation. Except as set forth in this
Regulation, an Owner is not eligible for a disbursement from the Fund for the
purchase of an Accessible Taxicab or the conversion of a vehicle into an
Accessible Taxicab if a previous disbursement was made from the Fund for the
purchase or conversion of that particular vehicle.
         To be eligible for reimbursement of up to $45,000, the Owner must
complete and submit a reimbursement application along with documentation of:
(1) the purchase of an Accessible Taxicab on or after July 1, 2022, that is
presently not more than three model years old, or (2) the conversion of a
vehicle that is presently not more than three model years old to an Accessible
Taxicab on or after July 1, 2022. An Owner who applies for capital
reimbursement under this program must agree that the PVL associated with the
Accessible Taxicab will be required to be associated with an Accessible Taxicab
for all subsequent renewals of the PVL.
         As part of the reimbursement application, the Owner must agree that
following reimbursement, and on a quarterly basis, the Owner must demonstrate
that the Accessible Taxicab has been in operation for a minimum of 40 hours per
week for at least 48 weeks (or equivalent thereof) each year for five years
immediately following payment. The Owner must agree that if these required
hours of operation are not met and demonstrated by manifests or data deemed
acceptable by MCDOT’s Taxicab Unit, that the Owner will be required, upon
demand by the County, to return the disbursed funds to the County, and the
County may take legal action against any recipient in violation of program
requirements.
      (b)   Accessible Taxicab Operating/Driver Expenses
         Background
         There are often higher costs associated with providing accessible
passenger service that are not reflected in a standard taxicab meter rate.
MCDOT will reimburse taxicab operators for the additional time required to
assist passengers in wheelchairs or motorized scooters to safely board and
disembark an Accessible Taxicab.
         Funding Opportunities
         Wheelchair Trips
         The County will reimburse Drivers of Accessible Taxicabs who
successfully transport passengers requiring wheelchair service at a rate of $20
per trip completed.
         To receive a disbursement, the Driver must complete and submit a
reimbursement application along with a signed manifest documenting all trips
provided in the previous month, with any wheelchair trips clearly identified.
Taxicab drivers must submit trip manifests to the Taxicab Regulation Unit on,
or before, the fifth day of every month, unless such day is not a County day of
business for the Taxicab Regulation Unit, in which case the driver must submit
the trip manifest by the following County day of business for the Taxicab
Regulation Unit. The applicant must highlight all dispatched and transported
passenger wheelchair trip pickups listed on trip records submitted to MCDOT.
MCDOT may verify the trip records with the affiliated Fleet or Association’s
record.
      (c)   Taxicab Service Incentives
         Background
         In order to entice more Owners and Drivers into purchasing,
retrofitting and driving Accessible Taxicabs, and to provide improved
transportation services for persons with disabilities, eligible senior
citizens, and persons of limited income, additional incentives must be offered
to reach the goal set forth in § 53-506(e) of the County Code and improve and
expand service options as set forth in § 53-801(d)(2) of the County Code.
         Funding Opportunities
         Mileage
         Drivers of Accessible Taxicabs are eligible for disbursement from the
Fund at the rate of 40 cents per mile for every mile that the Accessible
Taxicab travels when providing Taxicab Service, regardless of passenger type.
To receive a disbursement, the Driver must complete and submit a reimbursement
application along with a signed manifest documenting all trips provided in the
previous month, with any wheelchair trips clearly identified. Taxicab drivers
must submit trip manifests to the Taxicab Regulation Unit on, or before, the
fifth day of every month unless such day is not a County day of business for
the Taxicab Regulation Unit, in which case the driver must submit the trip
manifest by the following County day of business for the Taxicab Regulation
Unit. The applicant must highlight all dispatched and transported passenger
wheelchair trip pickups listed on trip records submitted to MCDOT. MCDOT may
verify the trip records with the affiliated Fleet or Association’s record.
MCDOT may verify mileage claims by examination of vehicle equipment or other
available data.
         To ensure the continued availability of robust on-demand Taxicab
Service for Montgomery County residents and guests, MCDOT will not provide
mileage reimbursement for any taxicab trip that is farther than 75 miles from
the initial pick-up location, or 150 miles round trip.
         Insurance
         For Accessible Taxicabs operating a minimum 48 weeks per year and 40
hours per week, or an equivalent thereof as demonstrated by manifests or data
deemed acceptable by MCDOT’s Taxicab Unit, Licensees may apply to be reimbursed
for costs to purchase a third-party policy of insurance meeting the minimum
amounts required by § 53-224(a) of the Montgomery County Code. The Licensee
must apply for reimbursement and demonstrate the expenditure for a third-party
policy of insurance meeting the minimum amounts required by § 53-224(a) of the
Montgomery County Code. If the Licensee demonstrates that the Accessible
Taxicab has operated for a minimum of 48 weeks per year and 40 hours per week
(or equivalent thereof), the Licensee may be approved to be reimbursed $1,000
per year for the actual costs spent on purchasing a policy of insurance for the
Accessible Taxicab. Licensees are eligible for reimbursement at the time they
can demonstrate adequate levels of Accessible Taxicab service for one year
prior to the date of reimbursement.
         Fees to MCDOT
         For Accessible Taxicabs operating a minimum 48 weeks per year and 40
hours per week, or an equivalent thereof as demonstrated by manifests or data
deemed acceptable by MCDOT’s Taxicab Unit, Licensees are eligible to be
reimbursed for the payment of certain fees as set forth in this Regulation.
         (1)   PVL Renewal Fee: Licensees may apply for reimbursement from the
Fund for their annual PVL renewal fee after demonstrating the provision of
accessible service in the Accessible Taxicab for the year following the PVL
renewal.
         (2)   PVL Transfer Fee: For a PVL transfer that involves changing the
vehicle associated with that PVL from a sedan to an Accessible Taxicab, the new
Licensee may apply to MCDOT, at the time of fee payment, for reimbursement from
the Fund for the PVL transfer fee. A Licensee who applies for reimbursement of
the PVL Transfer Fee must agree that the PVL will be required to be associated
with an Accessible Taxicab, and that all subsequent renewals of that PVL will
be for an Accessible Taxicab.
         (3)   Application and Initial License Fee for Newly Issued Licenses:
If the Department issues new Licenses for Accessible Taxicabs, an applicant for
the License who is found qualified to compete for a PVL by the Department may,
after being found qualified, apply for reimbursement of the application fee,
irrespective of whether the applicant is issued a License. An applicant who is
issued a PVL for an Accessible Taxicab may apply to MCDOT, at the time of fee
payment, for reimbursement from the Fund for costs to pay the initial license
fee.
         Call-n-Ride Guaranteed Fare
         Background
         Call-n-Ride customers requiring taxicab transportation for shorter
trips are less attractive trips for taxi dispatch because of the low resulting
fare, but Call-n-Ride customers may have no alternative to transportation by
taxi, including trips across relatively short distances.
         Funding Opportunity
         To encourage timely and more reliable service to Call-n-Ride
customers, MCDOT will round up any Call-n-Ride fare to $10, resulting in a $10
guaranteed fare to taxicab Drivers for both accessible and non-accessible Call-
n-Ride trips, and regardless of taxicab vehicle type. The difference between
the meter rate charged to the Call-n-Ride customer and the $10 guaranteed fare
will be paid to Drivers and be based on the Driver’s trip manifest and any
standard verifications conducted by the Call-n-Ride program staff.
53.801.01.06 Reimbursement Transparency
   Reimbursements from the Fund will be reported annually by the Department of
Transportation’s Taxicab Services Section.
53.801.01.07 Application and Requirements
   All applications and required documentation shall be on forms and in a
format approved by the Director of MCDOT.
53.801.01.08 Minimum Fund Levels and Prorated Disbursements
   All disbursements from the Fund are subject to the availability and
appropriation of adequate funding.
   MCDOT may halt or temporarily freeze the application process for any or all
reimbursement opportunities included in this Regulation if projected financial
obligations for previously-approved applicants meet or exceed funds already
transferred from the State to the Fund.
53.801.01.09 Misuse of Funds
   Any recipient of a disbursement under this regulation who uses the monies
for any purpose other than as permitted by the County hereunder must refund all
monies received within seven (7) days of a County demand for a refund. Any
individual who makes a false statement or submits fraudulent information in
order to obtain a disbursement from the fund to which the person is not
entitled, or any recipient who misuses a disbursement is barred from
participating in this program and is subject to any action that may be brought
in law or in equity, including all actions and penalties contained in Chapter
53 of the Montgomery County Code.
53.801.01.10 Reimbursement Not to Exceed the Purchase Price of the Accessible
Taxicab
   Reimbursement from the Fund to purchase an Accessible Taxicab or retrofit
the vehicle into an Accessible Taxicab may not exceed the amount the applicant
actually paid to purchase or retrofit the vehicle. Awardees of federal, state
or private funding grants towards the procurement of an Accessible Taxicab are
ineligible to receive reimbursement from the Fund for costs incurred to
purchase or retrofit the vehicle, such that the total amount of grants and
reimbursements exceeds the purchase price of the vehicle.
53.801.01.11 Transportation Enhancements
   At the end of each calendar year, the Director will review the Fund balance
to determine what portion of the Fund may be used to improve or expand
transportation options for persons with disabilities, eligible senior citizens
or persons with limited income.
53.801.01.12 Effective Date
   This Regulation becomes effective when the Council adopts a resolution
approving the Regulation or on a later date specified in the Regulation. If the
Council does not approve or disapprove the proposed Regulation within 60 days
after receiving it, or by any subsequent deadline set by resolution, the
Regulation is automatically approved.
(Administrative History: Reg. No. 18-24 (Method 2); Orig. Dept.:
Transportation; Supersedes: Reg. No. 10-22, which superseded Reg. No. 11-19,
which superseded Reg. No. 1-17)
CHAPTER 53A. TENANT DISPLACEMENT — REGULATIONS
COMCOR 53A.00.01 Tenant Displacement
53A.00.01.01 Tenant Relocation Payments
1.1   (a)   Giving of notice.
      (1)   An owner must give tenants 120 days’ written notice before
converting the rental housing in which the tenants live. The notice of the
owner’s intention to convert the rental housing must also include a notice to
the tenants that relocation assistance is available.
      (2)   An owner must provide the Department of Housing and Community
Affairs (“Department”) a copy of the notice of conversion, a list of all of the
tenants, the address of each tenant, and proof that the notice was given to
each tenant.
   (b)   Method of delivery. The notice will be considered to have been given
to each tenant if mailed, first class, postage prepaid, to the tenant’s last
known address. When mailed, the owner must obtain a certificate of mailing from
the United States Postal Service. For purposes of these notice requirements,
the third day after the postmark date is the date of delivery. In addition, the
notice must be posted in the public areas of the rental housing.
   (c)   Termination of lease by tenant. After receiving a notice of
conversion, a tenant may terminate a lease without penalty by giving the owner
at least 30 days’ written notice.
   (d)   The owner must pay relocation assistance equal to twice the monthly
rent that the tenant was paying at the time of the notice. Payment must be made
to the tenant not more than ten days after the owner receives a tenant’s notice
of termination under Section 1.1(c) if the tenant:
      (1)   agrees to move out of the rental housing within 180 days after the
tenant receives the notice of conversion; and
      (2)   is current with rent at the time that the relocation is due to the
tenant.
   (e)   Payment of this relocation assistance does not relieve the tenant of
his/her obligation to make any rent payment that comes due for the period of
time he/she continues to occupy the rental housing.
1.2   Form of notice. The following language must be in a conspicuous location
on the notice:
      NOTICE — PURSUANT TO CHAPTER 53A OF THE MONTGOMERY COUNTY CODE AND
EXECUTIVE REGULATIONS ENFORCING CHAPTER 53A, YOU ARE ELIGIBLE FOR RELOCATION
ASSISTANCE FROM THE OWNER OF {'{'}INSERT NAME OF THE RENTAL HOUSING{'}'}.
      You are entitled to a payment by the owner in an amount equal to two
months’ rent if:
         (a)   you agree to move out of your rental housing within 180 days
after you receive this notice; and
         (b)   you are current with rent at the time the relocation assistance
is paid to you.
      To receive the relocation assistance, give your landlord at least 30
days’ written notice that you intend to terminate your lease and provide the
landlord with the date that you will leave your rental housing. The date that
you vacate your rental housing must be no later than 180 days from your receipt
of this notice.
      The landlord must pay you the relocation assistance within ten days of
receiving your notice to terminate the lease if you are current on your rent.
You must continue to pay rent to the landlord from the time you receive this
notice until the time that you vacate the rental housing.
      For more information, please refer to the Montgomery County regulations
attached to this notice.
1.3   The owner must issue the payment directly to a tenant unless the owner
notifies the Department in writing that the tenant is not current with rent.
The notice to the Department must include the tenant’s name, address and rental
account information and a copy must also be forwarded to the tenant at the
tenant’s last known address.
1.4   Any dispute concerning the payment or non-payment of relocation
assistance to a tenant must first be referred to the Department. After an
investigation, the Department will determine the amount of the relocation
payment that is to be paid. The Department’s determination is binding on the
tenant and the owner.
53A.00.01.02 Certification of Tenant Organization
2.1   A tenant organization may be certified by making a written request for
certification to the Department. The request must be filed within 45 days of
receipt of the owner’s offer to sell under Section 53A-3 of the Code.
2.2   The certification request must be accompanied by a list of the names,
addresses and signatures of the members of the tenant organization and a
notarized affidavit from the President of the tenant organization stating that
the tenants are a bona fide tenant organization representing a minimum of 30%
of the occupied rental units. Only leaseholders may be members of the tenant
organization. Occupants are not eligible. Department staff will verify the
information provided in the tenant organization’s certification request.
2.3   In the event that more than one tenant organization from the same rental
housing applies for certification, the tenant organization with the highest
percentage of representation of occupied rental units will be certified.
53A.00.01.03 Required Offer, Supporting Documents and Inspection Under Right of
First Refusal
3.1   The owner’s first right of refusal offer must include the following
information/documentation:
   (a)   a copy of any pending sales contract;
   (b)   site plan, if available;
   (c)   statement of income and expenses for the three previous years of
operation;
   (d)   current rental schedule by apartment showing date of last rent
increase, names of current tenants, addresses and telephone numbers;
   (e)   expected re-rent rates;
   (f)   latest tax assessment and tax rate;
   (g)   names of mortgage holders, existing mortgage balances and terms,
repayment terms, interest rates, loans for which rental units are used as
collateral, liens, covenants, easements and any other documents recorded
against the property;
   (h)   security deposit schedule and identification of escrow accounts; and
   (i)   any other agreements the owner may have concerning the rental housing
that may materially affect a decision to purchase the rental housing.
3.2   The offer is not complete until all of the information and documentation
identified in 3.1 is provided to the Department, Housing Opportunities
Commission (HOC), and/or a tenant organization. The timelines to exercise the
right of first refusal in 3.9 and 3.10 do not begin to run until all the
information and documentation is provided.
3.3   Information and documentation submitted by the owner pursuant to Section
3.1 will not be disclosed by the County, HOC, a tenant organization, or any
qualified entity except as required by law.
3.4   In addition, if requested and available, the owner must provide the
following information and documentation within five business days of a request
for the information or documentation:
   (a)   any architectural, engineering, mechanical, structural plans or
specifications;
   (b)   lead certification;
   (c)   Phase I environmental survey;
   (d)   information concerning underground storage tanks;
   (e)   copies of all service contracts such as property management and
maintenance contracts; and
   (f)   existing warranties on any major component of the rental housing, such
as the roof, heating, air conditioning and hot water heater.
3.5   Any request for information or documentation identified in Section 3.4
extends the time period provided in Section 3.8 by any amount of time beyond
five business days of receiving the request.
3.6   The County, HOC, any tenant organization, and any County assignee must
pay the owner the reasonable cost of reproduction, or a reasonable and
refundable deposit, for any requested information and documentation.
3.7   Within five business days of receiving a request for inspection, an owner
must provide access to the rental housing to the County, HOC, a tenant
organization, or any County Assignee. The owner may have a representative
present at the time of the inspections.
3.8   Under the right of first refusal, the owner’s offer to sell the property
to the County and HOC must remain open for 60 days after it is received by the
County and HOC and must remain open for 90 days after it is received by the
tenants. The offer must remain open one additional day for each day that
documents requested under subsection 3.4 are received after the five-day
response time. If any material term or condition, including but not limited to,
a change in price or financing in any pending contract is altered, or if an
owner enters into another contract of sale subsequent to any initial or other
offer from an owner to the County, HOC, or a tenant organization, the owner
must make a new offer to the County, HOC, or a tenant organization reflecting
the new material terms and conditions. Each new offer must remain open for 60
days following receipt by the County and HOC, and for 90 days following receipt
by the tenants.
3.9   The County, HOC, and any County assignee may exercise the right of first
refusal by accepting the offer within 60 days of receiving the offer, plus any
extension required by Section 3.8. In the event that either the County, HOC,
and/or any County assignee exercise the right of first refusal at any time
during the 60-day period, the right of first refusal provided to a tenant
organization is no longer enforceable.
3.10   Upon approval of a majority of tenants in the occupied units of the
rental housing, a tenant organization may exercise the right of first refusal
by accepting the offer within 90 days of receiving the offer, plus any
extension required by Section 3.8.
3.11   An acceptance of an offer under the right of first refusal must include:
   (a)   substantially the same terms contained in the owner’s offer, including
any bona fide real estate commission payable to an independent broker; and
      (i)   notwithstanding the general requirement in subparagraph (a) above
or any term of the owner’s offer including the pending sale contract, the
County, HOC, any tenant organization, or any County assignee shall not be
required to pay to the owner a deposit of more than 5% of the contract price to
accept the offer and exercise its right of first refusal. The deposit is
refundable in the event of a good faith failure of the County, HOC, any tenant
organization, or any County assignee to perform under the contract;
   (b)   a 180-day financing contingency.
   The time periods specified in Sections 3.9 and 3.10 are included in the 180-
day period.
3.12   The purchase of the rental housing by the County, HOC, a tenant
organization, or any County assignee must be completed within 180 days of
receipt of the owner’s offer, unless a longer time is agreed to by the owner
and the County, HOC, the tenant organization, or any County assignee.
3.13   If the County, HOC, a tenant organization, or any County assignee
accepts an owner’s offer to purchase the rental housing in compliance with
Chapter 53A and these regulations, the owner must sell the rental housing to
the County, HOC, the tenant organization, or any County assignee.
3.14   Any sale of rental housing in violation of Chapter 53A and these
regulations is void.
3.15   If the sale of rental housing is void, the owner must offer the rental
housing to the County, HOC, or any tenant organization in compliance with
Chapter 53A and these regulations and under the same terms offered to the
original purchaser.
53A.00.01.04 Agreement Not to Convert
4.1   The County, in its sole discretion, may refuse to enter into an Agreement
Not to Convert.
4.2   An Agreement Not to Convert may be approved or rejected by the Department
after the Department considers, among other factors, the following:
   (a)   physical condition of the rental housing, including any rehabilitation
necessary to correct dangerous defects;
   (b)   tenants’ ability to afford rent increases; and
   (c)   need to preserve low- and moderate-income rental housing in the
County.
4.3   Within 30 days of a purchaser entering into an Agreement Not to Convert,
the owner of the rental housing must provide the Department:
   (a)   a copy of each current lease; and
   (b)   a current rental schedule identifying each rental unit and showing the
date and amount of the last rent increase, the name of the current tenant, and
the tenant’s telephone number.
4.4   Tenants who, under Section 53A-5(a)(1)(C)(ii) of the Code, are eligible
for rents to be capped at the voluntary rental guidelines in years four and
five of the Agreement Not to Convert, must provide certain information and
documentation to the Department. This documentation and information will
include, but will not be limited to, personal income information. A tenant who
fails to provide the information requested by the Department will forfeit his
or her right to receive the protections afforded him or her in the Agreement
Not to Convert and in Section 53A-5 of the Code.
4.5   Each year on the anniversary of the Agreement Not to Convert, the owner
must submit a compliance report to the Department in a form acceptable to the
Department containing at least the following information:
   (a)   current rent roll;
   (b)   copy of any lease by a new tenant within the last 12 months;
   (c)   list of tenants vacating the rental housing within the last 12 months;
and
   (d)   any rent increases within the last 12 months.
4.6   If the owner petitions the Department for a rental increase above the
limits set forth in the Agreement Not to Convert, the owner must provide all
necessary and reasonable information requested by the Department in support of
the owner’s petition.
4.7   An owner must not increase the rent for any unit in the rental housing
above the limits set forth in the Agreement Not to Convert without first
obtaining prior written authorization from the Department.
53A.00.01.05 Process for Designating Qualified Entities and Assigning the Right
of First Refusal
5.1   The Department must conduct a rolling application process for designating
qualified entities under Section 53A-4(g). A designated qualified entity
remains qualified for a period of five years after which the entity must
reapply under Section 53A-4(g).
5.2   To be designated as a qualified entity by the Department, the applicant
must:
   (a)   certify in writing that for the past ten years the applicant,
inclusive of its principals, members, managers and directors, has complied with
all laws related to the acquisition, maintenance, and management of housing;
   (b)   commit in writing that it will not disclose any information or
documentation it receives from the Department under
53A.00.01.03.1 unless required by law;
   (c)   demonstrate that it has expertise and experience acquiring, owning,
operating, managing, and developing rental and affordable housing by providing
the following information:
      (1)   a list of lenders and equity sources used in prior projects;
      (2)   a comprehensive list of the applicant’s prior residential
developments with property addresses, numbers of units, project financing, and
affordability covenants as applicable;
      (3)   a complete certified list of code citations if any, for each
property owned, managed, and operated by the applicant for the last five years;
      (4)   a complete certified list of judgments issued against the applicant
in a landlord/tenant or similar proceeding, if any, related to the applicant’s
ownership, management, or operation of any property for the last five years;
      (5)   a description of property and asset management experience with a
list of any management companies used at other properties;
      (6)   a certification that the applicant has never been in financial
default as either a borrower or guarantor, or if to the contrary, explaining in
complete detail all the circumstances;
   (d)   demonstrate a commitment to community engagement, such as working with
neighborhood-based organizations or tenant counseling organizations on anti-
displacement activities;
   (e)   demonstrate such other criteria as may reasonably be determined by the
Department or County from time to time; and
   (f)   demonstrate that it is registered and licensed to do business in
Maryland and otherwise in good standing under Maryland law.
5.3   The Department must require an assignee in the assignment agreement to
implement the following restrictions:
   (a)   a landlord must not evict a tenant from a rental unit, notwithstanding
the expiration of the tenant’s lease or rental agreement. Exceptions only apply
if the tenant of said unit:
      (1)   breaches the lease or causes damage to a rental unit or other area
of the property and refuses to pay for damages or correct the breach of lease
within 30 days after receiving notice from the landlord;
      (2)   fails to pay rent as required per the lease, provided that the
nonpayment of a late fee may not be the basis of the eviction;
      (3)   disturbs the peace and quiet of other tenants despite receiving
notice from the landlord;
      (4)   engages in illegal activity on the property; and
      (5)   refuses without reasonable cause to allow a landlord onto a leased
premises to make repairs or inspect the property.
   (b)   provide existing tenants the right to return to their unit or an
equivalent unit at the same rent levels after any rehabilitation or
redevelopment that requires relocation; and
   (c)   limit rent increases to no more than the Voluntary Rent Guidelines
(VRG) for 15 years, unless the units are covered by other agreements that
ensure long-term affordability of greater than 15 years or as otherwise
required by law.
5.4   The Department must publish on its website, and make available upon
request, a list of qualified entities.
5.5   Disqualification of qualified entities.
   (a)   The Department must promptly investigate any complaint alleging that a
qualified entity has violated or is in violation of any provision of Section
53A. If, after providing the qualified entity with notice, the County Executive
determines that a qualified entity has violated or is in violation of any
provision of Section 53-A, the County Executive may suspend or revoke the
designation as a qualified entity.
   (b)   If a qualified entity is chosen by the County Executive or designee
and fails to complete the purchase of the rental housing using the right of
first refusal for reasons other than the good faith failure to secure
financing, the Department must promptly investigate the reasons for the failure
to purchase and the County may suspend or revoke the designation as a qualified
entity. For purposes of this section, good faith failure to secure financing
includes failure to secure adequate funding to reach the amount or depth of
affordability included in the qualified entity’s proposal to purchase rental
housing.
5.6   If the County Executive or designee decides to explore assigning the
right of first refusal to purchase rental housing, the County Executive or
designee must issue a request for submittals to all qualified entities.
   (a)   Each request for submittals must be disseminated via electronic mail
or web link to all qualified entities.
   (b)   The request for submittals must include the following:
      (1)   all restrictions under
53A.00.01.5.3; and
      (2)   other information affecting the development of the housing
accommodation, including:
         (A)   a copy of all materials provided to the County by the owner of
rental housing under
53A.00.01.03.3.1 and
53A.00.01.03.3.4, if the County has previously requested and received the
latter information;
         (B)   the covenant template that will be placed on the rental housing;
         (C)   the date when proposals are due;
         (D)   the criteria the County Executive or the County Executive’s
designee must use for selecting assignees from among qualified entities;
         (E)   the procedure that will be used following acceptance of a
proposal until execution of an assignment agreement; and
         (F)   other information the Department determines appropriate to
further the purposes of Section 53A-4.
5.7   Criteria for selecting a qualified entity as a County assignee. The
County Executive must consider the following criteria for selecting among
qualified entity applications to be the County assignee of a rental housing
sales contract:
   (a)   the commitment of the qualified entity to preserve the existing number
of units affordable to households with incomes at or below 70 percent of the
Area Median Income for the Washington Metropolitan Statistical Area and the
relative levels of affordability of those units at the time the Department
received the notice of sale under Section 53A-3;
   (b)   the commitment of the qualified entity to the creation of more units
affordable to households with incomes at 30 percent, 40 percent, 50 percent, 60
percent, and 70 percent of Area Median Income for the Washington Metropolitan
Statistical Area than existed at the time the Department received the notice of
sale under Section 53A-3;
   (c)   tenant anti-displacement protections proposed by the qualified entity;
   (d)   the cost per unit of funding requested from the County;
   (e)   the availability of County funds;
   (f)   the sufficiency of other funding sources proposed by the qualified
entity;
   (g)   the past success of the qualified entity with similar affordable
housing developments;
   (h)   the qualifications of any partners proposed by the qualified entity;
   (i)   the past success of the qualified entity in providing resident
services at other properties and any proposal to provide resident services at
the rental housing being considered for assignment;
   (j)   the commitment of the qualified entity to maintaining the
affordability of the units for a term longer than 15 years; and
   (k)   the demonstrated experience developing, preserving, owning, operating,
and/or managing housing for the specific population of the rental housing, if
applicable.
53A.00.01.06 Severability
6.1   The provisions of this regulation are severable and if any provision,
clause, sentence, section, word, or part is held illegal, unconstitutional, or
inapplicable to any person or circumstance such illegality, invalidity,
unconstitutionality, or inapplicability will not affect or impair any of the
remaining provisions, clauses, sentences, sections, words, or parts of this
regulation or its application to other persons or circumstances.
(Administrative History: Reg. No. 16-23 (Method 2); Orig. Dept.: Housing and
Community Affairs; Supersedes Reg. No. 2-02AM, which superseded Reg. Nos. 18-
97, 19-97, 20-97, 21-97, and 22-97)
