CHAPTER 55. TREE CANOPY — REGULATIONS
COMCOR
55.00.01    Tree Canopy
COMCOR 55.00.01 Tree Canopy
55.00.01.01 Purpose
      This regulation implements the Tree Canopy Law, Chapter 55 of the
Montgomery County Code as adopted by Bill No. 35-12.
55.00.01.02 Definitions
      Definitions of the terms used in the regulation are provided in Section
55-3 of the County Code. For the purpose of this regulation, the following
additional words and phrases will have the meaning respectively ascribed to
them in this regulation:
         Growing zone: a contiguous area at least 400 square feet of open
surface area free of any impervious surface, utility, stormwater management
system, or any other impediment to tree and root growth and development.
         Planting area: any location within a growing zone where a shade tree
can be planted.
         Planting plan: an approved sediment control plan that shows all
approved potential growing zones, approved potential planting areas within each
growing zone, and an approved planting detail.
         Record drawing plan or as-built plan: at a minimum, a set of drawings
comparing the approved planting plan requirements with what was constructed.
The Director may require additional information as needed.
55.00.01.03 General Administration
      Except as otherwise provided in this regulation, procedures for
application, implementation, review, approval, denial, and appeal are the same
as the procedures for sediment control permits under Chapter 19 of the County
Code.
55.00.01.04 Documents Incorporated by Reference
      The following documents are incorporated by reference as if fully set
forth. Whenever the provisions of this regulation and those of the following
documents are in conflict, the provisions of this regulation will govern and be
enforced in the County:
      A.   American National Standards for Tree Care Operations, ANSI A300,
American National Standards Institute, hereinafter referred to as ANSI A300, in
effect as of December 1, 2013.
      B.   American Standard for Nursery Stock, ANSI Z60.1, American Nursery &
Landscape Association, hereinafter referred to as ANSI Z60.1, in effect as of
December 1, 2013.
55.00.01.05 Exemptions
      Any person exempt under Section 55-5 of the County Code must include the
exemption on the sediment control plan at the time of application, on all
approved revisions, and on any record drawing plans or as-built plans.
55.00.01.06 Required Number of Shade Trees
      A.   The number of shade trees required shall be as specified in Section
55-6(b) of the County Code.
      B.   If the square footage of the limits of disturbance is more than
40,000, then the number of shade trees required must be calculated using the
following formula:
            (Number of Square Feet in Limits of Disturbance + 40,000) × 15
         If necessary, the number of shade trees required shall be rounded to
the nearest whole number using standard rounding rules. No less than one
additional shade tree shall be required for any square footage above the first
40,000 square feet within the limits of disturbance.
55.00.01.07 Submissions
      A.   Required submissions for application. In addition to other required
information and supporting certifications as required for submission of
sediment control plans under Chapter 19 of the County Code and as required by
Section 55-7 of the County Code, a person subject to this Chapter must also
submit to the Director the following information with each application for a
sediment control permit:
         (1)   a planting plan delineating:
            (a)   boundaries for all potential growing zones;
            (b)   all acceptable planting areas within each potential growing
zone;
            (c)   a tree planting detail if trees can be planted on-site to
satisfy mitigation requirements under Section 55-6 of the Code.
         (2)   a table summarizing:
            (a)   the square footage of the property;
            (b)   the square footage of the limits of disturbance of the
proposed activity as shown on the sediment control permit application;
            (c)   the square footage of each potential growing zone;
            (d)   the number of shade trees required under 55-6 of the County
Code;
            (e)   the number of shade trees to be planted on site; and
            (f)   the amount of fees to be paid under Section 55-6 of the
County Code.
      B.   Issuance of sediment control permit. The Director must not issue a
sediment control permit to a person that is subject to this regulation until:
         (1)   the Director has approved the applicant's planting plan if no
exemption under Section 55-5 of the County Code applies;
         (2)   the applicant provides all fees required under Chapter 55-6 of
the County Code; and
         (3)   the applicant has satisfied all applicable requirements under
Article I of Chapter 19 of the County Code.
      C.   Revisions to Approved Plans.
         (1)   If the limits of disturbance or disturbed area are increased
after issuance of the sediment control permit, the shade tree planting
requirements must be recalculated based upon the revised area. The table
required in Section 55-7(a)(2) of the County Code must be revised accordingly.
         (2)   If any approved growing zones shown on the approved sediment
control plan are later revised, or if additional growing zones are added, the
sediment control plan must be revised and resubmitted for review. The fee for
reviewing the revised plans must be the minimum fee for the review of a
sediment control plan.
         (3)   If the disturbed area, or limits of disturbance, are decreased,
without changes to approved growing zones, after issuance of the sediment
control permit, the tree planting requirements may not be decreased if any
disturbance has occurred under that permit.
      D.   Closure of Sediment Control Permit. Upon completion of a project
that is subject to this section and before the sediment control permit is
closed by the Department, the applicant must submit a record drawing plan or
as-built plan that includes the following:
         (1)   all information required by 55.00.01.07(A)(1) and (2) of this
regulation;
         (2)   any revisions to plans, specifically to growing zones and
planting areas including those approved in the field;
         (3)   any revisions to the table summarizing requirements in Section
55-6(b) of the County Code; and
         (4)   all other requirements under Chapter 19 of the County Code.
55.00.01.08 Shade Tree Planting
      The planting of each shade tree under Chapter 55 of the County Code must
conform to the following requirements:
      A.   Each shade tree must be planted within the planting area within a
growing zone as defined under this regulation and as approved on the sediment
control plan.
      B.   The growing zone may be of any shape subject to the following:
         (1)   The distance from any point on the growing zone boundary to any
other point must not be greater than 30 feet.
         (2)   It must be possible to draw a straight line from every point in
the growing zone to the stem of the planted tree without going outside the
boundary.
         (3)   The entire growing zone must be completely within the boundary
of the subject property; except open surface area on an adjacent right-of-way
may be included if no utility, public utility easement, stormwater management
system, or impervious surface is located in that part of the right-of-way.
         (4)   The growing zone must not contain any impediments to tree and
root growth and development, including:
            (a)   No part of the growing zone can be closer than 5 feet,
measured horizontally, from any electric, gas, water, sewer, telephone, cable
television, or other overhead or underground utility.
            (b)   No part of the growing zone can be closer than 5 feet,
measured horizontally, from any stormwater management system.
            (c)   The growing zone must not include any concrete, asphalt,
brick, gravel, or other impervious surface.
            (d)   The growing zone must not include any retaining walls, clean
construction fill (including but not limited to brick, block, stone, or sand),
underground storage tanks, bedrock, compacted soil, or other impediment to root
growth.
            (e)   The growing zone must not include any area within a septic
easement or a septic reserve.
      C.   The stem of any shade tree planted within a growing zone must:
         (1)   Be planted such that a straight line can be drawn from the stem
to any point on the growing zone boundary without going outside the growing
zone.
         (2)   Be no closer than 5 feet from any point on the growing zone
boundary.
         (3)   Be no closer than 10 feet from any structure with a building
foundation below grade.
         (4)   Be no closer than 15 feet, measured horizontally, from the
closest point on the ground directly below an electric, telephone, cable
television, or other overhead wire.
         (5)   Be on the subject property and no closer than 5 feet from any
property boundary, right-of-way, public utility easement or other public
improvement easement.
      D.   Each shade tree must conform to the following:
         (1)   Shade trees must meet all requirements for plant material in
ANSI Z60.1;
         (2)   Shade trees must be a minimum of 2" caliper.
      E.   The installation of each shade tree must:
         (1)   meet all requirements of ANSI A300.
         (2)   At the time of planting:
            (a)   Tree guards to protect trees from deer rubbing, mowers, weed
eaters, other equipment, and large rodents must be installed on all shade
trees.
            (b)   Mulch must be applied.
            (c)   Sufficient water must be applied to aid in proper planting.
      F.   Timing of Plantings
         (1)   Shade trees must be installed between October 15th and May 15th
as long as the ground is not frozen, saturated, or covered with snow such that
a suitable hole cannot be dug to plant the tree properly.
         (2)   Shade trees must not be installed between May 16th and October
14th of each year.
         (3)   If shade trees are installed prior to final stabilization of the
land disturbing activity then no additional disturbance must occur within five
feet of the stem of the tree. Protective fencing must be installed at edge of
this area at the same time the tree is installed and must remain in place until
final stabilization occurs.
         (4)   If installation of shade trees to meet the requirements of
Chapter 55 of the County Code cannot occur between October 15th and May 15th
for any reason, or will not be planted for any other reason, the applicant must
pay the required fees.
55.00.01.09 Field Markings
      A.   Field markings must exist on site before and during installation of
all newly planted shade trees, sediment and erosion control measures,
construction, or other land disturbing activities.
      B.   The location of all potential growing zones must be clearly marked
in the field prior to any land disturbing activity.
      C.   The location of all potential growing zones and planting areas must
be clearly marked in the field prior to installation of any shade trees.
55.00.01.10 Inspections
      A.   A copy of the approved sediment control plan showing all approved
growing zones and planting areas, must be available on the site at all times.
      B.   At least one inspection must occur after all construction activities
are completed to determine the level of compliance with shade tree planting
requirements.
55.00.01.11 Severability
      If a court holds that a portion of this regulation is invalid, the other
portions remain in effect.
   (Administrative History: Reg. No. 22-13 (Method 2); Orig. Dept.: Permitting
Services)

***** ARTICLE I. IN GENERAL, SEC. 56-1A DEMOLITION LOAN PROGRAM — REGULATIONS
*****
COMCOR 56.01A.01 Financial Assistance to Demolish Commercial Properties
** 56.01A.01.01 Authority **
      In accordance with Section 56-1A of the Montgomery County Code 1994, as
amended, the following Executive Regulation establishes guidelines and
procedures to administer the Demolition Loan Program as part of the Economic
Development Fund.
** 56.01A.01.02 Definitions **
      Urban renewal area shall mean a slum area or blighted area or both, which
the county council for Montgomery County designates as appropriate for an urban
renewal project.
      Blighted area shall mean an area in which a majority of buildings have
declined in productivity by reason of obsolescence, depreciation or other
causes to an extent they no longer justify fundamental repairs and adequate
maintenance.
      Private Property Owner - An owner of property in Montgomery County.
      Enterprise Zone shall be defined as in Maryland Annotated Code Article
83A, Section 5-401(f) (1998).
      Commercial Revitalization shall be defined as programs described in
Maryland Annotated Code Article 83A, Section 3-401(c) (1998).
** 56.01A.01.03 Eligibility **
   (a)   Any private property owner whose property is located in the County
that plans to demolish a vacant or severely underutilized commercial building
located in geographic areas defined in Section 56-1A.
   (b)   Projects in municipal incorporated areas must be approved by the
legislative body of that jurisdiction.
   (c)   Highest consideration may be given to properties proven to be
uneconomical to rehabilitate in commercial revitalization areas, enterprise
zones, or areas declared by the county council as being blighted.
** 56.01A.01.04 Loan Guidelines **
   When making loans, consideration should also be given to the following:
   (a)   Priority may be given to assistance that will materially improve the
County's economy and advance the County's economic development objectives and
strategies.
   (b)   Highest consideration may be given to assistance that brings
significant employment growth.
   (c)   Priority may be given to assistance that causes significant investment
by the private property owner that over time will provide significant revenues
to the County.
   (d)   In urban revitalization areas, private property owners of sites with
good public transportation may be given priority consideration.
   (e)   Priority may be given to commercial building demolition that reverses
commercial deterioration.
   (f)   Special consideration may given to commercial building demolition
projects where County assistance will enhance the comprehensiveness and
competitiveness of the overall financial package and compliment State financial
incentives.
** 56.01A.01.05 Program Operations **
   A.   Accounting of Funds
      (1)   The Director of the Department of Finance must establish an
identification mechanism in the Economic Development Fund to track all revenues
and expenditures provided under the Demolition Loan Program.
      (2)   The Director of Finance may spend or allocate loans or grants from
the program on the basis of criteria defined in the Executive Regulations and
the law.
      (3)   The County Executive must notify the County Council at least two
working days (or five working days during a Council recess) before offering
assistance valued at more than $100,000, specifying the proposed terms of
assistance offered including any repayment provisions. The Council President,
by notification to the County Executive, may request an additional two working
days (or five working days during Council recess) for Council comment before
the offer of assistance is made to the private property owner. Any change in
assistance made after initial notification that increases the amount of
forgiveness of a loan is subject to this same requirement.
   B.   Administration of Loan Program
      (1)   The Department of Housing and Community Affairs shall be
responsible for the day-to- day administrative support for the program
including, but not limited to: intake, project eligibility determination,
recommending appropriate levels of assistance, loan document preparation,
defining collateralization requirements, underwriting determinations, and
recommending loan terms.
      (2)   The County Executive shall designate a Conunercial Building
Demolition Program Committee composed of the Directors of the Department of
Housing and Community Affairs, Finance, and the Department of Economic
Development, or their designees, to oversee the operations of the program and
make recommendations to the County Executive on specific projects requesting
assistance over $20,000. For loans $20,000 or less, the Director of the
Department of Housing and Community Affairs may approve loans without the
review and approval of the Committee.
   C.   Loan Assistance
      (1)   Loan assistance will be limited to actual demolition expenses,
utility cut-offs, and final site grading and finishing.
      (2)   Terms and conditions of assistance for loans greater than $20,000
shall be determined by the Committee.
      (3)   The repayment terms for any loan may allow for partial or full
forgiveness of the loan when the Director of the Department of Housing and
Community Affairs finds that forgiveness would best accomplish the purposes of
the program.
      (4)   The Committee may require loan applicants in this program to
provide documentation establishing proof of property ownership, ability to
repay the loan, envirorunental hazard research related to the proposed
demolition and other material as needed and appropriate.
      (5)   Assistance under this program may include a range of financing
mechanisms, including but not limited to "balloon payment loans," "interest
only loans," "staggered payment loans," and "deferred payments," until certain
economic development objectives are attained.
      (6)   The minimum annual repayment of loans under this program shall be
equivalent to the current year real estate taxes on the improvements to be
demolished through use of the assistance, unless waived by the Committee.
      (7)   All loans made under this program must be secured to 100% of the
loan value and collateral may include Deeds of Trust, Letters of Credit, and/or
the pledge of other assets. All assets, real or personal, offered as collateral
must be accompanied by a current professional appraisal.
      (8)   No funds will be disbursed to borrowers under this program until
all demolition work is complete and all environmental hazard mitigation
requirements satisfied.
      (9)   Borrowers of funds under this program shall indemnify and hold
harmless the County from all claims and liabilities related to the use of these
funds.
   (Administrative History: Reg. No. 5-99AM (Method 2); Orig. Dept.: Housing
and Community Affairs)
Editor’s note—2015 L.M.C., ch. 36, § 6, states, in part: Reference to the
Department of Economic Development in COMCOR 56.01A.01 (Financial Assistance to
Demolish Commercial Properties) is deleted.
2015 L.M.C., ch. 36, § 8, also states, in part: All other provisions of this
Act take effect 180 days after the Montgomery County Economic Development
Corporation is designated under Section 30B-2.
***** ARTICLE II. HOMEOWNERS’ REPLACEMENT LOAN FUND, SEC. 56-6 ADMINISTRATION —
REGULATIONS *****
COMCOR 56.06.01 Administrative Guidelines for the Replacement Loan Fund
56.06.01.01 Program Purpose
1.1   The purpose of a loan from the Fund is to eliminate existing conditions
of deterioration and obsolescence that contribute to the threat of the health
and safety of owners and their families living in substandard housing, when the
condition of the existing housing is not economically feasible to rehabilitate.
1.2   Construction funded by this loan is determined to be needed to bring the
property into compliance with all applicable State and County statutes, codes
and ordinances. Replacement loans are limited to constructing housing which is
reasonably necessary to accommodate the present occupancy and usage while
protecting the County's investment.
1.3   Enhancing energy conservation measures will be taken into consideration
in making loans from this fund.
56.06.01.02 Administration
2.1   The Department of Housing and Community Development - The Department of
Housing and Community Development (DHCD) will administer the Homeowners'
Replacement Loan Fund (hereinafter "the Fund"). DHCD is responsible for
establishing the necessary departmental procedures and practices to ensure the
expeditious handling of all requests for replacement assistance. The Director
of DHCD assigns the staff needed to provide the technical and advisory services
required for the proper and efficient administration of the Fund. Further, DHCD
staff is responsible for determining if the existing dwelling is in violation
of State or County statutes, codes or ordinances and whether the dwelling can
be economically rehabilitated. When the dwelling is located within a
municipality, DHCD will request an inspection from the appropriate public
agency responsible for enforcing housing code standards.
2.2   Department of Finance - The Department of Finance will disburse and
collect funds and keep permanent financial records for each rehabilitation
loan.
2.3   Basic Eligibility - The Planning Manager, Division of Housing, DHCD, will
receive applications for processing and determine the ability of the homeowners
to meet the following basic criteria:
   a.   Applicant is an owner-occupant,
   b.   Income limits established for the program,
   c.   Single-family structure,
   d.   Availability of safe and sanitary water supply and sewage disposal
systems, and
   e.   Ability of the homeowner to maintain the property in a habitable
condition.
      The Director, DHCD, may redelegate this authority.
2.4   Loan Approval Authority - The Chief, Division of Housing, DHCD, approves
or denies loans for homeowners that meet the basic criteria.
   The Director, DHCD, may redelegate this authority.
2.5   Disposition - Any homeowner whose loan request is denied is advised in
writing as to the reason(s) for this decision.
2.7   Appeals - Any homeowner whose request for a loan is not approved may
appeal the decision to the Director of DHCD or the Director's designee. The
appeal must be in writing and must be forwarded to the Director within thirty
(30) days from the date the homeowner receives notification that the loan was
not approved. The Director will review the application, and within thirty (30)
days from receipt of the appeal, render a final decision on behalf of
Montgomery County.
2.8   Waiver Authority - The Director of DHCD may waive any procedure or
criterion established by this regulation when, in the judgment of the Director,
it is in the public interest.
56.06.01.03 Property Eligibility Requirements
3.1   To be eligible for loans from the Fund, properties must meet the
following requires:
   1.   Properties must be single-family, owner-occupied homes or mobile homes
which are in violation of one or more of the provisions of the State and County
statutes, codes and ordinances relating to the use, maintenance, facilities and
occupancy of existing property.
   2.   Land on which replacement houses will be constructed must be situated
in locations they are not in conflict with the following types of governmental
projects:
      a.   Federally-assisted urban renewal and concentrated code enforcement
projects.
      b.   Projects for the construction or development of public schools,
parks, streets, highways, utilities or other public works.
         This requirement must not be construed to preclude loans on properties
located within Federally-assisted urban renewal projects that are not in
conflict with any governmental project or for when a similar Federal program
for rehabilitation loans are not available.
   3.   Properties must be located where safe, sanitary and adequate water
supply and sewage disposal are available, will be provided as a result of
receipt of the loan proceeds, or will become available within a foreseeable
period of time by future construction of programmed capital projects.
   4.   The dwelling must be determined to be not economically feasible to
rehabilitate. This decision is based on a finding that the expense required to
bring the property into compliance with the applicable County Codes and
ordinances would be excessive in relation to the resulting benefit to the
property.
   5.   Loans may be made for replacement houses that will be constructed on a
lot other than the one on which the deteriorated house is situated when the
original lot cannot be served by a safe, sanitary and adequate water supply and
sewage disposal system, or does not conform to other Chapters of the County or
State Codes. In this event, DHCD will determine whether a deed transferring the
lot from the applicant to the County will be required, whereby the value of
this lot will be credited to the loan balance.
56.06.01.04 Financing Requirements
4.1   Loans from this program will be made only to homeowners whose incomes and
assets preclude financing through normal banking or other financial channels.
Loans made from the Fund are subject to the following requirements and
limitations:
   1.   Loans will be made only to those households whose gross family incomes
do not exceed the Section 8 Lower Income standards established by the U.S.
Department of Housing and Urban Development, for the Washington Metropolitan
Area.
   2.   Loans made to homeowners must carry an initial interest rate from one
to six percent per year determined by the monthly costs of interest, taxes,
insurance, maintenance, and utilities so that the total costs will not exceed
thirty-five percent (35%) of the gross family income based on a 45 year
amortization term. When necessary, the Director may approve the deferral of all
or part of the interest and principal payment until there is an increase in the
homeowner's income, or until such time that there is a transfer of the property
by deed or probate, the homeowner moves from the premises, or the loan period
terminates.
   3.   Gross family income is defined as the total gross income from all
sources including wages, investment income, social security payments,
retirement pensions, public assistance payments, alimony payments, and
unemployment benefits received by all family members on the deed and family
members residing in the household, or the rent that may reasonably be
attributed from these household members.
   4.   The initial loan term and interest rate must be based on the financial
circumstances of the homeowner at the time of the loan approval. Every two
years the homeowner must provide DHCD, on its request, with financial
information similar to that provided in the original application. If the
initial rate of interest is less than six percent, the interest rate must be
increased to a higher rate upon determination that 35 percent of the family
gross income is sufficient to pay monthly shelter costs at the higher rate. The
initial rate, as well as the principal repayment amount, may be subsequently
decreased upon a determination by DHCD that the homeowner will pay more than 35
percent of family gross income for monthly shelter costs or that the property
will suffer undue financial hardship if the interest rate and payments remain
as previously established. "Shelter costs" means principal and interest
payments on the loan, taxes, insurance, maintenance and utilities.
   5.   An analysis of the verified income and expenses of the homeowner is
performed by DHCD staff. This analysis must conclude that, based upon
conventional underwriting standards, the homeowner would not be able to obtain
financing through normal banking or other financial channels. Whenever a
financial analysis by the DHCD staff indicates that the homeowner should be
able to secure home financing through normal banking channels, the homeowner
must provide sufficient documentation requested by DHCD staff to demonstrate
that the homeowner has not been able to obtain this financing. In determining
the ability of the homeowner to obtain adequate private financing, the
following will be taken into consideration:
      a.   The present condition and value of the property;
      b.   Real estate owned by the homeowner that would be a source of funds
if sold, leased, or mortgaged;
      c.   Gross family income and assets of persons whose names appear on the
title;
      d.   Interest rates available for real estate loans from commercial and
other sources; and
      e.   Other pertinent financial information as deemed necessary by DHCD.
   6.   In order to be eligible for a replacement loan, the homeowner must
prove adequate capacity to repay the loan or show that the security for the
loan poses little risk for the County's investment. A replacement loan will not
be approved if the credit record shows a disregard by the homeowner of
financial obligations. A co-signer may be required to sign the note to further
protect the County's interests.
   7.   A part of the loan proceeds may be used to consolidate or pay off prior
liens when it will contribute substantially to the affordability of the
replacement house, but will not jeopardize the security of the County's
investment as determined by DHCD.
56.06.01.05 Contractor Eligibility
5.1   In order to participate in the replacement house program, a contractor
must have the following:
   1.   A valid and current Montgomery County Builder's license.
   2.   Liability insurance covering death or bodily injury with limits of not
less than $100,000 for one person and $300,000 for any one accident or
disaster.
   3.   Property damage insurance, with limits of not less than $100,000.
   4.   Good credit standing with suppliers and subcontractors.
   5.   A minimum of two years experience in constructing single or multifamily
housing.
5.2   Homeowners may not act as general contractors or be paid for their own
labor or materials.
5.3   Contractors who desire to participate in this program must agree to
provide references to DHCD upon request.
56.06.01.06 Contractor Selection
6.1   DHCD may maintain a list of licensed general contractors interested in
doing new home construction work. Such contractors should meet the requirements
of
56.06.01.04 of this regulation.
6.2   DHCD staff may solicit proposals on the homeowner's behalf for
contractors for each job. The homeowner will also be provided with appropriate
bid documents to solicit bids on his own behalf. DHCD reviews all bids with the
homeowner, who must select the lowest responsible bidder.
56.06.01.07 Contract Agreement
7.1   All homeowners and contractors who participate in the Replacement Loan
Program must execute contractual agreements on forms provided by DHCD and
approved by the Office of the County Attorney. The Replacement Loan contract is
between the homeowner and the contractor. This contractual agreement must
contain the work to be performed, the guarantees to be provided for the work
performed, the method of payment, and the requirements for inspections that may
be required by DHCD.
56.06.01.08 Disbursement of Loan Funds
8.1   Disbursement of funds must be made according to a schedule of payments.
This schedule must be established no later than the start of construction.
Funds may be placed in an escrow account. No payment may be disbursed for any
work which has not been satisfactorily completed as determined by DHCD. In most
cases checks shall be made jointly payable to the homeowner and the contractor,
although in some cases, DHCD may make payments directly to a contractor or
supplier.
8.2   Each disbursement is made to the contractor upon certification by DHCD
staff that the work has progressed at least to the proportionate amount of the
draw, or that the work has been completed so that the amount of the balance of
the contract is due. All construction draw payments are subject to a ten
percent retainage which is released upon total completion of the work including
punch list items. Prior to the final disbursement, the contractor must supply a
release of liens of subcontractors and suppliers, and provide written
warranties as provided in the contract. The homeowner must certify that all
contract work is satisfactorily completed.
56.06.01.09 Insurance
9.1   All homeowners must provide and maintain for the life of the loan a fire
insurance policy designating Montgomery County as a loss payee. The policy must
be provided no later than the time of loan settlement and must be in an amount
sufficient to cover the loan in the event the property is destroyed by fire. In
the event such coverage cannot be secured, DHCD may take whatever steps it
deems appropriate to ensure the County's best interests are protected.
56.06.01.10 Compliance with Federal and State Lending Laws
10.1   DHCD will issue a disclosure statement to each homeowner. This statement
will indicate the principal amount of the loan, total amount of interest, loan
origination fee if any, inspection fee, credit fee, settlement charges on the
loan, annual effective rate of interest and any other fees collected at
settlement. DHCD will provide the homeowner with a notice of the opportunity to
rescind the agreement to borrow from the Fund. This disclosure statement and
notice to rescind are required by Federal law.
56.06.01.11 Deferral of Payments
11.1   The Director of DHCD or the Director's designee may temporarily defer
payments when a homeowner demonstrates, to the satisfaction of the Director,
sufficient hardship as to be unable to make the required payments; however,
such deferral will not be construed to be a waiver of any of the County's
rights to recover its loan.
56.06.01.12 Collection Enforcement
12.1   DHCD will monitor the loan to ensure that homeowners make prompt
payments on their replacement loan. DHCD will counsel any homeowners who are
having problems making their loan repayments. Whenever a homeowner is in
default, DHCD will determine whether or not the County will foreclose on the
loan. Upon request of the Director, the County Attorney may institute
foreclosure proceedings.
56.06.01.13 Disputes
13.1   Any disputes arising between the homeowner and the contractor or the
DHCD staff and the homeowner will be brought to the attention of the Director
or his designee for resolution. The Director is empowered to mediate or
arbitrate such disputes or to institute proceedings for its resolution by an
outside arbitrator.
56.06.01.14 Percolation Test, Well Drilling Test, and Title Search
14.1   Whenever the homeowner does not have the financial resources to pay for
a percolation test, a well drilling test, or a title search, or reasonable
costs to clear title, DHCD may authorize expenditure from available funds. If a
loan is executed, the expended monies will be included in the loan amount.
56.06.01.15 Transfer of Property
15.1   Upon transfer of title or a sale of a property for which a loan has been
made from this program, DHCD reserves the right to accelerate the payments of
the loan in which case the entire balance including interest will be due and
payable, or DHCD may negotiate an assumption of the loan with the interest and
terms based upon the income and other eligibility characteristics of the new
homeowner.
56.06.01.16 General
16.1   Where a new home or mobile home replaces an existing substandard home or
mobile home, the substandard structure must be removed from the property
promptly after completion or installation of the new dwelling.
(Administrative History: Reg. No. 79-92 (Method 2); Orig. Dept.: Housing and
Community Affairs; Supersedes Reg. No. 45-89)

   (a)   Opportunity housing: Those dwelling or housing units for which the

      4 persons            $56,430
      5 or more persons         $60,940

for the Washington, D.C. metropolitan statistical area (MSA) established by the
U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (DHUD) and published in
memorandum from time to time by the Washington, D.C. DHUD Field Office, Region
III.
56.30.01.03 Effective Date

***** SEC. 57-4 (formerly § 57-3) DISCHARGE OF GUNS IN THE URBAN AREA —

COMCOR 57.04.01 Weapons - Discharge of Guns Within Montgomery County
57.04.01.01 Purpose 
      Procedure to allow the discharge of a firearm within the urban area under
a deer management permit issued by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources
and approved by the Chief of Police and to establish rules for deer hunting on
private property at least 50 acres in size.
57.04.01.02 Procedures
      (a)   An applicant for a deer management permit inside the urban area
must contact the Montgomery County Police Department’s (MCPD) police district
serving the area in which the requestor’s site is located within 24 hours of
submitting the application to the Department of Natural Resources (DNR). An
MCPD executive officer (lieutenant or above) will contact DNR as soon as
practical but no more than 24 hours after receiving such notification to
arrange to meet at the location where the permit has been requested.
The MCPD executive officer will meet the DNR agent at the location where the
permit has been requested to jointly inspect the location to resolve any issues
or questions. If the MCPD executive officer and DNR agent cannot meet at a
mutually convenient time, the MCPD executive officer must contact the applicant
to arrange to inspect the location within three (3) calendar days of the
issuance of the permit. The DNR agent will have the sole responsibility for
determining the need for the issuance of the deer management permit. The MCPD
executive officer will inspect the site from the standpoint of safety issues,
including, but not limited to, the location’s proximity to occupied buildings
and/or roadways, whether the location provides for downward trajectory, and any
other considerations that may necessitate restricting the use of a firearm to
carry out the stated purpose of the deer management permit.
If the DNR agent determines that a deer management permit is to be issued, the
MCPD executive officer will request a copy of the completed permit from the DNR
agent or the applicant. The MCPD executive officer will then complete an MCP
Form #590, Addendum to DNR Deer Damage Control Permit, listing all restrictions
with which the permit holder must comply. The MCPD executive officer will
forward the deer management permit and addendum along with a memorandum
outlining the reasons for any restrictions to the Chief of Police for review
and signature within three (3) calendar days.
After reviewing the documentation submitted for the deer management permit from
both the DNR and MCPD executive officer, the Chief of Police will either
approve or disapprove the request, sign and date the MCP Form #590. After
signing, the originals of the MCP Form #590 and the deer management permit will
be returned to the person requesting the permit by U.S. mail within four
calendar days. The remaining two copies of the forms will be forwarded to the
Department of Natural Resources for their records. The Department of Police
will maintain its files.
      (b)   Whenever deer hunting is to occur on private property of at least
50 acres in size during hunting season, the property owner(s) must, at least 15
days before any weapon is discharged, post the perimeter of the property and,
where applicable, at each road entrance to the property, with signs that:
         (1)   are placed where the signs may reasonably be seen by passersby
or from any adjacent roadway or public waterway;
         (2)   are posted at least every 100 yards along the perimeter of the
property;
         (3)   are at least 12 inches wide by 17 inches high;
         (4)   have black lettering on a yellow background;
         (5)   that include the following warning: “CAUTION: Firearms in use
for deer hunting on this property from (date) to (date). No Trespassing.”
      (c)   Whenever deer hunting is to occur on private property within the
urban area pursuant to a deer management permit, the property owner must follow
the requirements in subsection (b) except that the owner must post the required
warning signs at least two days before any weapon is discharged.
57.04.01.03 Applicability
      Any person within an urban area whose livelihood is threatened by
property damage caused by deer may apply for a deer management permit, except
that no permit is necessary on land at least 50 acres in size during hunting
season.
57.04.01.04 Severability
      If a court holds that part of this regulation is invalid, the invalidity
does not affect other parts.
(Administrative History: Reg.  No. 34-08AM (Method 2); Orig. Dept.: Police;
Supersedes Reg. No. 16-93, which superseded Reg. No. 86-91)
***** SEC. 57-6 (formerly § 57-4A) DISCHARGE OF BOWS — REGULATIONS *****
COMCOR 57.06.01 Safety Guidelines for Target Archery Practice
57.06.01.01 Purpose
      To establish safety guidelines for practicing target archery and to
establish penalties for violations of this regulation.
57.06.01.02
   Target archery may be practiced in the County under the following
circumstances:
   (a)   Target archery may be practiced on public property in the County in
any area designated for target archery.
   (b)   Target archery may be practiced on private property in the County with
the owner or occupant's written consent as long as:
      (1)   an arrow does not travel across or hit on a public road or strike
any person, animal, or vehicle on a public road; and
      (2)   an arrow does not travel across or land on property owned or
occupied by a person who has not given written consent for the target archery,
or hit any person, animal, building, or vehicle.
57.06.01.03 Penalty
   Any violation of this regulation is a class A violation to which the maximum
penalties for the class A violation apply.
57.06.01.04 Severability
   If a court holds that part of this regulation is invalid, the invalidity
does not affect other parts.
57.06.01.05 Effective Date
   This regulation becomes effective 30 calendar days after approval by the
County Council or 90 calendar days after Council receipt of the Regulation if
Council takes no action within 60 days of receipt.
(Administrative History: Reg. No. 85-92AMII (Method 2); Orig. Dept.: Police;
Supersedes Reg. No. 85-92AM)
***** SEC. 57-8 (formerly § 57-5A) CHILD SAFETY HANDGUN DEVICES AND HANDGUNS —
REGULATIONS *****
COMCOR 57.08.01 Child Safety Handgun Devices
57.08.01.01 Enforcement
   The director of the Department of Housing and Community Affairs or the
director's authorized representative must initially inspect each firearm dealer
to determine compliance with this regulation. Thereafter, random inspections
will be made at the discretion of the director or when a complaint is filed.
57.08.01.02 Child Safety Handgun Device Approval
   A child safety handgun device that meets the requirements of
57.08.01.03 is approved unless the director of the Department of Housing and
Community Affairs finds in a review that the device is not effective in
rendering the handgun inoperable. The director of Housing and Community Affairs
will maintain a publicly available list of unapproved child safety handgun
devices.
57.08.01.03 Child Safety Handgun Device Requirements
      A.   The firearm dealer must maintain a record indicating that a child
safety handgun device was provided to the recipient of a handgun. The director
of the Department of Housing and Community Affairs, the director's authorized
representative, or any officer or other authorized employee of a law
enforcement agency may inspect these records.
      B.   The child safety handgun device must be either:
         1.   a lock that attaches to the handgun to prevent movement of the
trigger of the handgun or otherwise renders the handgun inoperable until
removed by a key or combination; or
         2.   a lockable box designed to hold the handgun being transferred
that requires a key or combination to open and renders the handgun inoperable
when locked.
57.08.01.04 Public Notification
      A.   Signs for Firearm Dealers Having a Retail Store
         1.   A sign must be posted in plain view in the sales area.
         2.   The sign must state the following: “Section 57-5A of the
Montgomery County Code requires that a child safety handgun device be provided
by the firearm dealer at the time of purchase, lease, or transfer of each
handgun. State law prohibits keeping firearms anywhere an unsupervised child
could gain access to the firearm”.
         3.   The sign must have letters at least 3/4 inches in height and a
contrasting color to the sign background.
      B.   Notices for Firearm Dealers Not Having a Retail Store
         1.   A firearm dealer not having a retail store must provide a written
notice with the wording in A.2 above.
         2.   The notice must be given by the firearm dealer to the recipient
of any handgun at the time of purchase, lease; or transfer.
         3.   The notice must be at least font size 12 and on paper of a
contrasting color.
      C.   Source of Signs and Notices
         1.   The sign or notice may be purchased from the Department of
Housing and Community Affairs. The Department of Housing and Community Affairs
may charge a fee for the sign or notice not to exceed the cost of producing the
sign or notice.
         2.   The firearm dealer may provide the sign or notice provided that
they comply with
57.08.01.04, A or B, above.
57.08.01.05 Severability
      If a court holds that a portion of this regulation is invalid, the other
portions remain in effect.
(Administrative History: Reg. No. 43-97AM (Method 2); Orig. Dept.: Health and
Human Services)

COMCOR 59.00 01 Permit Fees and Requirements Related to Construction Debris
Reclamation Facility
59.00.01.01 Purpose and Authority
      The following schedule of fees and requirements are adopted pursuant to
the authority contained in Section 59-C-9.84 of the Montgomery County Code
1994, as amended.
59.00.01.02 Definitions
      Construction Debris Reclamation Facility: Any land or building used for
the collection, sorting and recovery of construction or demolition debris where
debris:
   (a)   Is separated, collected, processed or marketed in the form of raw
materials or products;
   (b)   Has marketable value; and
   (c)   Is sorted at the reclamation facility site, with the inventory, by
volume, being turned over at least once every 3 months.
59.00.01.03 Development Standards
   (a)   Minimum lot size of 10 acres.
   (b)   Minimum frontage of 1,000 feet and direct access to a road classified
as a primary industrial street or higher.
   (c)   No more than 2 miles from an interstate highway interchange.
   (d)   A building setback of 50 feet from any road right-of-way, except a
limited access freeway which is controlled by Section 59-C-9.81, and 75 feet
from any adjoining property not classified in an industrial zone or the RS
zone.
   (e)   Off-street parking of haul trucks and roll off containers must be in a
building or screened from off-site visibility, and
   (f)   A landscaping plan approved by the Planning Board as part of the site
plan approval process.
59.00.01.04 Construction Debris Reclamation Permit Requirements
   This regulation requires that:
   (a)   Construction debris be transported to the construction recycling
facility in covered "Roll off' containers or covered trucks.
   (b)   All sorting and processing be done in an enclosed structure.
   (c)   When construction debris is separated, collected and processed, an
average of 50% of the processed materials by weight have a marketable value
   (d)   Permanent storage is not permitted and inventory by volume turned over
at least once every three months.
   (e)   Fifty-one percent (51%) of the materials processed be collected by the
facility operator and
   (f)   The total volume of construction and demolition debris collected and
recycled be reported to the Division of Solid Waste Services on an annual
basis.
59.00.01.05 Construction Debris Reclamation Permit Fees
      Annual Permit Fee - $110.00
59.00.01.06 Indexing of Fees to Labor Cost Increases
The Director of Permitting Services must adjust each fee set in or under this
regulation on July 1 of each year by regulation by a percentage that does not
exceed the rate of the increase (if any) in the department’s approved personnel
costs for the then-current fiscal year compared to the approved personnel costs
for the preceding fiscal year. For fees of $100 or more, the Director must
calculate the revised fee to the nearest five dollars. For fees under $100, the
Director must calculate the revised fee to the nearest dollar.
59.00.01.07 Severability
The provisions of these regulations are severable. If a court of competent
jurisdiction holds that a provision is invalid or inapplicable, the remainder
of the regulation remains in effect.
(Administrative History: Reg. No. 10-08 (Method 2); Orig. Dept.: Permitting
Services; Supersedes Reg. No. 15-07, which superseded Reg. No. 11-06, which
superseded Reg. No. 10-05, which superseded Reg. No. 38-01)
COMCOR 59.00.02 Requirements for Registered Living Units
** 59.00.02.01 Authority **
      This Executive Regulation is authorized by Montgomery County Code 1984,
as amended, Section 59-A-6.10, "Registered Living Unit - Standards and
Requirements" and applies to all Registered Living Units (RLU).
59.00.02.02 Administration
      A.   Approval. The standards and requirements for RLUs contained in
Chapter 59 are administered by the Director of the Department of Environmental
Protection (DEP), who is the final authority in all matters pertaining to the
approval or disapproval of a RLU.
      B.   Delegation of authority for routine operations. The Director of DEP
has designated the Director of the Department of Housing and Community
Development (DHCD), by an Agreement, dated November 11, 1989, to administer
routine registration and inspection functions of RLU for DEP.
59.00.02.03 Definitions
      The following words or phrases are defined as follows for use in this
regulation:
      Owner-Occupant. A person(s) who holds legal title to a one-family
detached dwelling unit. An owner-occupant of a RLU must occupy the dwelling
unit, except for bona fide temporary absences not exceeding six months in any
twelve month period.
      Party wall. A common partition wall, having at least seven feet of length
horizontally in one direction, directly dividing the main dwelling and its
adjoining RLU. The main dwelling and the RLU must be contiguous along this
common wall with no intervening uninhabitable spaces or areas. The party wall
requirement may be met, if the RLU is in whole or in part, above or below the
main dwelling, provided that there is a common wall meeting the above
conditions, or a common floor/ceiling assembly directly dividing the RLU from
the main dwelling.
      Subordinate to the main dwelling. The total floor area of the RLU must be
less than 50% of the total habitable floor area of the main dwelling.
59.00.02.04 Standards and Requirements for Occupancy
      A RLU must comply with the Requirements of the Housing and Building
Maintenance Code for Accessory Apartments adopted by Executive Regulation No.
59-89.
59.00.02.05 Procedure for Registration and Inspection of RLU
   The owner-occupant must register the RLU with DHCD, as follows:
   a.   An owner-occupant must obtain an Affidavit of Compliance (Affidavit)
form from DHCD.
   b.   The owner-occupant must file a completed Affidavit with DHCD which
affirms that:
         1.   the RLU meets the Occupancy, Property and Ownership requirements
as set forth in the Zoning Ordinance;
         2.   the owner-occupant will disclose to any prospective purchaser(s)
of the property that there is a RLU on the property and an affidavit on file
with DHCD; and
         3.   DHCD will be informed in writing if the property is sold by the
owner-occupant and the owner-occupant will inform DHCD of the names of the new
owner(s).
   c.   After the Affidavit is filed by the owner-occupant, DHCD will determine
whether the Affidavit is complete and meets the requirements of the Code. If
the Affidavit meets such requirements, then DHCD will approve it by stamping it
and initialing it. Any application for a building permit for a RLU submitted to
DEP must be accompanied by an approved Affidavit.
   d.   DHCD will inspect the existing RLU for which an Affidavit has been
approved for compliance with applicable codes, as follows:
         1.   The RLU must be maintained in compliance with all applicable
codes, including the Housing and Building Maintenance Standards of Chapter 26
of the Montgomery County Code, 1984, as amended.
         2.   If any code violations are found they will be listed by DHCD and
the owner will be given a reasonable opportunity to make corrections.
         3.   If necessary, the owner must obtain building, electrical or
plumbing permits in order to correct the code violations.
         4.   When work has been completed under permits, the owner must obtain
a final inspection and approval by the appropriate County agency.
   e.   If a RLU is to be created for which an Affidavit has been approved:
         1.   The owner must obtain the necessary building, electrical and
plumbing permits which may be required for its creation.
         2.   When work has been completed under permits, the owner must obtain
a final inspection and approval by the appropriate agency.
   f.   When a final inspection by DHCD has verified that the owner has
corrected all code violations and/or completed all construction, and meets all
Code requirements, DHCD will issue a Certificate of Registration to the owner.
   g.   The owner must inform DHCD in writing when the occupancy of the RLU
changes. The owner must file a new Affidavit with DHCD, indicating who the new
occupant will be, if any, and defining the relationship of the occupant to the
owner. DHCD reserves the right to inspect the RLU at any change of occupancy.
If the Affidavit meets the requirements of the Code, then UHCU may approve it.
59.00.02.06 Standards for Inspection of the RLU
      The RLU must be maintained in compliance with all applicable codes,
including the Housing and Building Maintenance Standards of Chapter 26 of the
Montgomery County Code, 1984, as amended. DHCD may conduct inspections, as
follows:
   a.   Each RLU will be annually inspected and at such other times as may be
appropriate.
   b.   The owner must permit DHCD inspector(s) to enter and inspect the RLU
and the main dwelling unit, at reasonable times during normal business hours.
An appointment may be arranged if necessary, however the inspector's request at
the time of a visit shall be considered to be adequate notice of an inspection.
   c.   The DHCD inspector(s) must be permitted to interview all occupants of
the dwelling units who are present during such inspections.
   d.   DHCD will notify DEP when a violation of Chapter 59 occurs.
59.00.02.07 Standards for Removal of the RLU
   a.   Whenever the RLU is no longer occupied as an RLU, when a special
exception has been granted in accordance with the Code, or whenever the one-
family detached dwelling in which the RLU is located is no longer occupied by
the owner, tnen the owner must remove the cooking facility of the RLU.
   b.   Removal of the cooking facility means removal of all equipment that
could be used for cooking, heating, or preparing food. Removal of all cooking
equipment and facilities includes, but is not limited to any stove, oven,
microwave oven, toaster oven, hot plate, other appliance for heating food. Food
preparation surfaces, storage facilities (for food and/or utensils) and clean-
up facilities such as countertops, refrigerator and sink may remain.
   c.   The space approved for the RLU must be internally connected to the main
dwelling, as appropriate, by the owner, so that a person is not required to go
outside the main dwelling to enter the space of the discontinued RLU.
   d.   The owner must notify DHCD in writing within 15 days of when the RLU is
no longer used as a RLU and must complete removal of the cooking element within
90 days of the discontinuance of the RLU use.
   e.   UHCD may inspect the main dwelling and the discontinued RLU to assure
compliance with the requirements of the Code.
59.00.02.08 Effective Date
      This Executive Regulation will take effect 30 days after the date of
adoption by the County Council.
   (Administrative History: Reg. No. 1-90 (Method 2); Orig. Dept.:
Environmental Protection)
COMCOR 59.00.03 Non-Profit Organization Sign Permit and Sign Variance Fees
59.00.03.01 Purpose
   This regulation establishes a process for waiving or reducing sign permit
and sign variance fees for non-profit organizations.
59.00.03.02 Applicability
   This regulation applies to any non-profit organization that seeks to obtain
a sign permit or sign variance for a sign in Montgomery County.
59.00.03.03 Definitions
   Applicants on the Planning Board’s list of civic and homeowners associations
must only submit proof of their non-profit status. All other applicants must
provide 501(C)(3) certificate and proof of annual income for the tax year
immediately preceding the date of application.
59.00.03.04 Policy
   Applicants on the Planning Board’s list of civic and homeowners associations
must only submit proof of their non-profit status. All other applicants must
provide 501(C)(3) certificate and proof of annual income for the tax year
immediately preceding the date of application.
59.00.03.05 Procedures
   A non-profit organization applying for a sign permit or sign variance must
follow all the permitting requirements found in Chapter 59-F of the Montgomery
County Code. In addition, non-profit organizations will be required to provide
the following with the application:
      1.   proof of non-profit status, and
      2.   proof of annual revenue (not required for non-profit organizations
on the Planning Board’s list of civic and homeowners associations), and
      3.   line drawing showing that the size of the proposed sign is smaller
than the maximum size permitted in the zone in which the sign will be located.
   Fees will be waived for non-profit organizations on the Planning Board’s
list of civic and homeowners associations. All other fees will be assessed in
accordance with the fee scale noted below after all of the items above are
submitted.
59.00.03.06 Fees
   Fees will be on a sliding scale based upon the annual revenue of the
applicant. The fee scale is as follows:
      ANNUAL REVENUE               FEE
      $0.00 - $50,000.00                  $0.00
      $50,000.01 - 100,000.00               33% of Current Fees
      $100,000.01 - $200,000.00               66% of Current Fees
      $200,000.01 and above               100% of Current Fees
59.00.03.07 Severability
   The provisions of these regulations are severable. If a court of competent
jurisdiction holds that a provision is invalid or inapplicable, the remainder
of the regulation remains in effect.
(Administrative History: Reg. No. 13-08 (Method 2); Orig. Dept.: Permitting
Services; Supersedes Reg. No. 19-06AM)
COMCOR 59.00.04 Additional Stories on Sloping Lot
59.00.04.01 Purpose
This regulation establishes the process for determining if a lot slopes
sufficiently to allow additional stories on the downhill side of a building
erected on a sloping lot.
59.00.04.02 Applicability
This regulation applies to any lot that is determined to slope sufficiently to
allow additional stories in excess of the number of stories allowed in the zone
as defined in 59-A-5.41 of the Zoning Ordinance.
59.00.04.03 Policy
It is the policy of the Department of Permitting Services to determine a lot to
be sloping when any of the following circumstances occur on the lot:
      (1)   There is a change in vertical elevation of at least one (1) foot
for each twelve (12) feet of horizontal distance when measured from pre-
development grade between any of the following points:
         (a)   from front lot line to rear of building or addition;
         (b)   from rear lot line to front of building or addition;
         (c)   from front building restriction line to rear building
restriction line;
         (d)   from rear building restriction line to front building
restriction line;
         (e)   from front of building or addition to rear of building or
addition;
         (f)   from rear of building or addition to front of building or
addition;
         (g)   between side building restriction lines; or
         (h)   from one side of building or addition to other side of building
or addition, and
      (2)   Between the points selected, there is a change in elevation of at
least six feet.
(Administrative History: Reg. No. 18-09AM (Method 2); Orig. Dept.: Permitting
Services)
COMCOR 59.00.05 Administrative Procedures for Development Review
[https://export.amlegal.com/media/340a0401e0434d101bf71e4da3162922bb44f633/
IMAGES/0-0-0-6911.png]
[https://export.amlegal.com/media/340a0401e0434d101bf71e4da3162922bb44f633/
IMAGES/0-0-0-6913.png]
59.00.05.01 Purpose and Applicability
      A.   Purpose. These regulations define administrative procedures for the
submission and review of all plans submitted to the Montgomery County Planning
Department, under the Subdivision Regulations and the Zoning Ordinance of the
Montgomery County Code. These procedures are designed to provide accurate and
complete information and to ensure a thorough and timely review process as a
basis for decisions. These regulations were adopted by the Planning Board and
approved as regulations by the County Council under Chapter 50, Section 10.1
and as contemplated by Chapter 59, Section 7.3.4.F.3. These regulations
supersede the Montgomery County Planning Department’s Manual of Development
Review Procedures (December 2007).
         1.   These regulations:
            (a)   define a process that is comprehensive, clear, transparent,
and understandable to citizens, developers, applicants, review agencies, staff,
and other interested parties;
            (b)   clarify standards and procedures for submission of timely and
relevant information by applicants;
            (c)   provide procedures for timely participation by government
agencies in the review of applications; and
            (d)   provide procedures for participation by interested parties,
such as owners of properties adjoining the project site, so that their issues
and concerns can be submitted to staff and the Board for consideration during
the review process before the Board decides and acts on the proposed land
development project.
         2.   These regulations are intended to identify the steps that an
applicant must take to apply for the review and approval of specific types of
development approvals that are acted upon by either the Board or Director, and
to provide a comprehensive explanation of what is involved in processing a
development application, including the steps to ensure a thorough and timely
review.
      B.   Applicability. The development review process covered in these
regulations apply to all development applications submitted to the Montgomery
County Planning Department and acted upon by the Board or Director under
Chapter 50 and Chapter 59 of the County Code.
      C.   Definitions. All terms used in these regulations that are defined in
Chapter 50 or Chapter 59 have the same meanings as the definitions in those
Chapters.
      D.   Rules of interpretation. The rules of interpretation contained in
Chapter 50 and Chapter 59 apply to these regulations. Footnotes used in these
regulations are a part of the requirements.
59.00.05.02 Basic Planning Department Policies for the Development Review
Process
      A.   In processing and reviewing the application, the Planning Department
staff must:
         1.   Appoint a lead reviewer to coordinate the review of the
application and the receipt of inquiries related to the application or the
regulatory process.
         2.   Review the application carefully, fairly, and in a timely manner.
         3.   Apply the applicable laws, regulations, and guidelines
consistently.
         4.   Work with all parties to present a recommendation to the Board
that complies with the applicable standards of review.
         5.   Attempt to identify issues early in the process and strive to
resolve them as early as possible.
         6.   Cooperate with other agency and utility company staffs, the
applicant, and the public to seek a mutually satisfactory resolution when
issues arise.
         7.   Collaborate with other review agencies and other parties,
actively seeking solutions that achieve the County’s planning and community-
building goals.
         8.   Carry out County and Planning Board policies, with special
attention to:
            (a)   adopted Master Plans;
            (b)   applicable land use, transportation, and environmental laws,
regulations, and guidelines;
            (c)   the Subdivision Staging Policy;
            (d)   standards of professional responsibility; and
            (e)   promotion of design excellence.
      B.   Planning Department staff and other government agency and utility
company staff who participate in the review of development applications must:
         1.   Review each application carefully, fairly, and in a timely
manner.
         2.   Participate in scheduled Development Review Committee (DRC) and
pre-DRC meetings, either in person or by transmitting written comments to the
DRC chair.
         3.   Make reasonable efforts to participate, when necessary, in
supplemental meetings on specific cases, as requested by either the lead
reviewer or the applicant.
         4.   Work collaboratively to identify and seek mutually satisfactory
resolutions, using the lead-agency protocol for conflicting recommendations
created though a Memorandum of Understanding between the Planning Department
and several of the agency members of the DRC to involve appropriate managers or
chiefs from the conflicting agencies.
         5.   Report recommendations to the Board that are contrary to Planning
staff’s in the rare event that agencies with conflicting comments are unable to
timely reach a mutually satisfactory recommendation on issues related to a
development application after following the protocol referenced above.
      C.   Applicants must:
         1.   Select a development team, consultants, and representatives
appropriate for the project.
         2.   Follow Planning Board and County policies, procedures, and
regulations related to the proposed development project.
         3.   Submit complete and accurate applications.
         4.   Refer questions, issues, and all revisions concerning the filed
application to the lead reviewer.
         5.   Notify the lead reviewer promptly if there is a major change to
the development project under review.
         6.   Work with review staffs and the public in a cooperative manner to
seek a mutually satisfactory resolution when issues arise.
59.00.05.03 Overview of the Application Types
These regulations specify the submission, notice, review and approval
procedures that must be followed for all development applications and
associated requests that are submitted to the Montgomery County Planning
Department and acted upon by the Board or Director. The types of application
that may be required before an applicant can apply for permits to disturb land
and construct are dependent on many factors, such as, the zoning on the subject
site, the legal status (i.e., recorded lot, unplatted parcel, etc.) of the
site, and the type of land use proposed for the project. This section includes
an overview of the various application types.
      A.   Land Development Plan Applications. The land development plan
applications covered by this manual include: pre-preliminary submissions,
sketch or project plans, preliminary and administrative subdivision plans, site
plans, and record plats. Figure 1, below summarizes these plans, including
references to the specific sections of the County Code that contain their
requirements, and how they fit into the overall regulatory review process.
[https://export.amlegal.com/media/340a0401e0434d101bf71e4da3162922bb44f633/
IMAGES/0-0-0-6921.png]
   Figure 1. Land Development Plan Application Types
      B.   Plan Amendments. Proposed changes to a plan that has been approved
and certified by the Board or Director must be approved as a plan amendment. A
plan amendment may be filed to request changes to features of an approved plan
drawing, or to specific conditions of the Board’s or Director’s approval for
the plan.1
         1.   Classification of Preliminary and Site Plan Amendments. An
amendment to a preliminary plan or site plan may be classified as major or
minor depending on the purpose of the proposed amendment and as specified by
the Subdivision Regulations (Section 50.4.2.F) or the Zoning Ordinance (Section
59.7.3.4.J).
            (a)   Major amendments must be reviewed and acted on by the Board.
            (b)   Minor amendments to a preliminary plan must be acted on by
the Board; however, if the amendment is to change the validity period of the
approved plan’s phasing schedule, the Director may act on the proposed
amendment.
            (c)   Minor site plan amendments may be acted upon by the Director
under certain circumstances.
            (d)   A new preliminary plan or administrative subdivision plan is
required to resubdivide previously approved and recorded lots, or change a
previous plan application that was denied.
         2.   Amendment to a Preliminary or Site Plan to change an associated
Forest Conservation Plan. Preliminary or site plan amendments that involve
amendments to associated forest conservation plans may be filed as minor
amendments.
            (a)   Per the Forest Conservation regulations (COMCOR 22A.00.01,
Section 22A.00.01.13.A(1)), a forest conservation plan amendment that proposes
no more than 5000 square feet of additional forest clearing may be acted on by
the Director.
            (b)   A proposed forest conservation plan amendment that involves
changes to recorded conservation easements approved by the Board must be acted
on by the Board. Corresponding amendments to the associated preliminary or site
plan to reflect any easement changes must also be filed.
         3.   Changes to Site Plan-approved structures. A structure located on
property covered by an approved site plan may be replaced without applying for
a site plan amendment if the replacement conforms to the specifications
approved as part of the site plan; for instance, replacing an existing fence or
retaining wall, in kind. Changes that do not conform to approved specifications
must be filed as a minor site plan amendment, except for those changes allowed
under 59-7.3.4.G.2.
            (a)   Playground areas and equipment. Many approved site plans that
have residential uses include details for playground areas and equipment. For
the purposes of site plan review, the term “playground equipment” includes
benches, picnic tables, and trash receptacles, in addition to structures that
are used for outdoor recreation activities by children, such as swing sets and
slides. Over time, playground equipment may become old and outdated and need to
be replaced; or a resident association may want to change its location or
configuration, or remove it entirely.
               i.   Installation of a new playground or removal of an existing
one requires review and action under the Minor Site Plan Amendment process.
               ii.   Replacing playground equipment requires review and
approval by Planning Department staff. Such a change is not classified as a
site plan amendment. The following rules apply to the substitution of
playground equipment, for a site that has an approved site plan and specific
playground equipment requirements:
                  a.   A request for a playground equipment substitution must
be made by submitting a complete Recreational Equipment Substitution Request
Form.
                  b.   The form may be filled out by the provider of the
proposed playground equipment, but the project developer must also submit a
cover letter confirming that the current Site Plan applicant supports the
proposed substitution.
                  c.   Staff must review the substitution request to determine
if the proposed equipment is equal in capacity, features, age group served, and
quality2 (including conformance with CPSC and ASTM3 safety standards.)
                  d.   If staff does not render a decision as to whether the
proposed substitution meets the “or approved equal” standard within 45 calendar
days after the applicant’s complete submission of a Recreational Equipment
Substitution Request Form, the substitution is automatically approved.
                  e.   After deciding, staff must reply, in writing, to the
current Site Plan applicant. If the request is denied, the staff must specify,
in writing, each reason for the denial. Staff must place a copy of the reply
letter in the Site Plan file. The Site Plan applicant may appeal a denial to
the Board.
      C.   Other Application Types. An application must also be submitted to
the Planning Department for the following:
         1.   Request to Extend a Validity Period for an Approved Plan. A
request for approval of an extension to the validity period of an approved plan
or the validity period of an Adequate Public Facilities determination.
         2.   Subdivision Waiver Request. A request for a waiver from the
requirement to submit a preliminary plan or administrative subdivision plan
under Division 50.9 of Chapter 50.
         3.   Adequate Public Facilities Ordinance (APFO) Review at Building
Permit. A request for Planning Board APF review and finding required under
Chapter 8 before issuance of a building permit for development on an existing
recorded lot that is not subject to a previous preliminary plan approval, and
does not require a site plan under Chapter 59, Section 7.3.4.
         4.   Request to Extend a Hearing Date. A request for extension of a
Board hearing date pursuant to Chapter 59, Sections 7.3.3.C or 7.3.4.C, and
Chapter 50, Section 4.1.E.
         5.   Exemption to Platting. A request for exemption under Chapter 50,
Section 3.3 from the requirement to record a plat prior to the division or
conveyance of land, or to support issuance of a building permit under Chapter
8.
----------
1 A plan amendment is different than a plan revision. A plan revision is a
change to a submitted application that an applicant chooses to make prior to
action. Significant revisions may, on a case-by-case basis, require re-notice
of the application.
2 The equipment proposed must also be able to fit in the space shown on the
Site Plan. If the proposed substitution becomes so big that it no longer fits
in the “play area” shown on the Site Plan, a Site Plan Amendment will be
required.
3 If there is a conflict between Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) and
American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM) standards, ASTM standards
will govern.
59.00.05.04 Notice
Certain types of notice must be provided by both the applicant and Planning
Department staff at specific steps during the regulatory review process. The
individuals receiving these notices vary depending upon the notice type, but
include: owners of adjoining and confronting properties; nearby civic and
homeowners’ associations; “interested parties” who request notice during the
process; and the general public.
Individuals, groups, and interested parties receive notice in writing, either
by mail, or by email if they have indicated email as their preference. The
general public receive notice from signs that are required to be posted on a
project site, and for applications that are acted upon by the Board, from the
weekly Planning Board agenda on the Board’s website.

following table, or as otherwise specified in the Code:
